Name: Meadow Management at Adelaide Local Nature Reserve
Stump Up For Trees

Name: Heal Somerset

Name: Cambridge City Chalk Streams Project
Description: Restoring Cambridge's chalk streams into thriving, resilient ecosystems and reviving wildlife habitats.

Name: Dundreggan Estate

Name: Boothby Wildland

Name: Eastern Moors Partnership

Name: South Arran MPA

Name: The Grange Project

Name: Harold's Park Wildland

Name: Hepple Wilds

Name: Geltsdale
Description: RSPB Geltsdale in the North Pennines uplands combines blanket bog, hay meadows and heathland management to support hen harriers, black grouse and curlews.

Name: Hesketh Out Marsh
Description: RSPB Hesketh Out Marsh on the Ribble Estuary is one of the UK’s largest recent realignment projects, restoring saltmarsh for thousands of wintering waders and wildfowl.

Name: High Fen Wildland

Name: Knepp Estate
Description: The pioneering 3,500‑acre rewilding project in West Sussex where free‑roaming livestock drive natural processes, supporting nightingales, turtle doves, purple emperor butterflies and thriving biodiverse wetlands.

Name: Mapperton Wildlands

Name: Steart Marshes

Name: Moor Barton

Description: Discover a charming garden at Avebury Manor, providing a vital green space and habitat in the heart of the village.

Name: Aversley Wood
Description: Aversley Wood is an ancient woodland in Cambridgeshire, managed by the Woodland Trust. It features oak, ash, and hazel coppice, supporting diverse ground flora. Public footpaths provide access. Parking is available.

Name: Avery's Pightle
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Avery's Pightle is a 1.3-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south of Enborne in Berkshire.

Name: Avon Valley Woods
Description: Avon Valley Woods, managed by The Woodland Trust, is a beautiful stretch of ancient woodland in South Devon, covering around 139 hectares near Woodleigh. It features a diverse mix of steep, valley-sided ancient woodland and areas of new woodland, brimming with wildlife and a wide variety of tree species. Visitors can explore a network of paths and observe local wildlife, with the River Avon running through the site.

Name: Axmouth to Lyme Regis Undercliffs NNR
Description: A unique coastal landslip wilderness in Dorset and East Devon, part of the Jurassic Coast World Heritage Site. Rich in diverse flora and fauna, the reserve features a dynamic landscape of ancient woodlands, scrub, and grasslands formed by historic geological movements.

Name: Aykley Wood
Description: Aykley Wood is an ancient semi-natural woodland and local nature reserve in Durham. It features a significant number of mature oak trees, providing an important green space and habitat for wildlife within the city.

Name: Baal Hill Wood
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 16 hectares.

Name: Babcary Meadows
Description: Babcary Meadows is a 13.6 hectares biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north of Babcary in Somerset, notified in 1988.

Name: Bacombe Hill
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Bacombe and Coombe Hills is a 76.4-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Upper Bacombe in Buckinghamshire.

Name: Bacton Wood
Description: This expansive woodland offers a haven of ancient trees and vibrant undergrowth, teeming with diverse wildlife. Visitors can explore winding trails perfect for invigorating walks or cycling adventures, immersing themselves in the sights and sounds of nature. Discover tranquil glades and the rustling secrets of this beautiful natural space.

Name: Baddesley Clinton
Description: Its tranquil moated grounds, park, and gardens offer diverse habitats.

Name: Badgeworth SSSI, Gloucestershire
Description: Badgeworth SSSI is a 3. 08-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Gloucestershire notified in 1954 and renotified in 1983.

Name: Baggy Point
Description: Experience a dramatic North Devon headland, a Site of Special Scientific Interest renowned for its unique geology, maritime heathland, and abundant coastal wildlife including seals and rare birds.

Name: Baker's Pit Nature Reserve
Description: Baker's Pit Nature Reserve is a nature reserve and former china clay quarry in the parish of Ludgvan, west Cornwall managed by the Cornwall Wildlife Trust.  The reserve is on the moorland of Noon Diggery and is south of the Castle-an-Dinas hillfort and Roger's Tower, a folly built within the hillfort.

Name: Ballard Down
Description: Sweeping chalk downland on the Jurassic Coast, Ballard Down forms a dramatic headland with calcareous grasslands and stunning coastal views.

Name: Balloo Wetland Nature Reserve
Description: Balloo Wetland, near Bangor, is a nature reserve featuring a mosaic of habitats, including ponds, reedbeds, wet grassland, and woodland. It supports a variety of wildlife, such as otters, kingfishers, and various invertebrates. A boardwalk offers visitor access.

Name: Balls Wood
Description: Balls Wood is a 58.5-hectare nature reserve managed by the Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust in Hertford Heath in East Hertfordshire.

Name: Ballyaghagan Nature Reserve
Description: Ballyaghagan Nature Reserve protects ancient woodland and wildflower meadows near Belfast. It preserves one of the area's few remaining ancient woodland fragments, featuring notable wildflowers in spring and early summer. It is home to diverse bird and invertebrate species.

Name: Ballynahone Bog
Description: Ballynahone Bog is a significant lowland raised bog in Northern Ireland. It supports rare plants like bog-rosemary and great sundew, along with diverse insect life. The site forms part of the Moyola River catchment area, providing crucial habitat for various wildlife species.

Name: Balmacara Estate
Description: This expansive crofting estate offers scenic coastal landscapes along the shores of Loch Alsh and Balmacara Bay.

Name: Bamff Wildland
Description: Bamff Wildland is a rewilding project in Perthshire, Scotland. It focuses on the reintroduction and monitoring of European beavers, observing their transformative impact on the landscape. The estate actively supports biodiversity and habitat restoration.

Name: Banovallum House
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 1 hectares.

Name: Barkway Chalk Pit
Description: Barkway Chalk Pit is a small former chalk quarry and nature reserve in North Hertfordshire, managed by North Hertfordshire District Council. It is a Regionally Important Geological Site (RIGS) due to its chalk exposure, displaced by the Anglian ice sheet. The site features chalk grassland and scrub, supporting wildflowers like bee orchid and common spotted orchid, and butterflies such as the grizzled skipper and brown argus.

Name: Barkway Chalk Pit
Description: Barkway Chalk Pit is a small nature reserve in Barkway in North Hertfordshire.  It was managed by the Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust.

Name: Barle Valley
Description: Barle Valley is a 1,540 acres Site of Special Scientific Interest within Exmoor National Park, situated in the counties of Devon and Somerset through which the River Barle flows.  It was notified in its current form under the Wildlife and Countryside Act in 1988.

Name: Barlow Burn
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 20 hectares.

Name: Barn Elms Wetland Centre SSSI
Description: Barn Elms Wetland Centre SSSI, located in London, is a nationally important site for wildlife. It encompasses a variety of wetland habitats and supports diverse bird species and other wildlife in an urban environment. It is managed to conserve its ecological value.

Name: Barnsley Warren
Description: Barnsley Warren is a 61.3-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Gloucestershire, notified in 1954 and renotified in 1984.

Name: Barnwell Meadows
Description: Barnwell Meadows is a traditional hay meadow in the heart of Cambridge, managed by Cambridge Past, Present & Future. It supports diverse wildflowers, grasses, and insects, offering a glimpse into the area's agricultural past. Visitors enjoy peaceful walks and observe wildlife.

Name: Baron's Haugh
Description: Baron's Haugh is an RSPB reserve in Motherwell, North Lanarkshire, Scotland. It features a diverse wetland habitat alongside the River Clyde, attracting numerous waterfowl, waders, and other bird species throughout the year. Visitors can enjoy several trails and hides.

Name: Barossa
Description: Barossa is a 498-hectare nature reserve north of Camberley in Surrey.  It is owned by the Ministry of Defence and managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Barra Head
Description: Barra Head's dramatic cliffs host profuse seabird colonies, making this uninhabited Outer Hebridean island a vital Special Protection Area for marine birdlife.

Name: Barrington Court
Description: Barrington Court features extensive Arts and Crafts gardens, including walled kitchen gardens, fruit orchards, and ornamental displays, supporting diverse plant and insect life.

Name: Barrow Blow Wells
Description: Barrow Blow Wells is a local nature reserve with an area of over 2.7 ha located in Barrow-upon-Humber, North Lincolnshire, England.

Name: Barrow Haven Reedbed
Description: Barrow Haven Reedbeds is a local nature reserve with an area of over 12.7 ha located in Barrow-upon-Humber, North Lincolnshire, England.

Name: Barry Water Mill
Description: This mill is set in a secluded natural area, powered by the Barry Burn, a tranquil watercourse vital to the local landscape.

Name: Barton Broad
Description: Barton Broad is a large lake that forms part of the River Ant which gives its name to a 164-hectare nature reserve north-east of Norwich in Norfolk.  The reserve is owned and managed by the Norfolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Barton Meadows
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 32 hectares.

Name: Basing Wood
Description: This expansive woodland in the South East offers a haven of ancient trees and diverse habitats, perfect for exploring on foot or by bike. Keep an eye out for elusive woodland birds and discover the quiet beauty of its natural landscapes, a true escape into nature.

Name: Bassenthwaite Lake NNR
Description: Bassenthwaite Lake NNR is a shallow lake in the Lake District National Park, Cumbria. It hosts diverse habitats like reedbeds, woodlands, and open water, supporting a variety of wildlife including rare fish and otters.

Name: Basted Mill
Description: Basted Mill Public Open Space is located near Borough Green, Kent. It features diverse habitats including an old mill pond, meadows, and woodland, providing a haven for wildlife. Public access paths are available.

Name: Baston Fen
Description: Baston Fen is nature reserve of the Lincolnshire Wildlife Trust, near the village of Baston and about 5 miles north of Market Deeping, in Lincolnshire, England.  It is uncultivated fenland, which is a habitat for particular plants and wildlife.

Name: Battle Great Wood
Description: This ancient woodland in the South East is a haven for diverse wildlife, with mature oak and beech trees forming a rich canopy that shelters a vibrant understory. Visitors can wander along winding paths, enjoying the dappled sunlight and the sounds of birdsong, or explore by bicycle, immersing themselves in the natural beauty and tranquil atmosphere. It's a perfect place to connect with nature, spot woodland creatures, and experience the timeless appeal of a well-loved forest.

Name: Battle of Culloden
Description: Vast open moorland and heathland reflect the natural beauty of the Scottish Highlands at Culloden.

Name: Bawdeswell Heath
Description: Bawdeswell Heath, near Dereham, Norfolk, is a medieval heathland fragment. It features wet and dry heath, acid grassland, and woodland. Diverse flora and fauna thrive, including common lizards and adders. Site management maintains its character.

Name: Bay Pond
Description: Bay Pond is a 7-hectare nature reserve in Godstone in Surrey.  It is managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Beacon Hill
Description: Beacon Hill is a peaceful woodland and recovering heathland site in Monmouthshire, Wales, located within the Wye Valley National Landscape. Managed by Natural Resources Wales, it offers stunning views and public footpaths, protecting diverse habitats and supporting varied wildlife, including Nightjars. Gwent Wildlife Trust is actively involved in conservation efforts and events at the site.

Name: Beacon Hill Country Park
Description: Beacon Hill Country Park in Leicestershire features ancient 600-million-year-old rocks and panoramic views across Charnwood Forest. The park contains mature woodlands, heathland, wildflower meadows, walking trails, and reconstructed Bronze Age log houses.

Name: Beam Parklands
Description: Beam Parklands is a multi-award-winning 53-hectare wetland park in the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham, managed by The Land Trust. Created as part of the Thames Gateway regeneration, it serves as a crucial flood defense and provides diverse habitats including open water, reedbeds, wet woodland, and grasslands for wildlife. The River Beam flows through the site, offering a valuable green space for local communities.

Name: Beatrix Potter Gallery
Description: This gallery showcases art inspired by the rich landscapes and beloved wildlife of the surrounding Lake District.

Name: Beaulieu Road Pony Sale Yard
Description: Explore a haven of ancient woodland in the heart of the New Forest, where sunlight dapples through the canopy onto winding trails perfect for walking and cycling. Keep an eye out for native wildlife, from graceful deer to a vibrant array of birdlife, as you immerse yourself in the tranquil beauty of this protected natural landscape. This serene environment offers a refreshing escape for nature lovers seeking adventure and peace.

Name: Beckenham Place Park
Description: Beckenham Place Park in South London hosts the River Ravensbourne, a site of significant river restoration work. Thames21, in partnership with local groups, improves habitats and naturalises the river course, with ongoing volunteer tasks contributing to its ecological recovery.

Name: Beddington Farmlands
Description: Beddington Farmlands, a nature reserve in south London, is built on a former landfill site. Managed for biodiversity since the 1980s, it provides a crucial habitat for various wildlife, particularly birds. It serves as a significant area for ecological restoration.

Name: Bedfords Park
Description: Bedfords Park is a nature reserve located in Havering, offering panoramic views across London. It features woodlands, ponds, and meadows, supporting a variety of wildlife including red deer. The site has a visitor centre and promotes environmental education.

Name: Bedfords Park
Description: Bedfords Park is public open space of 215 acres or approximately 87½ hectares near Havering-atte-Bower in the London Borough of Havering in England.  It is one of three large parklands around Havering-atte-Bower; the others are Havering Country Park and Pyrgo Park.

Name: Bedgebury National Pinetum and Forest
Description: This expansive woodland offers a breathtaking natural environment, showcasing a remarkable collection of trees from around the globe alongside thriving native flora. Visitors can immerse themselves in this diverse ecosystem, encountering a rich tapestry of wildlife as they explore miles of walking and cycling trails. It's a place to truly connect with nature, from the rustling leaves overhead to the hidden creatures of the forest floor.

Name: Beechenhurst
Description: This expansive woodland offers a vibrant tapestry of ancient oaks and diverse habitats, teeming with wildlife that ranges from chattering woodland birds to elusive deer. Visitors can immerse themselves in nature by exploring a network of trails perfect for walking and cycling, discovering hidden glades and enjoying the tranquility of this natural haven. It's a place to connect with the beauty of the English countryside and witness the cycles of the natural world unfold.

Name: Beinn Eighe and Loch Maree Islands National Nature Reserve
Description: Beinn Eighe and Loch Maree Islands National Nature Reserve, established in 1951, is the UK's first National Nature Reserve. Located in Wester Ross, Scotland, it encompasses a vast area from loch-side to mountain top, including the Beinn Eighe ridge and over 60 islands in Loch Maree. It is famed for its ancient Caledonian pine forests, diverse upland habitats, and a wealth of Scottish wildlife such as golden eagles, pine martens, and black-throated divers.

Name: Beinn Eighe NNR
Description: Beinn Eighe and Loch Maree Islands National Nature Reserve, established 1951 in Wester Ross, Scottish Highlands, is the UK's first National Nature Reserve. This approximately 4,800-hectare site features ancient Caledonian pinewood, mountain habitats and diverse wildlife.

Name: Belfairs Woodland Centre
Description: Great Wood and Dodd's Grove is a 36.8-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Leigh-on-Sea in Essex.

Name: Belhus Chase
Description: Belhus Chase is a 55.44-hectare (136.99 acres) site near Aveley in Essex, within the Thames Chase Community Forest. This new woodland, acquired by the Woodland Trust in 1998, features a mix of mature native broadleaves and younger plantings, creating a parkland atmosphere. It offers walking routes through diverse habitats, providing a green space for wildlife and visitors, and is connected to the historic Belhus Estate.

Name: Bellever Forest
Description: This enchanting woodland offers a haven for diverse wildlife, from soaring buzzards to shy deer, amidst ancient oaks and towering pines. Miles of trails invite exploration, whether you prefer a leisurely stroll amidst the trees or a more invigorating cycle through its scenic landscapes. Immerse yourself in the tranquility of nature, breathing in the fresh forest air and discovering hidden glades teeming with life.

Name: Belsize Wood
HostOrg: Camden Council (managed with The Conservation Volunteers - Camden Green Gym)
Description: Belsize Wood is a 0.7 hectare Local Nature Reserve in Belsize Park, London Borough of Camden. It is managed by Camden Council, with active involvement from Camden Green Gym volunteers who undertake woodland management, coppicing, path clearance, and litter picking. The site offers a peaceful retreat and habitat for wildlife in London.

Name: Belton House
Description: Belton House is surrounded by formal gardens and a larger wooded park, featuring avenues and follies.

Name: Belvide Reservoir
Description: Belvide Reservoir is a Site of Special Scientific Interest in South Staffordshire. Managed as a private bird reserve, it focuses on wildlife conservation and bird observation. The site hosts a bird ringing station, recording over 200 species annually. Access requires a permit.

Name: Bembridge Fort
Description: Perched on the highest point of Bembridge Down, this site offers expansive views over the Isle of Wight's coastline and open landscapes.

Name: Bemersyde Moss
Description: Bemersyde Moss is a Scottish Wildlife Trust nature reserve and a Site of Special Scientific Interest at Bemersyde in the Scottish Borders area of Scotland.  Located near the River Tweed, this reserve features a mix of marshlands, willow scrub, and open water, creating a vital habitat for diverse wildlife.

Name: Ben Lawers
Description: Ben Lawers is a towering Munro in the Scottish Highlands, featuring a dramatic ridge of peaks and unique metamorphic rock formations.

Name: Ben Lomond
Description: Ben Lomond is a popular Scottish Munro offering spectacular Highland views from the eastern shore of Loch Lomond within a National Park.

Name: Beningbrough Hall
Description: Overlooking the River Ouse, Beningbrough Hall is set within extensive grounds featuring redesigned gardens and surrounded by open pastoral landscapes.

Name: Benmore Botanic Garden
Description: Benmore, within Argyll Forest Park, features an impressive avenue of towering Californian giant redwoods. This botanical garden near Dunoon showcases a wide variety of trees and shrubs, including a unique Chilean rainforest glade, offering diverse plant collections.

Name: Benshaw Moor
Description: Benshaw Moor is nature reserve of the Northumberland Wildlife Trust, near Elsdon, in Redesdale, Northumberland, England.  It is a large site with varied habitats.

Name: Benthall Hall
Description: Explore extensive woodlands surrounding Benthall Hall, with a long-distance footpath leading to the River Severn.

Name: Bentley Community Woodland
Description: Bentley Community Woodland is a former colliery site in Doncaster, transformed into a green space with native trees, shrubs, ponds, and wildflower meadows. It enhances local biodiversity and is managed with community volunteer involvement.

Name: Bernwood Forest
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Bernwood Forest is a forest in England.  Historically it was one of several forests of the ancient Kingdom of England and was a Royal hunting forest.

Name: Bernwood Forest
Description: This sprawling woodland in the South East offers a haven for diverse wildlife, from ancient oaks sheltering rare insects to open glades buzzing with pollinators. Meander along winding paths, breathe in the scent of damp earth and pine, or cycle through dappled sunlight, discovering hidden brooks and panoramic views. It's a place to truly connect with nature, whether you're seeking a gentle stroll or an invigorating adventure.

Name: Bernwood Meadows
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Bernwood Meadows is a 7.5-hectare nature reserve near Oakley in Buckinghamshire.

Name: Berrington Hall
Description: Explore Capability Brown's final landscape design at Berrington, featuring Berrington Pool, a lake and island designated a Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Berwick Glades
Description: This expansive woodland offers a haven for wildlife, with ancient trees and diverse habitats supporting a wealth of species. Visitors can immerse themselves in nature, exploring winding paths perfect for walking and cycling, and discovering the tranquility of this beautiful natural landscape. It's a place to breathe in fresh air and reconnect with the natural world.

Name: Betchworth Quarry and Lime Kilns
Description: Betchworth Quarry and Lime Kilns is a 27-hectare nature reserve north of Betchworth in Surrey.  Betchworth Quarry only is managed by Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Bevere Fish Pass
Description: Bevere Fish Pass is a significant fish pass near Worcester on the River Severn. It allows migratory fish, such as shad and salmon, to bypass Bevere Weir and access upstream spawning grounds. The pass is a key part of the Unlocking the Severn project.

Name: Bewdley
Description: Bewdley sits on the River Severn in the Severn Valley, acting as a gateway to the Wyre Forest national nature reserve.

Name: Bibury
Description: Bibury showcases the beautiful Cotswold landscape, with the River Coln winding through its heart.

Name: Bicester Wetland Reserve
Description: Bicester Wetland Reserve, a former Thames Water sewage sludge disposal site, offers a mosaic of habitats including ponds, scrapes, and reedbed. It supports diverse wildlife, notably wading birds like lapwing and curlew, and various invertebrates. The reserve aims to increase biodiversity within its varied landscapes.

Name: Biddulph Grange
Description: Discover a unique garden renowned for its diverse global plant collections and immersive designed landscapes.

Name: Big Pool Wood
Description: Big Pool Wood is a Nature reserve located near Gronant, Flintshire, Wales.  The site is part of the Dee Estuary SSSI & SAC due to the unique wildlife and organisms found in the area.

Name: Big Waters
Description: Big Waters is nature reserve in Tyne and Wear, England, a pond formed by former mine workings.  It is the largest body of open water in the region, and is designated a Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Bigbury Camp
Description: Bigbury Camp is a univallate hill fort in the parish of Harbledown and Rough Common in Kent in England.  The fort is a Scheduled Ancient Monument, with a list entry identification number of 1005169.

Name: Bignalls, Jaguar Lount and Alistair's Woods
Description: Explore ancient woodlands alive with the rustle of leaves and the songs of diverse birdlife, where dappled sunlight filters through a canopy of mature trees. Wander along winding paths, spot elusive woodland creatures, or cycle through a landscape rich with natural beauty and a sense of peaceful seclusion. This tranquil haven offers a refreshing escape into nature, inviting you to reconnect with the wild.

Name: Birch Moss Covert Nature Reserve
Description: Birch Moss Covert Nature Reserve is a nature reserve managed by the Cheshire Wildlife Trust.  It is located on Carrington Moss, north of Sinderland Lane, which runs off the A56 road at Broadheath, Greater Manchester.

Name: Birchden Wood
Description: Step into a vibrant tapestry of ancient oaks and whispering pines, where sunlight dapples through the canopy, illuminating carpets of wildflowers. This South East woodland teems with life, offering opportunities to spot elusive deer, listen for woodland birdsong, and immerse yourself in the tranquility of nature. Explore winding trails perfect for walking and cycling, uncovering hidden glades and breathing in the fresh, earthy scents of the forest.

Name: Birklands Sherwood Forest
Description: This ancient woodland, steeped in legend, offers a haven of towering trees and dappled sunlight where a rich tapestry of wildlife thrives. Explore winding paths perfect for walking and cycling, immersing yourself in the serene beauty and discovering the natural wonders that have inspired tales for centuries. It's a place to connect with nature, from the rustle of leaves to the call of woodland birds.

Name: Birling Gap
Description: Birling Gap offers dramatic chalk cliffs and a dynamic coastline constantly shaped by powerful coastal erosion.

Name: Birmingham EcoPark
HostOrg: Birmingham and Black Country Wildlife Trust
Description: The Birmingham EcoPark is an environmental education centre in the Small Heath area of Birmingham, England, operated by the Wildlife Trust for Birmingham and the Black Country.  Each year there are thousands of visitors to the site.

Name: Bishop Middleham Quarry
Description: Bishop Middleham Quarry is a disused quarry, about 4 kilometres north-west of Sedgefield, County Durham, England.  Quarry-working here ceased in 1934, and the site has since been colonised by vegetation.

Name: Bishop's Wood
Description: Bishop's Wood is a 33.7-hectare ancient woodland near Selby, North Yorkshire. The site features a diverse mix of tree species and supports rich wildlife, including ground flora. It offers walking trails and is part of a wider landscape.

Name: Bishopswood Meadows
Description: Bishopswood Meadows is a nature reserve situated within the Blackdown Hills Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty in the county of Somerset, England.  The reserve comprises five fields totalling 9.

Name: Bisley and West End Commons and Reidon Hill
Description: Bisley and West End Commons is a 37.2-hectare Local Nature Reserve west of Woking in Surrey.

Name: Black Bourn Valley
Description: Black Bourn Valley, formerly called Grove Farm, is an 88 hectare nature reserve between Thurston and Elmswell in Suffolk.  It is managed by the Suffolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Black Brook Nature Reserve
Description: Black Brook is a nature reserve of the Staffordshire Wildlife Trust, about 7 miles north-east of Leek, in Staffordshire, England.  It is moorland, part of Leek Moors, and most of it is in a Special Area of Conservation.

Name: Black Devon Wetlands
Description: Black Devon Wetlands is a key wildlife reserve near the Firth of Forth in Scotland. It features a mosaic of wetland habitats, including reedbeds, lagoons, and wet grassland. It provides a vital stopping point for migrating birds and supports many resident species. Visitors can observe diverse birdlife from hides.

Name: Black Firs and Cranberry Bog
Description: Black Firs and Cranberry Bog is a nature reserve of the Staffordshire Wildlife Trust, adjacent to Balterley Heath and about 1 mile north of the village of Betley, in Staffordshire, England.  It is an important peatland site; it is designated a Site of Special Scientific Interest, and a Ramsar site.

Name: Black Firs Wood Nature Reserve
Description: Black Firs Wood Nature Reserve is a 1.15-hectare nature reserve managed by the Cheshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Black Hill (Clydesdale)
Description: A prominent South Lanarkshire hill providing extensive panoramic views of the Clyde Valley, Southern Highlands, and distant islands.

Name: Black Lake Nature Reserve
Description: Black Lake is a nature reserve in Delamere Forest, Cheshire, England.  It lies in the southwestern corner of the forest, just south of the Manchester–Chester railway.

Name: Black Moss Covert Nature Reserve
Description: Black Moss Covert Nature Reserve is a 2.1 hectare nature reserve in England managed by the Cheshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Black Mountain Quarry Biodiversity Transition
Description: The Black Mountain Quarry Biodiversity Transition project enhances biodiversity through habitat management, grassland restoration, scrub control, tree planting, and pond creation. This former quarry within the Belfast Hills offers a mosaic of habitats for various wildlife species.

Name: Black Plantation
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 14 hectares.

Name: Black Rocks
Description: Discover a vibrant tapestry of ancient woodland where sunlight dapples through a canopy of mature trees, alive with the buzz of insects and the calls of woodland birds. Wander winding paths that invite exploration, offering opportunities to spot elusive wildlife and immerse yourself in the peaceful beauty of this natural haven. Whether on foot or bike, the landscape provides a refreshing escape for all to enjoy the simple wonders of the forest.

Name: Blacka Moor
HostOrg: Wildlife Trust for Sheffield and Rotherham
Description: Blacka Moor Nature Reserve is a nature reserve located on Hathersage Road between Sheffield and Hathersage in the Peak District National Park in the United Kingdom.  The site is managed by the Wildlife Trust for Sheffield and Rotherham.

Name: Blackburn Flow
Description: Blackburn Flow is a significant peatland restoration project, likely referring to work at Butterburn Flow, a key site within the Border Mires on the Cumbria/Northumberland border. As part of the Great North Bog initiative, it aims to rewet 450 hectares of peatland to reduce carbon emissions and enhance wildlife habitats.

Name: Blackhall Rocks
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 32 hectares.

Name: Blackleach Country Park
Description: Blackleach Country Park is a Green Flag park in Salford, Greater Manchester. It features a large reservoir, woodland, and grassland, providing habitat for diverse wildlife including waterfowl and woodland birds. Visitors enjoy walking, fishing, and birdwatching.

Name: Blackmoor Copse
Description: Blackmoor Copse is a woodland in southeast Wiltshire, England, managed as a nature reserve by the Wiltshire Wildlife Trust.  The copse lies within Pitton and Farley parish, about 5+1⁄2 miles east of Salisbury.

Name: Blackwater
Description: This extensive woodland in South East England offers a haven of ancient trees and vibrant heathland, echoing with the calls of diverse birdlife. Visitors can wander through dappled sunlight, explore winding trails perfect for cycling, and immerse themselves in the tranquil beauty of nature. It's a place to discover rare insects, spot deer, and simply breathe in the fresh air.

Name: Blackwood Forest
Description: Ancient trees create a haven for diverse wildlife, where dappled sunlight filters through a canopy alive with birdsong. Explore winding paths perfect for invigorating walks or cycling adventures, immersing yourself in the tranquil beauty of this natural woodland. Discover a vibrant ecosystem teeming with life, offering a peaceful escape into the heart of nature.

Name: Blagrove Common
Description: Blagrove Common is a 4. 0-hectare Site of Special Scientific Interest in Green End near Sandon in Hertfordshire.

Name: Blair-nam-Faoileag NNR
Description: Blair-nam-Faoileag National Nature Reserve protects a vast area of blanket bog, forming part of the internationally important Flow Country of Caithness and Sutherland. This peatland landscape supports diverse wildlife.

Name: Blakeney Point
Description: Blakeney Point features a shingle spit, sand dunes, and salt marshes, vital for breeding terns, migrating birds, and a large seal colony.

Name: Blashford Lakes
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Blashford Lakes is a 159-hectare nature reserve north of Ringwood in Hampshire, England, which is managed by the Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust.  The site is part of the River Avon System Nature Conservation Review site, Grade I, Avon Valley Ramsar site, River Avon Special Area of Conservation and Special Protection Area, and of Avon Valley, which is a Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Blaxhall Common
Description: Blaxhall Common is a nature reserve in the parish of Blaxhall in the East Suffolk District of Suffolk.  The reserve is owned by Blaxhall Parish Council and managed by Suffolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Blengdale Forest
Description: Venture into this expansive woodland in Northern England, where ancient trees create a haven for diverse wildlife, from chattering squirrels to elusive woodland birds. Explore winding trails perfect for invigorating walks or exhilarating bike rides, immersing yourself in the sights and sounds of nature. This Forestry England gem offers a peaceful escape, inviting you to discover its natural beauty and reconnect with the outdoors.

Name: Blenheim Farm
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Blenheim Farm is a 1-hectare nature reserve near Charlbury in Oxfordshire.  It is owned and managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Blickling Hall
Description: Expansive 5,000-acre parkland embraces a scenic loop of the River Bure, providing diverse habitats for wildlife.

Name: Blidworth Woods
Description: This extensive woodland in the heart of the Midlands offers a haven for diverse wildlife, from rustling leaves underfoot to the calls of woodland birds echoing through ancient trees. Visitors can explore winding paths, ideal for walking and cycling, immersing themselves in the peaceful atmosphere and discovering the natural beauty of this Forestry England managed landscape. It's a place to connect with nature, breathing in the fresh air and enjoying the simple pleasures of the great outdoors.

Name: Blindley Heath
Description: Blindley Heath SSSI is a 26.3-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in the hamlet Blindley Heath, on the southern outskirts of Godstone in Surrey.

Name: Bloody Oaks Quarry
Description: Bloody Oaks Quarry is a 1.3-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north-west of Great Casterton in Rutland.

Name: Blue Bell Hill
Description: Blue Bell Hill is a chalk hill between Maidstone and Rochester in the English county of Kent.  It overlooks the River Medway and is part of the North Downs.

Name: Blue House Farm
Description: Blue House Farm is a 242.8-hectare nature reserve and farm in North Fambridge, on the north bank of the River Crouch between Burnham-on-Crouch and South Woodham Ferrers in Essex.

Name: Bluebank Pools
Description: Bluebank Pools, on the Chesterfield Canal near Staveley, is a former subsidence flash. It now thrives as a vibrant wetland, teeming with diverse wildlife and offering a significant habitat for various species.

Name: Blythe Alive - River Blythe SSSI
Description: Blythe Alive focuses on restoring the River Blythe SSSI and its surrounding habitats. The project enhances biodiversity and climate change resilience by removing weirs, reconnecting the river with its floodplain, and creating new wetlands and ponds. It also involves community engagement.

Name: Boarstall Duck Decoy
Description: A rare working duck decoy surrounded by natural woodland, attracting waterfowl for important ornithological study and ringing.

Name: Boarstall Tower
Description: Explore the wildlife-rich moated grounds and peaceful surrounding gardens of this Buckinghamshire site.

Name: Bodiam Castle
Description: Bodiam Castle is set within an artificial watery landscape, creating unique habitats for wildlife.

Name: Bog Meadows
Description: Bog Meadows, situated off the Falls Road in West Belfast, is a vital urban nature reserve. It offers a mosaic of reedbeds, meadows, ponds, and woodland, providing sanctuary for diverse wildlife including water rail, snipe, and various dragonflies.

Name: Bolam Lake
Description: Bolam Lake Country Park, located between Belsay and Whalton, offers extensive footpaths, lakeside walks, and open grasslands. The site supports diverse wildlife, including red squirrels and birds, across its managed woodlands and meadows, providing recreational and nature study.

Name: Bolberry Down
Description: This stunning clifftop area on the Devon coast boasts panoramic views, forming part of an SSSI within the South Devon AONB for its ecological value.

Name: Bold Forest Park
Description: Bold Forest Park in St Helens is a significant regeneration project transforming 450 hectares of former industrial land into new woodlands, wetlands, and grasslands. It offers walking, cycling, and horse riding opportunities and is part of the larger Mersey Forest initiative.

Name: Bolderwood
Description: Wander through ancient oak and beech trees, where sunlight dapples the forest floor and the air hums with life. This expansive woodland is a haven for diverse wildlife, offering tranquil walking and cycling trails that wind past serene ponds and open glades, inviting exploration and connection with nature. Discover the beauty of this wild space, perfect for a peaceful escape and immersion in the natural world.

Name: Bolton's Bench
Description: Discover a vibrant tapestry of ancient oaks and diverse woodland flora, a haven for wildlife where you might spot deer or hear the songs of woodland birds. This South East England gem offers winding paths perfect for invigorating walks and cycling adventures, allowing you to immerse yourself in the sights and sounds of nature. Explore this captivating landscape and connect with the natural world.

Name: Bonnetts Wood
Description: This ancient woodland in the South East offers a haven for diverse wildlife, from shy deer to vibrant birdlife flitting through the dense canopy. Immerse yourself in nature by exploring winding walking trails and dedicated cycling routes that weave through the trees, revealing picturesque glades and a rich tapestry of flora. It's a perfect place to connect with the natural world and enjoy the tranquility of the forest.

Name: Bonny Wood
Description: Bonny Wood is a 20 hectare nature reserve east of Barking Tye in Suffolk.  It is managed by the Suffolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Bonsai Bank
Description: Bonsai Bank is a flower-rich chalk grassland area within Denge Wood, known for its diverse orchid populations, including the rare Lady Orchid. It features stunted conifers, which gave it its name, and supports a rich ground flora on its sloping terrain.

Name: Bonsley Common
Description: Wander through ancient oak and beech woodlands teeming with diverse birdlife, where dappled sunlight illuminates winding paths perfect for exploring on foot or by bike. This expansive woodland offers a tranquil escape into nature, inviting visitors to discover its hidden glades and observe the gentle rhythm of wildlife. It's a place to reconnect with the outdoors, breathing in the fresh air and immersing yourself in the beauty of the natural world.

Name: Bookham Commons
Description: Bookham Commons comprise a large Site of Special Scientific Interest, preserving diverse natural habitats and wildlife.

Name: Booton Common
Description: Booton Common is an 8.2-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north-west of Norwich in Norfolk, England.

Name: Borough Hill
Description: Borough Hill, a Local Nature Reserve near Daventry, comprises heathland, grassland, and scrub. It supports rare plants and diverse butterflies. The site includes an Iron Age hillfort and Roman villa remains, with views across Northamptonshire.

Name: Borthwood Copse
Description: Borthwood Copse is an ancient woodland on the Isle of Wight, home to red squirrels, ancient oaks, beech groves, and spring bluebells with vivid autumn colours.

Name: Boscastle
Description: Boscastle offers a natural harbour on the stunning north Cornish coast, nestled within river valleys and the designated Cornwall National Landscape, traversed by the South West Coast Path.

Name: Botallack Mine
Description: Part of a coastal SSSI, this site offers dramatic cliffs and breathtaking views along the South West Coast Path.

Name: Bough Beech
Description: Bough Beech reservoir and surrounding woodland in west Kent is a Site of Special Scientific Interest. Formerly managed by Kent Wildlife Trust until July 2020, it is now managed by Sutton and East Surrey Water. It offers important habitats for wildfowl, waders, and gulls, with bird hides available for observation.

Name: Boughton Brake
Description: Discover a haven of ancient woodland in the heart of the Midlands, where dappled sunlight filters through a canopy of mature trees, creating a magical atmosphere. This tranquil forest teems with life, offering opportunities to spot diverse wildlife amidst its winding paths, perfect for leisurely walks or invigorating cycles. Immerse yourself in the natural beauty and breathing space this woodland provides.

Name: Bouldnor Forest
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 38 hectares.

Name: Boundary Wood
Description: Discover a vibrant tapestry of ancient trees and open glades teeming with life. This expansive woodland offers a haven for diverse wildlife, from soaring birds to shy woodland creatures. Explore winding trails perfect for walking and cycling, immersing yourself in the sights and sounds of nature.

Name: Bourne Mill, Colchester
Description: Bourne Mill's tranquil waterside setting supports a rich array of aquatic and riparian wildlife.

Name: Bourne Wood, Bourne
Description: Explore a vibrant tapestry of ancient oaks and whispering pines, a haven for diverse wildlife where sunlight dapples through the canopy. This expansive woodland offers miles of winding trails perfect for invigorating walks and scenic cycling adventures, inviting you to immerse yourself in the sights and sounds of nature. Discover a tranquil escape, alive with the buzz of insects, the calls of birds, and the rustle of unseen creatures.

Name: Bourne Wood, Farnham
Description: This expansive woodland in South East England offers a haven of natural beauty, where ancient trees shelter a diverse array of wildlife. Visitors can explore miles of winding paths and trails, perfect for walking, cycling, and immersing themselves in the tranquil sounds and sights of nature. From spotting woodland birds to enjoying the vibrant colours of the changing seasons, it's a place to reconnect with the outdoors.

Name: Bovey Heath
Description: Bovey Heath is a 32 hectare area of heathland between Bovey Tracey and Heathfield in south Devon, England.  Although primarily heathland habitat, the site has some wet mature oak woodland, and is home to rare species such as the Dartford warbler, European stonechat, European nightjar and the narrow headed ant.

Name: Bovey Valley Woods
Description: Bovey Valley Woods, within Dartmoor National Park, is an ancient woodland patchwork along the River Bovey. Managed by The Woodland Trust, it provides critical habitat for dormice, otters, and rare bats, featuring significant geological formations.

Name: Bow Creek Ecology Park
Description: Bow Creek Ecology Park is a wildlife haven in East London, at the confluence of Bow Creek and the River Thames. It features diverse wetland and brownfield habitats, supporting birds, insects, and plants, with peaceful walking routes and viewing platforms.

Name: Bowder Stone
Description: Set in Cumbria's scenic Borrowdale, the colossal Bowder Stone is a 2000-ton lava boulder that dramatically fell from Bowder Crag, a true geological marvel.

Name: Bowdown Woods
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Bowdown and Chamberhouse Woods is a 67.9-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south of Thatcham in Berkshire.

Name: Box Farm Meadows SSSI
Description: Box Farm Meadows is a 8.3-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Gloucestershire, notified in 1985.

Name: Box Hill, Surrey
Description: Discover ancient box woodlands and chalk downland, a haven for orchids and 38 butterfly species, with panoramic views across the Surrey Hills.

Name: Brackfield Wood
Description: Brackfield Wood is The Woodland Trust's First World War Centenary Wood for Ireland, nestled within the stunning Faughan Valley Woodlands, a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI). It is home to native tree species and diverse wildlife, including red squirrel, otter, and Atlantic salmon in the River Faughan. The site offers a network of footpaths for walking and nature observation, providing views of the River Faughan, and connects with other woods in the Faughan Valley.

Name: Bradenham, Buckinghamshire
Description: Discover a tranquil landscape of ancient beech woods and rare chalk grasslands, home to diverse wildlife within the scenic Chiltern Hills.

Name: Bradfield Woods
Description: Bradfield Woods is an 81.4-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest between Bury St Edmunds and Stowmarket in Suffolk.

Name: Bradley (house)
Description: Bradley is nestled amidst ancient woodlands and wildflower meadows, within the scenic valley of the River Lemon in Devon.

Name: Bradley Canal Restoration & Habitat Link
Description: This project restores a disused canal stretch in Bilston, West Midlands, creating a vital 'green corridor' linking existing green spaces. It aims to improve access to green and blue spaces and provide new walking and cycling routes.

Name: Bradwell Shell Bank
Description: Bradwell Shell Bank is a nature reserve on the coast of the Dengie Peninsula near Bradwell-on-Sea in Essex.  It is managed by the Essex Wildlife Trust.

Name: Braeburn Park
Description: Braeburn Park is a 22.3-hectare nature reserve in Crayford in the London Borough of Bexley.

Name: Bramley Bank
Description: Bramley Bank is a 10.3 hectare local nature reserve in Upper Shirley in the London Borough of Croydon.

Name: Bramshill Plantation
Description: Discover a haven of ancient trees and vibrant wildlife nestled in the heart of the South East. Wander through sun-dappled paths, keeping an eye out for elusive deer and colourful woodland birds. This expansive woodland offers ample opportunities for exploring on foot or by bike, immersing yourself in the sights and sounds of nature.

Name: Brandon Marsh nature reserve
Description: Brandon Marsh is a Site of Special Scientific Interest and nature reserve in Warwickshire, England.  It is situated adjacent to the River Avon, near the village of Brandon, a few miles east of Coventry.

Name: Brankley Pastures
Description: Brankley Pastures is a nature reserve of the Staffordshire Wildlife Trust.  It is about 2.

Name: Brassey SSSI
Description: Brassey is a 2.1-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Gloucestershire, notified in 1954 and renotified in 1983.

Name: Brean Down
Description: Brean Down is a dramatic limestone promontory extending into the Bristol Channel, featuring ancient fossils, diverse wildlife, and nationally rare plants.

Name: Brean Down Fort
Description: Brean Down Fort sits atop a dramatic coastal headland, offering breathtaking panoramic views of the Bristol Channel.

Name: Breckland
Description: Breckland in Norfolk and Suffolk is a 39,433 hectare Breckland_Forest Special Protection Area under the European Union Directive on the Conservation of Wild Birds.  The SPA partly overlaps the 7,544 hectare Breckland Special Area of Conservation.

Name: Bredhurst Wood
Description: Bredhurst Woods is a 600-acre (approximately 240-hectare) ancient woodland surrounded by chalk grassland, located on the North Downs in Kent. It is a Local Wildlife Site and part of the Kent Downs Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. Primarily managed by the Bredhurst Woodland Action Group (BWAG) in collaboration with Kent Wildlife Trust, the site features diverse oak, hornbeam, and sweet chestnut trees, and supports a rich biodiversity including fungi, invertebrates, butterflies (such as Adonis blue), and dormice.

Name: Bredon Barn
Description: Located by the River Avon, the area provides excellent opportunities to observe waterside wildlife and riparian ecosystems.

Name: Brenchley Wood
Description: Brenchley Wood is a 15-hectare nature reserve south of Paddock Wood in Kent.  It is managed by the Kent Wildlife Trust, and it is part of the High Weald Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty.

Name: Breney Common
Description: Breney Common is a nature reserve and Site of Special Scientific Interest, noted for its biological characteristics, in mid Cornwall, England, UK.  It is located mainly in Lanlivery civil parish, with the Saints' Way footpath running through it.

Name: Brentmoor Heath and Folly Bog
Description: Brentmoor Heath is a 28.6-hectare Local Nature Reserve east of Camberley in Surrey.

Name: Brettenham Heath
Description: Brettenham Heath is a National Nature Reserve in Norfolk, located north-east of Thetford. It is an important area of heathland, woodland, and acid grassland, forming part of the Breckland Special Area of Conservation and Special Protection Area. The reserve supports breeding woodlark, nightjar, and stone-curlew, along with reptiles such as slow-worm, common lizard, and adder. It is home to a diverse flora with over 240 plant species recorded.

Name: Brickfield Meadow
Description: Brickfield Meadow is a 1.4-hectare nature reserve north of Maresfield in East Sussex.

Name: Briddlesford Woods
Description: Briddlesford Woods is an ancient woodland and Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) on the Isle of Wight, managed by the People's Trust for Endangered Species (PTES). It is a significant habitat for red squirrels, dormice, and various bird species, featuring a mix of oak, ash, and hazel.

Name: Bridgham Heath
Description: Bridgham Heath, a fragment of Breckland heathland in Norfolk, features dry acid grassland, heather, and small copses. It supports diverse insects, common lizards, and various bird species, actively managed for conservation.

Name: Brierdene LNR
Description: Brierdene LNR, also known as Brierdene Wildlife Site, is a coastal denemouth and designated Site of Nature Conservation Importance (SNCI) in Whitley Bay, North Tyneside. It encompasses woodland, grassland, and freshwater habitats, supporting diverse wildlife. The dene connects directly to the beach, offering varied coastal and woodland environments. It is actively managed by the Friends of Brierdene, with support from Northumberland Wildlife Trust.

Name: Brimham Rocks
Description: This SSSI features spectacular water-eroded gritstone formations amidst a mosaic of upland birch woodland and valuable wet and dry heath, supporting specialised plants.

Name: Brinsley Headstocks
Description: Brinsley Headstocks is a 5.17-hectare Local Nature Reserve near Eastwood, Nottinghamshire. The site preserves former colliery structures and offers diverse habitats, including grassland and wetlands, supporting varied wildlife. It is managed for both heritage and biodiversity.

Name: Broad Colney Lakes
Description: Broad Colney Lakes is an 11 hectare nature reserve previously managed by Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust in London Colney in Hertfordshire.  It has recently been sold to an anonymous buyer but reports in The Herts Advertiser says "the selected buyer has stated that the site will continue to be used for fishing, with the woodland managed for the benefit of wildlife.

Name: Broadham Down
Description: Broadham Down is a 16-hectare nature reserve east of Chilham and west of Canterbury in Kent.  It is managed by the Kent Wildlife Trust.

Name: Broadstreet, Backside and Rydes Commons
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 158 hectares.

Name: Broadwater Lake
Description: Mid Colne Valley is a 132 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Harefield in the London Borough of Hillingdon and Denham in South Buckinghamshire.  Its main importance lies in its extensive diversity of birdlife in lakes in former gravel pits.

Name: Broaks Wood
Description: This expansive woodland in South East England offers a rich tapestry of ancient trees, vibrant meadows, and diverse wildlife, providing a haven for nature lovers. Visitors can explore winding paths perfect for walking and cycling, immersing themselves in the tranquil beauty of the natural environment and spotting a variety of woodland creatures. It's a place to connect with nature, breathe fresh air, and experience the simple joys of the outdoors.

Name: Brockham Limeworks
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 45 hectares.

Name: Brockhampton Estate
Description: Explore Brockhampton Estate's extensive woodlands, ancient parkland with specimen trees, and diverse farmland in the heart of Herefordshire.

Name: Brockholes Nature Reserve
Description: Brockholes is a nature reserve near Preston, Lancashire, England, just off Junction 31 of the M6 motorway.  It is owned by the Wildlife Trust for Lancashire, Manchester and North Merseyside.

Name: Brodick Castle
Description: Immerse yourself in spectacular gardens and designed landscapes, offering breathtaking views across the Firth of Clyde from the Isle of Arran.

Name: Brodie Castle
Description: Its diverse grounds, included in Scotland's Inventory of Gardens and Designed Landscapes, showcase varied plant life.

Name: Brodsworth Community Woodland
Description: Brodsworth Community Woodland is a former colliery site in South Yorkshire. TCV supports its management, with ongoing activities including path maintenance, tree planting, and coppicing. The woodland offers views across the Dearne Valley.

Name: Bromeswell Green
Description: Bromeswell Green is a 7.2-hectare nature reserve in Bromeswell, east of Woodbridge in Suffolk.

Name: Brompton Cemetery
Description: Brompton Cemetery is a Grade I listed garden cemetery established in 1840 in West London. It features over 20,000 monuments, including notable figures like Emmeline Pankhurst, and a diverse range of trees and wildlife. Managed by The Royal Parks, it is a site of special historic interest.

Name: Brooke House
Description: Brooke House in Ashbocking, north of Ipswich in Suffolk is the headquarters of the Suffolk Wildlife Trust.  The house was left to the trust by Mary Brooke.

Name: Brookes Nature Reserve
Description: Belcher's and Broadfield Woods is a 14.4-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest between Halstead and Braintree in Essex.

Name: Brookheys Covert Nature Reserve
Description: Brookheys Covert Nature Reserve is a Site of Special Scientific Interest and nature reserve managed by the Cheshire Wildlife Trust.  It is located at SJ 742 904 in Greater Manchester.

Name: Brookwood Lye
Description: Brookwood Lye is a 22-hectare nature reserve in Brookwood in Surrey.  It is managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Brotheridge Green Nature Reserve
Description: Brotheridge Green Nature Reserve is a nature reserve of the Worcestershire Wildlife Trust at Brotheridge Green, about 2.5 miles west of Upton-upon-Severn, in Worcestershire, England.

Name: Brough Law
Description: Brough Law is a Cheviot grassland site within Northumberland National Park undergoing peatland restoration. Volunteers remove non-native conifers and plant sphagnum moss to restore natural habitat and biodiversity. This project enhances the peatland ecosystem.

Name: Broughton Down
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Broughton Down is a 45.8-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest west of Broughton in Hampshire.

Name: Broughton House
Description: Discover the tranquil, Japanese-influenced gardens, celebrated for their unique design and horticultural beauty.

Name: Brown End Quarry
Description: Brown End Quarry is a nature reserve of the Staffordshire Wildlife Trust, near the village of Waterhouses in Staffordshire, England.  It is designated a Site of Special Scientific Interest, and a regionally important geological site.

Name: Brown's Folly
Description: Browne's Folly, or Brown's Folly, is a folly tower sitting within a 39.9 hectare biological and geological Site of Special Scientific Interest near the English village of Bathford in Somerset, notified in 1974: the site itself is known as the Farleigh Down Stone Quarry and is managed as a nature reserve by the Avon Wildlife Trust.

Name: Brownsea Island
Description: A haven of woodland and heath on Poole Harbour, Brownsea Island supports a wide variety of wildlife and offers superb coastal views.

Name: Broxa Forest
Description: Ancient woodlands and open heathland create a diverse tapestry of habitats within this expansive Forestry England woodland. Discover a rich array of wildlife, from soaring birds of prey to elusive mammals, as you explore miles of trails perfect for walking and cycling. Immerse yourself in the natural beauty, breathing in the fresh air and enjoying the tranquility of this northern English gem.

Name: BrueCREW River Restoration Bruton
Description: BrueCREW is a community group in Bruton, Somerset, focused on restoring, enhancing, and protecting the River Brue. They remove obstructions, create habitats, and manage invasive species to improve biodiversity for people and wildlife.

Name: Bucinch
Description: Bucinch is a heavily wooded island in Loch Lomond, rising steeply from a rocky coastline to a central summit.

Name: Buckland Park Lake
Description: Buckland Park Lake, a 50-acre site in Surrey, features a large spring-fed lake and diverse woodland, including Ancient Semi-Natural Woodland. Once a chalk quarry, it supports varied flora and fauna, offering birdwatching and walking trails.

Name: Bucklebury Common
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Bucklebury Common is an elevated common consisting of woodland with a few relatively small clearings in the English county of Berkshire, within the civil parish of Bucklebury centred 3 miles northeast of Thatcham and encircling the settled localities of Upper Bucklebury and Chapel Row.  It is one of the largest commons in Southern England covering 350 hectares.

Name: Budby South Forest
Description: Budby South Forest is a significant remnant of Sherwood Forest's ancient woodland. This RSPB reserve features open heathland, acid grassland, and mature trees, supporting species such as nightjars, woodlarks, and various heathland plants. Management focuses on restoring and maintaining diverse habitats.

Name: Bull Cross, The Frith And Juniper Hill
Description: Bull Cross, The Frith and Juniper Hill is a 42.33-hectare biological and geological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Gloucestershire, notified in 1954.

Name: Bull's Wood
Description: Bull's Wood is a 12 hectare nature reserve east of Cockfield in Suffolk, England.  It is managed by the Suffolk Wildlife Trust, and is part of the Thorpe Morieux Woods Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Bumble Hole & Warrens Hall Local Nature Reserves
Description: Bumble Hole and Warrens Hall Local Nature Reserves sit at a historic canal junction in the West Midlands. The site features restored canals, diverse wildlife habitats, and walking trails, offering a valuable green space for nature enthusiasts.

Name: Burgess Field
Description: Burgess Field Nature Park is a nature reserve of approximately 30-35 hectares (74-75 acres) on Oxford's northern edge, located between Port Meadow and the railway line, close to the River Thames. It features open grassland, scrub, and mature trees. Habitats include rough open grassland, small copses, and a wildflower meadow, supporting diverse wildlife like birds, butterflies, and deer.

Name: Burham Down
Description: Burham Down is a 110-hectare nature reserve between Maidstone and Chatham in Kent.  It is managed by the Kent Wildlife Trust.

Name: Burham Marsh
Description: Burham Marsh nature reserve is an 11 hectare tidal Reed bed on the River Medway 5 miles northwest of Maidstone.  It is just east of Snodland but being on the east bank of the river it is accessed via Burham.

Name: Burner's Heath and Swallows Pond
Description: Burner's Heath and Swallows Pond is a 5-hectare nature reserve in Pirbright in Surrey.  It is owned by Surrey County Council and managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Burnham Beeches
Description: Burnham Beeches is a National Nature Reserve and Site of Special Scientific Interest in Buckinghamshire. Managed by the City of London Corporation, it features ancient woodland, heathland, and ponds, supporting diverse wildlife. It is popular for walking and nature observation.

Name: Burnhope Pond
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 14 hectares.

Name: Burntollet Wood
Description: Burntollet Wood spans a steep valley slope overlooking the River Faughan. Mature broadleaf trees dominate, supporting diverse wildlife. Walking trails lead through this ancient woodland, designated an Area of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Burrow Mump
Description: A prominent hill overlooking the vast Southlake Moor and the meeting point of the Rivers Tone, Cary, and Parrett.

Name: Burton and Chingford Ponds
Description: Burton Park SSSI is a 57.7-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest west of Pulborough in West Sussex.

Name: Bury Ditches
Description: This ancient woodland in South East England offers a haven for wildlife, with carpets of bluebells in spring and a rich tapestry of trees that provide shelter for diverse birdlife. Visitors can immerse themselves in nature by exploring winding paths, perfect for walking or cycling, and discover the tranquility of this expansive green space. It's a place to connect with the natural world and enjoy the simple pleasure of a woodland stroll.

Name: Bury Lodge Wetlands
Description: Bury Lodge Wetlands in Enfield is a restoration project led by Thames21, in partnership with Enfield Council. The wetlands were created to improve water quality in the Salmons Brook by intercepting and treating polluted surface water runoff from the A10 and surrounding urban areas. This also helps reduce flood risk and enhances biodiversity. Community volunteering events regularly support these ecological enhancements.

Name: Buscot Park
Description: Explore Buscot Park's extensive formal and informal gardens and grounds, featuring diverse landscapes.

Name: Bushy Park - Water Gardens & Pheasantry
Description: Bushy Park's historic Water Gardens feature canals, ponds, and cascades, creating diverse habitats for birds and amphibians. The nearby Pheasantry area supports various ground-nesting birds and woodland species.

Name: Bushy Park SSSI
Description: Bushy Park is London's second largest Royal Park, covering 445 hectares. It features woodlands, formal gardens, and diverse wildlife, including free-roaming herds of deer. The park holds Site of Special Scientific Interest status.

Name: Butcher's Wood
Description: Butcher's Wood is a 7-hectare (17-acre) ancient semi-natural woodland at the northern extremity of the South Downs National Park in West Sussex. It is situated just outside of the village of Hassocks, between Burgess Hill to the north and Brighton to the south. The wood features diverse broadleaf trees and valuable ground flora, including extensive bluebells and wood anemones, and offers a network of permissive paths for visitors.

Name: Butterdon Wood
Description: Butterdon Wood is a 16-acre woodland in Moretonhampstead, Devon, serving as the outdoor base for Running Deer School. It provides a natural environment for specialist education, offering activities in traditional rural skills, bushcraft, conservation, and supporting young people with special educational needs.

Name: Buttermere and Ennerdale
Description: Expansive fells and common land, vital woodlands, and pristine lakes like Buttermere, Crummock Water, and Ennerdale Water define this stunning landscape.

Name: Cabilla and Redrice Woods
Description: Cabilla and Redrice Woods is a nature reserve of the Cornwall Wildlife Trust, about 3 miles east of Bodmin, in Cornwall, England.  It is an extensive area of mixed woodland.

Name: Cable Street Community Garden
Description: Cable Street Community Gardens provides green spaces in Tower Hamlets, East London, where residents grow food, enjoy nature, and connect. A network of garden sites host regular events and workshops, promoting biodiversity and community engagement for local residents.

Name: Cadbury Camp
Description: Actively managed scrub and woodland habitats on this hill fort provide a rich environment for wildlife.

Name: Cadishead and Little Woolden Moss
Description: Cadishead and Little Woolden Moss is a nature reserve of the Wildlife Trust for Lancashire, Manchester and North Merseyside, an area of Chat Moss which is being restored to its former state of peatland.

Name: Caer Brân
Description: Caer Brân is an important multi-period hillfort site in west Cornwall, a Scheduled Monument, with archaeological remains from both the Bronze Age and Iron Age periods. Visible remnants of ring cairns and an unfinished Iron Age hillfort are within its ramparts. The site offers panoramic views and supports diverse flora and fauna, which Cornwall Heritage Trust works to protect.

Name: Caerlaverock NNR
Description: Caerlaverock NNR protects expansive saltmarsh and mudflats on the Solway Firth, a critical wintering ground for barnacle geese and other wildfowl. The site supports diverse coastal habitats, offering birdwatching and walking opportunities.

Name: Cairngorms Connect
Description: Cairngorms Connect is a partnership of land managers working across 600 square kilometres of the Cairngorms National Park in Scotland. The project focuses on restoring habitats, enhancing species, and improving ecological processes over a 200-year timescale.

Name: Calf of Man
Description: Calf of Man is a 2.50-square-kilometre island, off the southwest coast of the Isle of Man.

Name: Calshot Marshes
Description: Calshot Marshes, a coastal reserve in Hampshire, features saltmarsh, reedbed, and freshwater lagoons. It provides habitat for bird species. The site is managed to mitigate coastal squeeze and adapt to sea-level rise.

Name: Calvert Jubilee
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Calvert Jubilee is a 22 hectares nature reserve in Calvert near Steeple Claydon in Buckinghamshire.  It is managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Cambourne Nature Reserve
Description: Cambourne Nature Reserve is a 170-hectare site featuring woodlands, wetlands, and grasslands. Three large lakes and ponds support diverse wildlife, including birds, insects, and mammals. Managed by Wildlife BCN, the reserve provides walking trails and birdwatching.

Name: Cambus o'May
Description: Cambus o'May is an ancient Caledonian pinewood forest between Ballater and Dinnet, north of the River Dee. Restoration returns it to a natural state, rich in native Scots pine through non-native species removal. Waymarked trails are available.

Name: Camley Street Natural Park
Description: Camley Street Natural Park is an urban nature reserve in St Pancras in central London and within the London Borough of Camden.  It is a local nature reserve.

Name: Cann Wood
Description: This expansive woodland in the heart of South West England offers a haven for diverse wildlife, with ancient trees creating a majestic canopy that shelters a wealth of flora and fauna. Visitors can immerse themselves in nature by exploring a network of trails perfect for walking and cycling, discovering the peaceful beauty of this managed forest. It's a place to connect with the natural world, observe wildlife in its habitat, and enjoy the serene atmosphere.

Name: Canna, Scotland
Description: This remote Inner Hebridean island is a conservation area, known for its unique coastal landscape and sandbank links to Sanday.

Name: Cannock Chase Forest
Description: This vast expanse of ancient woodland in the heart of the Midlands offers a sanctuary for diverse wildlife, from soaring birds of prey to elusive deer. Visitors can explore miles of trails winding through towering trees and heathland, perfect for invigorating walks and exhilarating cycle rides amidst the beauty of nature. It's a place to reconnect with the wild, breathe fresh air, and discover the vibrant ecosystems thriving within its embrace.

Name: Cannop Ponds
Description: Cannop Ponds are two large ponds, just north of Parkend in the Forest of Dean, Gloucestershire, England.  The ponds, and surrounding area, are a popular tourist destination.

Name: Cannop Ponds
Description: Explore a diverse woodland teeming with life in the heart of South East England. Wander along scenic paths, cycle through dappled sunlight, and immerse yourself in the tranquility of nature, spotting a variety of birds and woodland creatures. This vibrant landscape offers a perfect escape for those seeking outdoor adventure and a connection with the natural world.

Name: Canons Ashby House
Description: Experience the tranquil meadows of Canons Ashby, a valuable habitat supporting local wildlife within the Northamptonshire landscape.

Name: Canons Park
Description: Canons Park in Harrow is a Green Flag award-winning park featuring formal gardens, woodlands, and a lake. It serves as a vital ecological corridor, linking local green spaces and supporting diverse wildlife. The park offers recreational opportunities for the community.

Name: Canonteign Forest
Description: This extensive woodland in the South West of England offers a haven for diverse wildlife, from soaring birds of prey to elusive woodland creatures. Visitors can immerse themselves in the tranquil atmosphere, exploring ancient trees and winding trails that are perfect for walking and cycling adventures. The vibrant natural environment provides endless opportunities for nature observation and peaceful escape.

Name: Canvey Wick
Description: Canvey Wick is a unique brownfield site, renowned for its diverse invertebrate population, including rare bees and moths. It offers grassland and scrub habitats on former oil refinery land, now a Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Canvey Wick
Description: Canvey Wick is a former oil refinery site on Canvey Island, Essex, now a nationally important nature reserve. Recognised for its biodiversity, it supports rare invertebrates, plants, grassland, scrub, and wetland habitats.

Name: Captain's Wood
Description: Captain's Wood is a 62 hectare nature reserve in Sudbourne in Suffolk.  It is owned and managed by the Suffolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Carding Mill Valley
Description: Carding Mill Valley offers stunning 'Little Switzerland' landscapes within the Shropshire Hills Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, showcasing ancient geology.

Name: Cardinham Woods
Description: Explore a vibrant tapestry of ancient oak, beech, and pine trees that create a haven for diverse wildlife, from soaring birds of prey to shy woodland mammals. This expansive woodland invites you to wander along winding trails, perfect for both leisurely walks and invigorating cycling adventures, immersing yourself in the sights and sounds of nature. Discover hidden streams, enjoy panoramic views, and breathe in the fresh air of this beautiful natural landscape.

Name: Carlton and Oulton Marshes
Description: Carlton and Oulton Marshes is a 151 hectare nature reserve in Lowestoft in Suffolk.  It is managed by the Suffolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Carmel National Nature Reserve

Name: Carnewas & Bedruthan Steps
Description: Explore the dramatic cliff-tops and rocky beaches of Carnewas & Bedruthan Steps, a stunning stretch of north Cornish coastline shaped by powerful tides.

Name: Carngafallt
Description: Carngafallt, a mid-Wales reserve, features ancient upland oakwood, moorland, and rush pastures. It supports breeding curlew, lapwing, and other wading birds. Red kites are common. The site is managed for wildlife, with walking trails.

Name: Carnmoney Hill
Description: Carnmoney Hill is a local nature reserve with ancient woodland, wildflower meadows, and open grassland. It offers panoramic views of Belfast Lough and is home to diverse wildlife, including red squirrels and long-eared owls. Managed for conservation and public access.

Name: Carsington Water
Description: Carsington Water is a reservoir, operated by Severn Trent Water, between Wirksworth and Kniveton in Derbyshire, England.  The reservoir takes water from the River Derwent at Ambergate during winter months, pumping up to the reservoir by 10.

Name: Cassiobury Park
Description: Cassiobury Park is the principal public park in Watford, Hertfordshire, in England.  It was created in 1909 from the purchase by Watford Borough Council of part of the estate of the Earls of Essex around Cassiobury House which was subsequently demolished in 1927.

Name: Cassiobury Park LNR
Description: Cassiobury Park Local Nature Reserve, managed by Watford Borough Council with the Wildlife Trust, offers diverse habitats including woodland, river, and grassland. It is home to various bird species and invertebrates, providing a valuable urban green space.

Name: Castern Wood
Description: Castern Wood is a nature reserve of the Staffordshire Wildlife Trust.  It is an ancient woodland, with scrub and grassland, on the eastern slopes of the Manifold Valley, about 1 mile south of Wetton, in Staffordshire, England.

Name: Castle Drogo
Description: Standing on a mountain, Castle Drogo features significant listed gardens, combining wild landscape with cultivated natural beauty.

Name: Castle Marshes
Description: Castle Marshes is a 71 hectare nature reserve west of Lowestoft in Suffolk.  It is managed by the Suffolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Castle Neroche
Description: Explore a diverse landscape of ancient woodlands and open glades, alive with the chatter of birds and the rustle of unseen creatures. Wander through dappled sunlight, where winding paths invite exploration by foot or bike, revealing the beauty of native flora and fauna. This expansive woodland offers a tranquil escape, perfect for connecting with nature and enjoying the simple pleasures of the outdoors.

Name: Castlefield Viaduct
Description: An urban sky park transforms this elevated structure into a vibrant green oasis, offering unique perspectives on city nature.

Name: Caswell Wood

Name: Catfield Fen
Description: Catfield Fen is a nationally and internationally important wetland site within the Broads SAC. Designated as an SSSI and Ramsar site, it is arguably the UK's most species-rich wetland. The site is a private reserve and not open to the public.

Name: Catherton Common
Description: Catherton Common is a nature reserve of the Shropshire Wildlife Trust, between Cleehill and Cleobury Mortimer in Shropshire, England.  It is heathland, designated a Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Cattersty Gill Nature Reserve
Description: A local nature reserve.

Name: Cave Hill Country Park
Description: Cave Hill Country Park is an iconic green space in Belfast, Northern Ireland. It features walking trails, caves, and offers panoramic views over the city and Belfast Lough. The park is known for its biodiversity and historical significance, including Napoleon's Nose.

Name: Cawfields & the Whin Sill
Description: Cawfields Quarry, a Roman Wall site and Dark Sky Discovery location, sits near Haltwhistle. The Whin Sill, a prominent dolerite intrusion, forms a key geological ridge in Northumberland. Its unique basalt grasslands support specific flora, targeted for conservation by the Hadrian's Wall Wetlands project.

Name: Cely Woods
Description: Discover a haven of ancient trees and vibrant wildlife, where sunlight dapples through a rich canopy and winding paths invite exploration. This South East England woodland offers a peaceful escape, perfect for leisurely walks amidst nature's beauty or invigorating cycles along scenic routes, all while keeping an eye out for the diverse creatures that call this place home. Immerse yourself in the sights and sounds of a thriving natural environment.

Name: Centenary Wood

Name: Centre of the Earth

Description: The Centre of the Earth is a purpose-built environmental education centre in Birmingham, England, run by the Wildlife Trust for Birmingham and the Black Country.

Name: Cerne Giant

Name: Chaceley Meadow SSSI

Name: Chafford Gorges Nature Park

It's an ideal destination for anyone seeking connection with nature and a breath of fresh air.

Name: Chalkney Wood

Explore winding paths perfect for walking and cycling, immersing yourself in the sights and sounds of nature. Keep an eye out for diverse birdlife and the subtle signs of woodland creatures as you enjoy the peaceful embrace of this South East England gem.

Name: Chambers Farm Wood

Visitors can wander along peaceful trails, immersing themselves in the sights and sounds of nature, or explore by bicycle, discovering hidden glades and open spaces. It's a perfect place to connect with the natural world, observe woodland creatures, and enjoy invigorating outdoor activity.

Name: Chappetts Copse
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust

Name: Chargot Wood

Name: Chartwell
Description: Discover the serene gardens and tranquil lakes, offering a peaceful landscape in the Kent countryside.

Name: Chasewater Country Park
Description: Chasewater Country Park, located in Staffordshire, spans approximately 360 hectares (900 acres), including 90 hectares of water. It is designated as a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) for its rare plants and invertebrates. The reservoir, originally built as a canal feeder, is the largest in the West Midlands and provides water for the Birmingham Canal Network. The park offers diverse habitats, watersports, walking, and a heritage railway.

Name: Chawridge Bank
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust

Wander winding paths, cycle through dappled glades, and immerse yourself in the sights and sounds of nature, from birdsong to the rustle of leaves underfoot. This expansive woodland offers a refreshing escape for all who seek connection with the natural world.

Name: Cheddar Complex
