Name: Cheddar Wood
Description: Cheddar Wood is an 86.9-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest at Cheddar in the Mendip Hills, Somerset, England, notified in 1967.

Name: Chedworth Nature Reserve
Description: Chedworth Nature Reserve is a 6-hectare nature reserve in Gloucestershire.  The site is listed in the 'Cotswold District' Local Plan 2001-2011 as a Key Wildlife Site.

Name: Cherry Hinton Chalk Pits
Description: Cherry Hinton Chalk Pits, a Cambridgeshire SSSI managed by Wildlife BCN, features grassland, scrub, and woodland. The site supports diverse plant and insect species, and is known for rare orchids and butterfly populations.

Name: Chessel Bay
Description: Chessel Bay Local Nature Reserve on the River Itchen in Southampton is a vital high-tide roost for waders and wildfowl like curlew and shelduck. Its mudflats and saltmarsh habitats support diverse marine life. Public footpaths offer access.

Name: Cheviot Summit
Description: The Cheviot Summit site is part of a large-scale peatland restoration project within Northumberland National Park. This initiative aims to improve water quality, enhance biodiversity, and increase carbon storage in the upland peatlands.

Name: Chichester Harbour National Landscape
Description: Chichester Harbour National Landscape, a large natural harbour in Southern England, is a protected Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. The Chichester Harbour Conservancy manages the landscape, focusing on conservation, recreation, and planning within this cherished coastal area.

Name: Chiddingstone

Description: Chimswell Wood is a young broadleaf woodland, planted in November 1998 as part of the 'Woods on your Doorstep' project near Haverhill. It features a pond, open grassland, and a network of accessible paths, providing a local green space for walks.

Thames21 collaborates with the local council on environmental projects, regularly hosting volunteering events for community participation.

Spring wildflowers, including bluebells and wild garlic, provide seasonal interest for quiet walks.

Name: Church Farm Marshes
Description: Church Farm Marshes is a 56 hectare nature reserve in Thorington in Suffolk.  It is managed by the Suffolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Church Wood
Description: Church Wood is a large ancient woodland in Kent, forming part of the Blean Complex. It features mature sweet chestnut coppice and oak standards, providing habitat for rare heath fritillary butterflies, various bird species, and diverse flora. Public footpaths allow access.

Name: Churchtown Farm
Description: Churchtown Farm is a community nature reserve one mile south of Saltash, Cornwall, England.  It is leased from Antony Estate and managed by Cornwall Wildlife Trust, and includes diverse habitats such as grassland, estuarine mudflats, wetland, woodland, disused quarries and hedgerows.

Name: Cleethorpes Sands Local Nature Reserve
Description: Cleethorpes Sands Local Nature Reserve encompasses diverse coastal habitats including sand dunes, saltmarsh, and intertidal flats. Located on the Humber Estuary, it supports a rich array of bird species, particularly waders and waterfowl, making it a vital site for avian conservation.

Name: Clevedon Court

Name: Cley Marshes

Name: Cloatley Manor Farm Meadows

Name: Cloud Wood

Name: Clouds Hill

Name: Conwy

It's a place to connect with the natural world and discover the quiet beauty of the English countryside.

Name: Corehead & The Devil's Beef Tub
Description: Corehead, near Moffat, is a 600-hectare site in the Devil's Beef Tub, southern Scotland. Borders Forest Trust manages this land for native woodland restoration and peatland conservation, aiming to enhance biodiversity and ecological processes.

Name: Corfe Barrows Nature Park
Description: Corfe Barrows Nature Park comprises around nine natural areas, covering an area of 90 hectares, within the Borough of Poole that are being managed for the benefit of wildlife and people.  It was designated as a nature park in June 2016.

Name: Corfe Castle
Description: Corfe Castle is dramatically set within the Purbeck Hills on the Isle of Purbeck peninsula, offering expansive views of the surrounding landscape.

Name: Cornard Mere
Description: Cornard Mere is an 8.5-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Little Cornard in Suffolk.

Name: Cornmill Meadows Dragonfly Sanctuary
Description: Cornmill Meadows Dragonfly Sanctuary is a vital mosaic of wetland habitats within Lee Valley Regional Park. Over 20 species of dragonflies and damselflies thrive here. Boardwalks and trails provide access for wildlife observation, enhancing local biodiversity.

Name: Corrieshalloch Gorge National Nature Reserve
Description: Experience the majestic Corrieshalloch Gorge, a profound Highland ravine with the roaring Falls of Measach, revealing a landscape shaped by ancient glacial forces.

Name: Corrimony
Description: Corrimony is an RSPB reserve located seven miles west of Drumnadrochit, near Loch Ness. It features native woodland, open moorland, and a loch, providing habitat for species such as black grouse, red kites, and red deer. An 8.5-mile waymarked trail is available for visitors.

Name: Cors Caron NNR
Description: Cors Caron National Nature Reserve is a vast raised bog in Ceredigion, West Wales. This ancient landscape hosts diverse wildlife, offering accessible boardwalks and a viewing hide. The Afon Teifi river meanders through the reserve.

Name: Cors Crymlyn
Description: Cors Crymlyn (also known as Crymlyn Bog) is a National Nature Reserve, Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI), Special Area of Conservation (SAC), and Ramsar site, located near Swansea, South Wales. It is the largest lowland fen in Wales and one of the most important wetland sites in Europe, providing crucial habitat for various rare plants and invertebrates, including the fen raft spider.

Name: Cors Ddyga
Description: Cors Ddyga is an extensive low-lying wetland and working floodplain in Anglesey, Wales. Home to threatened wildlife like marsh harriers, bitterns, and otters. Restoration has created reedbeds, wet grassland, and fens, supporting a rich diversity of species.

Name: Cossington Meadows
Description: Cossington Meadows is an 88.9 hectares nature reserve west of Cossington in Leicestershire.

Name: Cotehele
Description: Nestled on the banks of the River Tamar, Cotehele offers rich riverine habitats and stunning waterside landscapes.

Name: Coton Country Park
Description: Coton Country Park, 120 hectares west of Cambridge, offers footpaths and cycle routes through diverse habitats. Managed by Cambridge PPF for public access and wildlife, it features meadows, woodland, and ponds. It connects directly to the Coton footpath to Grantchester.

Name: Coton Reserve
Description: Coton Reserve is a 35-hectare site near Coton village, west of Cambridge. Managed by CambridgePPF, it transforms former arable land into wildflower meadows, woodland, and wetlands. This project provides vital green space for wildlife and public access.

Name: Cotswold Water Park
Description: The Cotswold Lakes is the United Kingdom's largest marl lake system, straddling the Wiltshire–Gloucestershire border, north-west of Cricklade and south of Cirencester.  There are 180 lakes, spread over 42 square miles.

Name: Cottage Farm
Description: Cottage Farm, Ulster Wildlife's first nature reserve, is a hidden gem located near Omagh along the River Strule. This diverse site features ancient woodland, bog, species-rich grassland, hedgerows, and ponds. Formerly a dairy farm, it is undergoing restoration, including the removal of invasive scrub and non-native plants from the bog, to enhance its vital habitats. The reserve supports a wide array of wildlife, including various birds, butterflies, moths, damselflies, and mammals such as badger, otter, and red squirrel, and is used for education and research.

Name: Cotterill Clough Nature Reserve
Description: Cotterill Clough is a 5.6-hectare nature reserve near Manchester Airport.

Name: Cotton Dell
Description: Cotton Dell is a nature reserve of the Staffordshire Wildlife Trust.  It is a wooded valley area near the village of Cotton and about 0.

Name: Coulsdon Common
Description: Coulsdon Common, a 130-acre site in Coulsdon, features woodlands and open grasslands. Managed by the City of London Corporation, it provides habitats for diverse wildlife. Visitors enjoy walking and nature observation. It is a registered common.

Name: Coulsdon Common
Description: Coulsdon Common is a 126-acre public open space in south London, part of the City of London Commons and the South London Downs National Nature Reserve. It features ancient woodland, grassland, and chalk grassland, supporting diverse wildlife like roe deer and orchids. Managed for conservation and public access, it offers walking, cycling, and horse riding.

Name: Coulters Dean
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Coulters Dean is a 2.2-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south-east of Buriton in Hampshire.

Name: Cowden Pound Pastures
Description: Cowden Pound Pastures is a 5.9-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north of Cowden in Kent.

Name: Cowleaze Wood
Description: Discover a haven of ancient trees and vibrant wildlife in this South East England woodland. Wander through diverse habitats alive with birdsong and the rustle of unseen creatures, perfect for walking and cycling adventures. Immerse yourself in the natural beauty and experience the peaceful embrace of the forest.

Name: Craig Cerrig Gleisiad a Fan Frynych NNR
Description: Craig Cerrig Gleisiad a Fan Frynych NNR is a mosaic of habitats in the Brecon Beacons. It features an impressive glacial cwm with a lake, rocky outcrops, and moorland. The reserve supports arctic-alpine plants and various bird species.

Name: Craigellachie NNR
Description: Craigellachie NNR, near Aviemore, is an upland nature reserve in the Cairngorms National Park. It features ancient woodland, heather moorland, and a lochan. The reserve supports diverse wildlife, including peregrine falcons, ospreys, and red squirrels.

Name: Cranham Marsh
Description: Cranham Marsh is an English 15.3 hectare Local Nature Reserve and a Site of Metropolitan Importance for Nature Conservation in Cranham in the London Borough of Havering.

Name: Crathes Castle
Description: Crathes Castle features renowned walled gardens and extensive estate woodlands, supporting diverse plant life and wildlife.

Name: Credenhill Park Wood
Description: Credenhill Park Wood is an Iron Age hill fort in Herefordshire. Managed by the Woodland Trust, this site features ancient trees, diverse wildlife, and offers extensive views across the surrounding landscape near Hereford.

Name: Creech Wood
Description: This vast expanse of ancient woodland in the South East offers a haven for diverse wildlife, from chattering woodland birds to elusive deer that roam its dappled clearings. Visitors can immerse themselves in nature by exploring miles of winding trails perfect for walking and cycling, or simply soaking in the tranquil atmosphere and observing the natural world unfold. It's a place to reconnect with the beauty of the forest and its inhabitants.

Name: Cribb's Meadow
Description: Cribb's Meadow is a 4.2-hectare nature reserve east of Wymondham in Leicestershire.

Name: Cricklepit Mill
Description: Cricklepit Mill is a visitor centre of the Devon Wildlife Trust, located in Exeter, in Devon, England.  It is the headquarters of Devon Wildlife Trust, and one of two visitor centres of the Trust; the other is Wembury Marine Centre near Plymouth.

Name: Crimdon Dunes
Description: Crimdon Dunes is a significant dune system in County Durham, forming part of the Durham Coast Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and National Nature Reserve. It is known for its nationally and internationally important flora and fauna, including rare butterflies, orchids, and hosts the UK's most northerly breeding colony of little terns. The area is also notable for its unique geological features, being part of the Permian magnesian limestone system.

Name: Crinan Wood
Description: Crinan Wood is an ancient Atlantic oakwood on the banks of the Crinan Canal in Argyll and Bute, Scotland. It represents a prime example of this rare habitat, home to diverse flora, fauna, rare ferns, lichens, and mosses. The wood's unique ecosystem thrives in a mild, wet Atlantic-influenced climate.

Name: Croes Robert Wood
Description: Croes Robert Wood is a nature reserve and Site of Special Scientific Interest, noted for its biological characteristics, in Monmouthshire, south east Wales.  Gwent Wildlife Trust, the owners of the site, manage the woodland through methods of coppicing and charcoal burning to encourage its notable flora and fauna.

Name: Croft Castle
Description: Explore ancient woodlands, veteran trees, and diverse wildlife across the expansive parkland surrounding Croft Castle.

Name: Croft Pasture
Description: Croft Pasture is a 6.2-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest on the outskirts of Croft in Leicestershire.

Name: Cromers Wood
Description: Cromers Wood is a 28-hectare nature reserve between Milstead and Sittingbourne in Kent.  It is managed by Kent Wildlife Trust.

Name: Crook Hall, Durham
Description: Explore Crook Hall's renowned English country gardens, considered among the best in northern England, offering a tranquil natural escape.

Name: Crook Peak to Shute Shelve Hill
Description: A prominent ridge in the Mendip Hills with ancient woodlands, rare calcareous grasslands, and nationally significant species, including the unique Cheddar pink.

Name: Crooksbury Hill
Description: Crooksbury Hill is a 17.2-hectare nature reserve within Puttenham and Crooksbury Commons east of Farnham in Surrey.

Name: Croome Park
Description: Explore vast, scenic landscaped parkland, featuring sweeping open spaces and serene natural beauty.

Name: Cropton Forest
Description: This expansive woodland in Northern England offers a haven for nature lovers, with ancient trees forming a majestic canopy over winding trails perfect for walking and cycling. Discover a rich tapestry of wildlife, from chattering woodland birds to elusive deer, amidst the serene beauty of this Forestry England managed landscape. Immerse yourself in the tranquility and vibrant life that thrives within its leafy embrace.

Name: Crowsheath Wood
Description: Crowsheath Wood is an 8.1-hectare nature reserve in Downham, between Billericay and South Woodham Ferrers in Essex.

Name: Croxall Lakes
Description: Croxall Lakes is a nature reserve located between the villages of Croxall and Alrewas, Staffordshire, in the United Kingdom.  The nature reserve comprises two lakes and grassland between them.

Name: Croydon Hill
Description: This vibrant woodland in South East England offers a haven for diverse wildlife amidst ancient trees and rolling hills. Explore winding trails perfect for walking and cycling, immersing yourself in the sights and sounds of nature. Discover hidden glades, listen to birdsong, and feel the tranquility of this expansive natural space.

Name: Crymlyn Bog NNR
Description: Crymlyn Bog is one of the largest areas of lowland bog in the UK, supporting a variety of wildlife including otters and rare invertebrates. The site is a National Nature Reserve and a Ramsar site, featuring diverse habitats from open water to fen woodland.

Name: CS Lewis Nature Reserve
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: CS Lewis Nature Reserve is a 3-hectare nature reserve in Risinghurst, a suburb of Oxford in Oxfordshire.  It is managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Cucknell's Wood
Description: Cucknell's Wood is a 11-hectare nature reserve south-east of Shamley Green in Surrey.  It is managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Culloden Wood
Description: Culloden Wood offers walking routes through native woodland and plantations. Historically significant, it borders the famous Culloden battlefield and features ancient burial cairns. Visitors explore diverse flora and fauna here.

Name: Culpeper Community Garden
Description: Culpeper Community Garden is an award-winning Islington green space, offering individual plots and communal areas. It provides gardening opportunities for local people, run by volunteers. An oasis of peace, it is one of London's few successful community-managed open spaces.

Name: Culross
Description: Positioned on the Firth of Forth, the property offers views across this significant Scottish estuary.

Name: Culzean Castle
Description: The 240-acre Culzean Castle Country Park features dramatic clifftop views of the Firth of Clyde and includes a beautiful walled garden.

Name: Cumbernauld
Description: Cumbernauld is a town in North Lanarkshire, Scotland.  It lies within the historic county of Dunbartonshire.

Name: Cutsdean Quarry
Description: Cutsdean Quarry is a 0.83-hectare nature reserve in Gloucestershire, England.

Name: Cwm Du Glen
Description: Cwm Du Glen is a designated Local Nature Reserve near Pontardawe, Glamorgan, managed by Neath Port Talbot Council. It features a deep glen with a stream, waterfalls, ancient woodland, and diverse flora and fauna, supporting oak, ash, hazel, and various bird species. It is also known as Cwm Du Glen and Glanrhyd Plantation.

Name: Daisy Nook Country Park
Description: Daisy Nook Country Park is a 96-acre site in Oldham and Tameside, featuring woodlands, waterways, and a canal. It offers river and canal walks, fishing, a cafe, and children's play areas, serving as a popular destination for local recreation and nature activities.

Name: Dalby Forest
Description: Immerse yourself in this vast expanse of ancient woodland, where towering trees create a cathedral of green and dappled sunlight filters through the canopy. Explore a haven for diverse wildlife, from chattering birds to elusive deer, as you wander scenic walking trails or exhilarating cycle routes. This captivating natural playground offers a chance to connect with nature and discover its hidden beauty at your own pace.

Name: Dalston Eastern Curve Garden
Description: Dalston Eastern Curve Garden is a vibrant community green space in East London, built on a disused railway line. It provides a peaceful urban oasis for relaxation, hosts diverse community events, and supports educational activities, operating as a non-profit project.

Name: Dalton Crags Forest
Description: This extensive woodland in Northern England offers a haven for diverse wildlife amidst rolling hills and ancient trees. Explore winding paths that invite walkers and cyclists to immerse themselves in the tranquil beauty of the landscape, spotting native species and enjoying the fresh, invigorating air. It's a place to connect with nature and discover the wonders of the natural world at your own pace.

Name: Danbury Common
Description: Danbury Common is a 70.2-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Danbury in Essex, England.

Name: Danbury Common
Description: Danbury Common preserves one of Essex's largest heathland areas, featuring diverse woodlands, boggy habitats, rare flora, and a vital site for the rosy marbled moth.

Name: Danbury Ridge
Description: Danbury Ridge Nature Reserves are a group of nature reserves totalling 101 hectares near Danbury in Essex, England.  They are managed by the Essex Wildlife Trust, and most of them are in Sites of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Dancersend with Pavis Woods
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Dancersend is an 81.3-hectare Site of Special Scientific Interest south of Aston Clinton in Buckinghamshire.

Name: Danemead
Description: Danemead is a 5.6-hectare nature reserve west of Hoddesdon in Hertfordshire, managed by the Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust.

Name: Danes Moss Nature Reserve
Description: Danes Moss Nature Reserve is a 13.4-hectare nature reserve south of Macclesfield, Cheshire, England.

Name: Daneway Banks SSSI
Description: Daneway Banks is a 17-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Gloucestershire, notified in 1954 and renotified in 1983.  It lies half a mile west of Sapperton and is part of a group of wildlife sites in the Frome Valley that includes Siccaridge Wood and Sapperton Canal reserves.

Name: Dapdune Wharf
Description: Explore the tranquil waters and banks of the Wey and Godalming Navigations from this convenient riverside location.

Name: Darkhill Ironworks
Description: This ancient woodland in the South East of England is a haven for diverse wildlife, with dappled sunlight filtering through a canopy of mature trees, creating a truly enchanting atmosphere. Wander along winding paths, keeping an eye out for elusive deer and a symphony of birdsong, or explore on two wheels, immersing yourself in the tranquil beauty of nature. It's a place to reconnect with the natural world, offering peaceful walks and invigorating cycling routes through a landscape rich in history and biodiversity.

Name: Darland Banks
Description: Darland Banks is a 29.1-hectare Local Nature Reserve on the southern outskirts of Gillingham in Kent.

Name: Darsham Marshes
Description: Darsham Marshes is a 20 hectare nature reserve south of Darsham in Suffolk, England.  It is owned and managed by the Suffolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Davidstow Woods
Description: Immerse yourself in a vibrant tapestry of ancient trees and dappled sunlight, where a wealth of wildlife thrives amidst rolling hills. This expansive woodland offers enchanting trails perfect for leisurely walks and invigorating cycles, inviting you to discover its hidden glades and listen to the symphony of nature. Explore the diverse habitats, from moss-laden branches to sun-drenched clearings, and experience the tranquility of this South West gem.

Name: Dawcombe
Description: Dawcombe is a 23-hectare nature reserve north-west of Reigate in Surrey.  It is managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Dawlish Warren & Exe Estuary
Description: Dawlish Warren is a sand spit and nature reserve at the River Exe mouth in Devon. The Exe Estuary is a vital wetland ecosystem, supporting overwintering birds and diverse habitats. Both sites hold designations as SSSI and NNR.

Name: Dawlish Water
Description: This enchanting woodland in South West England offers a tranquil escape into nature's embrace. Wander along winding paths beneath a canopy of trees, where sunlight dapples the forest floor and the gentle sounds of birdsong fill the air. It's a haven for wildlife, with opportunities to spot deer, various bird species, and a rich tapestry of plant life, making it a perfect destination for walkers and nature enthusiasts seeking a peaceful connection with the natural world.

Name: Daws Hall
Description: Daws Hall is a tranquil nature reserve and education centre near Lamarsh, Essex, managed by the Daws Hall Trust. It features diverse habitats including meadows, woodlands, and a stretch of the River Stour, supporting a variety of wildlife.

Name: Decoy Heath
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Decoy Pit, Pools and Woods is a 17.7-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south of Aldermaston in Berkshire.

Name: Dedham Vale & Stour Valley National Landscape - Haverhill Headwaters
Description: Dedham Vale and Stour Valley National Landscape, on the Essex-Suffolk border, features low-lying landscapes. The Haverhill Headwaters mark the Stour River's source, flowing through ancient woodlands, meadows, and arable land, supporting diverse habitats and species within this protected area.

Name: Deepdene Terrace
Description: Deepdene Terrace is a historical landscape and nature reserve in Dorking, Surrey. Owned by Mole Valley District Council, it features ornamental gardens, woodland, and an arboretum. Conservation and maintenance are carried out by the Friends of Deepdene, offering visitors a tranquil space for walks and nature observation.

Name: Deeping Lakes Nature Reserve
Description: Deeping Lakes Nature Reserve, also known as Deeping Gravel Pits is a local nature reserve with an area of over 160 acres located south-east of Deeping St James in Lincolnshire, England.  It includes part of the Deeping Gravel Pits SSSI and is placed within a Higher Level Stewardship scheme.

Name: Deer's Leap Wood
HostOrg: Birmingham and Black Country Wildlife Trust
Description: Deer's Leap Wood is a nature reserve of the Wildlife Trust for Birmingham and the Black Country, in West Midlands, England.  There is woodland with a variety of tree species; also a pond and a meadow area.

Name: Deerpark
Description: This expansive woodland in South West England offers a haven for diverse wildlife, from soaring birds of prey to shy woodland mammals. Visitors can explore winding trails through ancient trees, perfect for immersive walks and invigorating cycles, all while soaking in the vibrant sights and sounds of nature. It's a place to reconnect with the wild, breathe in fresh air, and discover the beauty of a thriving forest ecosystem.

Name: Delamere Forest
Description: This vast expanse of ancient woodland offers a haven of natural beauty, where diverse wildlife thrives amongst towering trees and winding trails. Visitors can immerse themselves in the peaceful surroundings, enjoying invigorating walks or cycling adventures through the dappled sunlight. It's a place to reconnect with nature and discover the wonders of the forest ecosystem.

Name: Denaby Ings
Description: Denaby Ings are a nature reserve on the River Dearne, encompassing an area of 23 hectares north of Denaby Main, Doncaster, South Yorkshire, near the town of Mexborough.  The Trans Pennine Trail passes here.

Name: Denham Lock Wood
Description: Denham Lock Wood is a 6.3-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest next to the Grand Union Canal, and near Denham in the London Borough of Hillingdon.

Name: Denham Wood
Description: This ancient woodland in South West England offers a haven of natural beauty, alive with the rustling of leaves and the songs of diverse birdlife. Wander along winding paths, breathe in the fresh, earthy air, and keep an eye out for shy woodland creatures. It's a perfect place to explore on foot or by bike, immersing yourself in the peaceful embrace of nature.

Name: Deptford Creek
Description: The Creekside Discovery Centre in Deptford manages a 0.5-hectare natural habitat and the intertidal area of Deptford Creek, a unique urban ecosystem and one of London's most biodiverse landscapes. It provides environmental education, guided walks, and programmes for schools and community groups, fostering connection with its rich freshwater and saltwater flora and fauna.

Name: Dering Wood
Description: Dering Wood is an ancient semi-natural woodland near Pluckley, Kent, covering approximately 125-147 hectares (308-310 acres). Managed by the Woodland Trust, it features diverse tree species like sessile oak, hornbeam, and sweet chestnut, supporting a variety of wildlife including nightingales, dormice, and notable butterfly species. The site is actively managed for conservation and public access, preserving its ecological and historic value.

Name: Derwent Gorge and Horsleyhope Ravine
Description: Derwent Gorge and Horsleyhope Ravine is a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and part of the Derwent Gorge and Muggleswick Woods National Nature Reserve (NNR). It comprises ancient semi-natural woodlands along the River Derwent and its tributary, Horsleyhope Burn, near Consett. The site features steep-sided ravines and diverse flora, including dry acid sessile oak woods and lime-rich ash and wet alder woodlands, supporting rare plants and protected species. It is a vital area for wildlife conservation in County Durham and Northumberland.

Name: Derwent Island House
Description: Discover the unique landscape of Derwent Island, a scenic seven-acre island nestled within the stunning waters of Derwent Water, Cumbria.

Name: Devil's Dyke, Sussex
Description: This dramatic V-shaped dry valley on the South Downs is a Site of Special Scientific Interest, offering spectacular views and walks.

Name: Dews Farm Sand Pits
Description: Dews Farm Sand Pits is a 1.2-hectare nature reserve near Harefield in the London Borough of Hillingdon.

Name: Dick Buck's Burrows
Description: Dick Buck's Burrows is a mature broadleaved woodland, dominated by oak, sweet chestnut, sycamore and beech, located two miles southwest of Cromer in Norfolk. The site features a waymarked path linking to the Weavers Way and offers public access. Managed by the Woodland Trust.

Name: Dickleburgh Moor
Description: Dickleburgh Moor is a fen habitat in Norfolk. It supports diverse flora including marsh orchids, bog pimpernel, and sundew. Management includes scrub clearance and water level control to maintain the wetland environment.

Name: Dimmingsdale
Description: Venture into a haven of ancient oaks and whispering pines, where dappled sunlight filters through a canopy teeming with life. This expansive woodland offers a sanctuary for diverse wildlife, inviting walkers and cyclists to explore its winding trails. Immerse yourself in the tranquility of nature, discovering hidden glades and the vibrant pulse of the forest.

Name: Dimminsdale
Description: Dimminsdale is a 37 hectare geological and biological Site of Special Scientific Interest partly in Derbyshire and partly in Leicestershire.  It is located east of Calke in Derbyshire.

Name: Dingle Marshes
Description: Dingle Marshes is a 93-hectare wildlife reserve on the North Sea coast of the English county of Suffolk.  The reserve is located between Dunwich and Walberswick, approximately 4 miles south-west of Southwold.

Name: Dinnington Community Woodland
Description: Dinnington Community Woodland is a popular local park in Rotherham. TCV South Yorkshire manages the site for nature conservation and community benefit. It offers valuable green space for the local community and supports diverse wildlife habitats.

Name: Dinton, Wiltshire
Description: Nestled in the scenic Nadder valley, Dinton offers characteristic Wiltshire countryside, providing varied natural habitats for wildlife.

Name: Distillery Farm Meadows
Description: Distillery Farm Meadows is an 18.7 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Wiltshire, notified in 1988.

Name: Ditchling Beacon
Description: Ditchling Beacon is the highest point in East Sussex, England, with an elevation of 248 m.  It is south of Ditchling and to the north-east of Brighton.

Name: Dodd Wood
Description: This vibrant Forestry England woodland in North England is a haven for nature lovers. Explore winding paths through ancient trees, where you might spot elusive red squirrels or listen to the songs of diverse birdlife. It's the perfect place to immerse yourself in the natural world, whether you're enjoying a leisurely walk or a more adventurous cycle.

Name: Doe Lea
Description: Doe Lea Local Nature Reserve, 14 hectares of grassland and woodland, offers accessible paths, a circular walk, benches, and a bird hide. Once an opencast coal mine, the site supports significant biodiversity, recording over 30 bird species. Weekly volunteer tasks maintain the area.

Name: Dolebury Warren
Description: Dolebury Warren is a 90.6-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest and ancient monument near the villages of Churchill and Rowberrow in North Somerset, part of South West England.

Name: Dolebury Warren
Description: This SSSI on a Mendip Hills limestone ridge supports an unusually wide range of plants, insects, and butterflies.

Name: Dollar Glen
Description: A dramatic glen within the Ochils, highlighting the striking landscape along the Highland fault.

Name: Dollis Brook
Description: Thames21 and partners restore Dollis Brook, a North London tributary of the River Brent. The project enhances natural river features, creates habitats, and reduces flood risk with sustainable drainage systems. Community engagement is key.

Name: Donna Nook National Nature Reserve
Description: Donna Nook is a point on the low-lying coast of north Lincolnshire, England, north of the village of North Somercotes and south of Grimsby.  The area, a salt marsh, is used by a number of Royal Air Force stations in Lincolnshire for bombing practice and shares its name with RAF Donna Nook.

Name: Dowdeswell Reservoir
Description: Dowdeswell Reservoir is in the parish of Dowdeswell in Gloucestershire.  The former water treatment works are in the parish of Charlton Kings.

Name: Downe Bank
Description: Downe Bank is a nature reserve owned and managed by the Kent Wildlife Trust in the North Downs, close to Downe in the London Borough of Bromley.  It is a Site of Special Scientific Interest together with the neighbouring High Elms Country Park.

Name: Downs Banks
Description: Downs Banks features open countryside, offering expansive views across the Staffordshire landscape.

Name: Doxey Marshes
Description: Doxey Marshes is a 150 hectares nature reserve located within two miles of Stafford town centre, and is managed by Staffordshire Wildlife Trust.  Designated as a Site of Special Scientific Interest for its wet grassland habitat and its breeding wading birds and wildfowl, it is particularly noted for its populations of breeding snipe.

Name: Draycott Sleights
Description: Draycott Sleights is a 61.95 hectares biological Site of Special Scientific Interest at Draycott in the Mendip Hills, Somerset, England, notified in 1987.

Name: Drinkwater Park
Description: Explore a vibrant woodland alive with the sights and sounds of nature, where ancient trees create a dappled canopy overhead. Wander winding trails and cycle through picturesque landscapes, keeping an eye out for diverse wildlife that calls this Northern England haven home. Discover a place to connect with the natural world, offering peaceful walks and invigorating adventures amidst its beauty.

Name: Droitwich Canals Reedbed Restoration
Description: The Droitwich Canals, restored in 2010, connect the Worcester & Birmingham Canal with the River Severn. A vital wildlife corridor, it supports otters, kingfishers, and dragonflies. Ongoing conservation efforts, particularly at the 5.5-hectare Coney Meadow reedbed nature reserve, maintain and enhance its crucial reedbed and wetland habitats.

Name: Drumnaph Wood
HostOrg: Woodland Trust and Carntogher Community Association
Description: Drumnaph Wood is a significant ancient native woodland, forming part of the larger Drumnaph Community Nature Reserve near Maghera, County Londonderry. Situated at the gateway to the Sperrin Hills, it features diverse habitats including ancient woodland, newly planted woodland, wildflower meadows, wetlands, and bog. The reserve supports a rich variety of flora and fauna, including diverse tree species, ground flora, and various bird and mammal populations, and is known for its bluebells in spring and butterflies in summer.

Name: Dry Sandford Pit
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Dry Sandford Pit is a 4.2-hectare biological and geological Site of Special Scientific Interest north-west of Abingdon-on-Thames in Oxfordshire.

Name: Dryhill
Description: Dryhill Local Nature Reserve, near Sundridge in Kent, is a former ragstone quarry now reclaimed by nature. It is a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and the first geological Local Nature Reserve in Kent, known for its exceptional rock formations and fossils. The reserve features acidic grassland and heathland, supporting rare plants, invertebrates, and reptiles, with sheep grazing helping to maintain these habitats. Elevated, it offers panoramic views.

Name: Duck Gutter
Description: Duck Gutter Nature Reserve in South Yorkshire is a wet grassland and fen habitat. It supports diverse plants such as water violets and marsh orchids, and breeding wading birds like snipe and redshank. The reserve features open water, ditches, and reedbeds, managed to maintain its wetland ecosystem.

Name: Dudley No. 2 Canal Windmill End
Description: The Dudley No. 2 Canal, managed by the Canal & River Trust, is part of the Birmingham Canal Navigations. At Windmill End, it meets the Netherton Tunnel Branch Canal and is adjacent to Bumble Hole Nature Reserve. This area is a tranquil haven with grassland, ponds, wildflowers, and birds, offering opportunities for walking, cycling, and wildlife spotting. It also features historic industrial remnants like Cobbs Engine House.

Name: Dudmaston Hall
Description: Explore the natural beauty and diverse habitats found within the scenic Severn Valley landscape.

Name: Dulwich Upper Wood
Description: Dulwich Upper Wood is a Local Nature Reserve in South London, one of four remnants of the Great North Wood. Managed by TCV, it features ancient woodland with oak, hornbeam, and ash, supporting diverse wildlife. The site offers a tranquil escape, promoting biodiversity.

Name: Duncliffe Wood
Description: Duncliffe Wood is an ancient woodland spanning over 92 hectares near Shaftesbury, Dorset. It offers diverse broadleaf habitats and open glades on a prominent hilltop. Managed by the Woodland Trust, the site provides marked trails for visitors to explore, supporting local wildlife populations and offering panoramic views.

Name: Dundreggan Rewilding Centre
Description: Dundreggan Rewilding Centre, near Loch Ness, offers an immersive experience into rewilding. It features a tree nursery and accessible trail, showcasing efforts to restore Scotland's wild forest and biodiversity. The centre opened in 2023.

Name: Dunham Massey Hall
Description: Dunham Massey features expansive formal gardens and a beautiful ancient deer park, home to a thriving herd of fallow deer.

Name: Dunkeld
Description: Dunkeld is the scenic gateway to the Highlands, nestled on the River Tay, and includes the beautiful countryside of The Hermitage.

Name: Dunmore Pineapple
Description: This Stirlingshire site features mature woodlands, orchards, and extensive parkland, providing habitats for diverse wildlife.

Name: Dunnet Head
Description: Dunnet Head is mainland Great Britain's most northerly point, offering panoramic coastal views. Its cliffs and heathland host puffins, guillemots, razorbills, and kittiwakes. Marine wildlife like seals and dolphins are often seen. It is a vital seabird breeding ground.

Name: Dunollie Wood
Description: Dunollie Wood is an ancient woodland situated on a hillside overlooking Oban Bay, offering views towards Mull and Lismore. This small, historically significant site features mature oak trees and diverse ground flora including bluebells. The Woodland Trust manages it for conservation and public access.

Name: Dunsdon National Nature Reserve
Description: Dunsdon National Nature Reserve is a nature reserve of the Devon Wildlife Trust, near Dunsdon and about 3.5 miles north-west of Holsworthy, in Devon, England.

Name: Dunstable Downs
Description: A dramatic chalk escarpment and the highest point in Bedfordshire, Dunstable Downs offers panoramic views across the Chiltern Hills.

Name: Dunstanburgh Castle
Description: Perched dramatically on the Northumberland coast, this striking location offers rugged coastal scenery and habitats for diverse marine and bird life.

Name: Dunster Working Watermill
Description: Set along the scenic River Avill, the watermill's location supports valuable riparian habitats and riverside wildlife.

Name: Dunwich Forest
Description: Dunwich Forest is an area of forest and lowland heath around 1 mile north-west of the village of Dunwich in the English county of Suffolk.  The forest covers an area of approximately 9 square kilometres and was originally planted by the Forestry Commission.

Name: Dunwich Forest
Description: This expansive woodland in South East England offers a haven for diverse wildlife, from soaring birds of prey to elusive woodland mammals. Explore miles of winding trails perfect for invigorating walks and cycling adventures, immersing yourself in the sights and sounds of a flourishing natural landscape. Discover ancient trees, peaceful glades, and the vibrant tapestry of life that thrives within this cherished forest.

Name: Dunwich Heath
Description: Dunwich Heath is a rare coastal lowland heath boasting vibrant heather and gorse, providing a vital habitat for deer, rare birds, reptiles, and unique invertebrates.

Name: Dutton Park Farm Nature Reserve
Description: Dutton Park Farm Nature Reserve is an 18-hectare nature reserve northwest of Weaverham, Cheshire, England.  It is managed by the Cheshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Dyfi Osprey Project
Description: The Dyfi Osprey Project is a conservation project at the Cors Dyfi nature reserve near Derwenlas, in the county of Powys, Wales, under the management of the Montgomeryshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Dyfi: Ynyslas NNR
Description: Ynyslas National Nature Reserve, within the Dyfi Biosphere, features a diverse landscape of dunes, saltmarsh, peatland, and estuary. The Nature Hub serves as a visitor centre, providing information, refreshments, and essential facilities for exploring this significant natural area.

Name: Dymock Forest
Description: This expansive woodland offers a vibrant tapestry of ancient trees and diverse habitats, alive with the calls of birds and the rustle of unseen creatures. Visitors can immerse themselves in nature by exploring winding paths, perfect for invigorating walks or cycling adventures, and discover the rich biodiversity that thrives within its leafy embrace. It's a place to connect with the wild, breathe in the fresh air, and witness the enduring beauty of the natural world.

Name: Dymock Woods SSSI
Description: Dymock Woods is a 53-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Gloucestershire, notified in 1990.  The site is listed in the 'Forest of Dean Local Plan Review' as a Key Wildlife Site.

Name: Dyrham Park
Description: Explore Dyrham Park's ancient deer park and extensive grounds, home to a herd of fallow deer and beautiful water features amidst its formal gardens.

Name: Eaglehead and Bloodstone Copses
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Eaglehead and Bloodstone Copses is a 10.3-hectare Site of Special Scientific Interest which is south of Ashey on the Isle of Wight.

Name: Eames Farm Thorney Island Wetland
Description: Eames Farm is a 132.5-hectare Local Nature Reserve on Thorney Island within Chichester Harbour National Landscape (AONB). It is owned by Chichester Harbour Conservancy, West Sussex County Council, and the Ministry of Defence, and managed by Chichester Harbour Conservancy. It protects saltmarsh, mudflats, reedbeds, and grazing marsh, forming an internationally important wetland and organic farm. The site supports diverse bird species, rare plants like Grass-poly, and insects. It is part of the Chichester and Langstone Harbours Ramsar site and Special Protection Area. The site is private land with no public access, though public footpaths exist around Thorney Island.

Name: East Blean Wood
Description: East Blean Woods is a 151.4-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south of Herne Bay in Kent.

Name: East Ham Nature Reserve
Description: East Ham Nature Reserve is a former graveyard transformed into a Local Nature Reserve in the London Borough of Newham. Newham Green Gym volunteers maintain diverse habitats, including woodland, wildflower meadows, and ponds, supporting local wildlife.

Name: East Harptree
Description: This expansive woodland offers a tranquil escape into nature, where ancient trees create a dappled canopy alive with the sounds of birdsong. Wander winding paths beneath the emerald green, keeping an eye out for deer and other woodland creatures that call this beautiful place home. It's an ideal setting for a refreshing walk or a peaceful cycle, immersing yourself in the sights and scents of the forest.

Name: East Riddlesden Hall
Description: Discover a rich mosaic of ancient woodlands, wildlife-rich ponds, and vibrant gardens, providing vital habitats for diverse birds, amphibians, and insects.

Name: East Sheen Common
Description: East Sheen Common offers woodlands, open common land, and a nature trail, providing a green escape adjacent to Richmond Park.

Name: East Town Park
Description: East Town Park in Haverhill spans 50 acres of meadows and woodlands, featuring diverse wildlife habitats, nature trails, and conservation areas. It holds Green Flag status and offers an easy access trail, a five-kilometre railway walk, and osier beds. Visitors can observe various wildlife, including snowdrops, yellow aconites, lizards, damselflies, frogs, toads, butterflies, and dragonflies. The park also includes a children's play area, skate park, cafe, and WCs.

Name: East Village Waterglades
Description: East Village Waterglades in Stratford, London, is a vital green space within a residential area. TCV volunteers manage these wetland habitats, ensuring they remain biodiverse and accessible. The site supports various plant species and provides a home for diverse urban wildlife.

Name: East Winch Common
Description: East Winch Common is a 26.1-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south-east of King's Lynn in Norfolk, England.

Name: East Wood, Tidenham
Description: East Wood and is a 0.82-hectare nature reserve in Gloucestershire, England.

Name: East Wretham Heath
Description: East Wretham Heath is a 141.1-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south-east of Thetford in Norfolk, England.

Name: Eastbrookend Country Park
HostOrg: London Borough of Barking and Dagenham
Description: Eastbrookend Country Park in Dagenham spans 76.1 hectares (188 acres). It is a Local Nature Reserve and a Site of Metropolitan Importance for Nature Conservation, featuring diverse habitats including open grassland, woodlands, marsh, and lakes, supporting a wide variety of wildlife. The park offers walking trails, a café, and a children's play area, and connects to The Chase Nature Reserve.

Name: Eastridge Woods
Description: This extensive woodland offers a haven of mature trees and diverse habitats, where ancient oaks stand tall alongside vibrant new growth. Keep an eye out for elusive woodland birds and a tapestry of insects, as well as the chance to explore winding paths perfect for walking and cycling adventures amidst nature's embrace.

Name: Eastwood Nature Reserve
Description: Eastwood Nature Reserve is a 4.7-hectare nature reserve in Stalybridge, Tameside, England.

Name: Ebbor Gorge
Description: Ebbor Gorge is a dry limestone gorge and National Nature Reserve within the Mendip Hills National Landscape. Managed by Natural England, it features ancient woodland, walking trails, and diverse wildlife. The site is noted for its geological formations and prehistoric archaeological interest.

Name: Ebbor Gorge
Description: Ebbor Gorge is a limestone gorge and national nature reserve, home to diverse flora, butterflies, and bats within the Mendip Hills.

Name: Ebernoe Common
Description: Ebernoe Common is a 233.9-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Ebernoe, north of Petworth in West Sussex.

Name: Eday
Description: Eday is one of the larger North Isles of Orkney, a low-lying island with a rich natural and historical heritage. The RSPB reserve covers the north-west part of the island, including the cliffs of Red Head, a nationally important seabird colony.

Name: Eddleston Water Project
Description: The Eddleston Water Project is a long-term initiative restoring the river's natural function, mitigating flood risk, and enhancing biodiversity in the Eddleston catchment. It uses nature-based solutions like tree planting, pond creation, and meander restoration to tackle climate change impacts.

Name: Edgbaston Reservoir
Description: Edgbaston Reservoir is a large urban water body in Birmingham, West Midlands. Managed by the Canal & River Trust, it serves as a vital canal feeder and a significant habitat for diverse wildlife. The reservoir provides a green oasis and recreational space within the city.

Name: Edgehills Bog
Description: Edgehills Bog is a 0.66-hectare nature reserve in Gloucestershire in the Forest of Dean.

Name: Edmondsley Wood
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 13 hectares.

Name: Eggardon Hill
Description: Experience panoramic views from Eggardon Hill's distinctive chalk uplands, home to unique wildflowers and diverse wildlife.

Name: Eggerslack Woods
Description: Explore a vibrant tapestry of ancient woodland and rolling hills in this expansive Northern English forest. Discover a haven for diverse wildlife, from elusive deer to a symphony of birdsong, as you wander through peaceful walking trails and exhilarating cycling routes. Immerse yourself in the beauty of nature, breathing in the fresh air and experiencing the tranquility of this stunning landscape.

Name: Elan Valley
Description: The Elan Valley in Mid Wales is a key site for the Celtic Rainforests LIFE project. Dŵr Cymru Welsh Water manages this estate, leading efforts to restore precious Atlantic woodlands. The area offers opportunities for both volunteering and fundraising.

Name: Elland Gravel Pits
Description: Elland Gravel Pits is a Yorkshire Wildlife Trust nature reserve. This former quarry site is now a haven for wildlife, featuring open water, reedbeds, scrub, and woodland. It supports various bird species, dragonflies, and amphibians.

Name: Elstead Group of Commons
Description: Elstead Group of Commons is a 180-hectare nature reserve east of Elstead in Surrey.  It is composed of Royal, Elstead and Ockley Commons, which are owned by the Ministry of Defence and managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust, and Bagmoor Common, which is owned and managed by the Trust.

Name: Elvaston Castle Country Park
Description: Elvaston Castle Country Park is home to Elvaston Castle, a gothic revival masterpiece (not open to the public) set within approximately 321 acres of parkland and formal gardens. Opened in 1970, it was England's first country park, offering nature trails, a children's play area, and hosting various events. It is managed by Derbyshire County Council.

Name: Emer Bog and Baddesley Common
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Emer Bog and Baddesley Common is a 50-hectare nature reserve north of North Baddesley in Hampshire.  It is managed by the Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust.

Name: Emmett Hill Meadows
Description: Emmett Hill Meadows is a 5.1 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Wiltshire, notified in 1987.

Name: Emmetts Garden
Description: Explore this Edwardian garden, renowned for its exotic trees, shrubberies, and vibrant seasonal displays.

Name: Ennerdale
Description: This vast expanse of ancient woodland in Cumbria offers a haven for diverse wildlife, from soaring birds of prey to elusive red squirrels, all thriving amidst stunning natural beauty. Explore miles of trails winding through majestic trees and alongside the tranquil waters of the lake, perfect for invigorating walks and cycling adventures. Immerse yourself in the sights and sounds of nature, discovering hidden glades and panoramic vistas.

Name: Epping Forest
Description: Epping Forest is London's largest open space, stretching 12 miles from East London to Epping in Essex. It is a unique remnant of an ancient forest, a Site of Special Scientific Interest, and a Special Area of Conservation, containing over 50,000 ancient trees.

Name: Eridge Rocks
Description: Eridge Green is a 8.4-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north-east of Crowborough in East Sussex.

Name: Esher Common
Description: Esher Common is a large open common in Surrey, featuring diverse habitats including extensive heathland, ancient woodland, and acid grassland. Ponds and wet areas support varied birdlife, reptiles, and butterflies. The site is managed for conservation and public enjoyment.

Name: Etherow Country Park
Description: Etherow Country Park, one of England's first country parks, sits on the Peak District's edge. Established in 1968, it features extensive open woodland, two reservoirs, and the River Etherow. Visitors can enjoy fishing, sailing, and a children's play area.

Name: Everdon Stubbs
Description: Everdon Stubbs is an ancient woodland, known for its extensive bluebell displays in spring. The reserve features diverse mature trees and ground flora. It supports a variety of woodland birds and invertebrates.

Name: Eyebrook Reservoir SSSI
Description: Eyebrook Reservoir is a critical site for wildlife, particularly waterbirds. Designated as a Site of Special Scientific Scientific Interest (SSSI), it supports significant populations of wildfowl and waders throughout the year. The reservoir is owned by Tata Steel UK and primarily operates as a trout fishery, with public viewing available from footpaths along its perimeter.

Name: Fackenden Down
Description: Fackenden Down is a 14-hectare nature reserve north of Sevenoaks in Kent.  It is managed by the Kent Wildlife Trust.

Name: Fair Isle
Description: Fair Isle, the UK's most remote inhabited island, is internationally renowned for its wild bird observatory and rich marine environment.

Name: Fairburn Ings
Description: Fairburn Ings, a former opencast coal mine near Castleford, West Yorkshire, is now a thriving wetland habitat. It attracts diverse birdlife, including avocets and kingfishers. The reserve features visitor trails, hides, and an accessible visitor centre for year-round nature observation.

Name: Fairlands Valley Park
Description: Fairlands Valley Park in Stevenage, Hertfordshire, is a large recreational area featuring lakes for watersports and fishing. The park includes a splash park, adventure play areas, walking routes, and a cafe, providing diverse activities for visitors. It serves as a vital green space for both leisure and local wildlife.

Name: Fairmile Common
Description: Fairmile Common is a diverse mosaic of acid grassland, heathland, woodland, and scrub in Surrey. It provides habitats for ground-nesting birds, invertebrates, and reptiles. Managed by Surrey Wildlife Trust, it is part of a larger network of interconnected wildlife sites.

Name: Falls of Clyde (Scotland)
Description: The Falls of Clyde are a series of linns or waterfalls on the River Clyde, near Lanark, Scotland.  They are renowned for their beauty and have frequently been painted by artists.

Name: Falls of Glomach
Description: The remote Falls of Glomach plunge 113m through wild Highland countryside, making it one of Britain's tallest and most spectacular waterfalls.

Name: Fames Rough
Description: Fames Rough is a 23-hectare nature reserve south-west of Chipstead in Surrey.  It is managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust and is part of the Chipstead Downs Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Far Ings National Nature Reserve
Description: Far Ings national nature reserve is an area of over 90 ha on the southern shore of the Humber Estuary in North Lincolnshire, England.  It is immediately west of the town of Barton-upon-Humber and the village of Barton Waterside.

Name: Farlington Marshes
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Farlington Marshes is a 119.7-hectare Local Nature Reserve near Portsmouth in Hampshire.

Name: Farnborough Hall
Description: Explore ancient woodlands, expansive parkland, and a tranquil lake, enjoying sweeping views over the rolling Warwickshire countryside.

Name: Farncombe Wood
Description: Farncombe Wood is a 1-hectare nature reserve in Farncombe in Surrey.  It is owned and managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Farne Islands
Description: A dynamic archipelago off the Northumberland coast, these islands are a vital haven for thousands of seabirds and grey seals.

Name: Farningham Wood
HostOrg: Sevenoaks District Council and Farningham Parish Council
Description: Farningham Wood is a 68-hectare (168-acre) ancient woodland and biological Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) in Kent, jointly owned and managed by Sevenoaks District Council and Farningham Parish Council. Designated as a Local Nature Reserve in 1987, it features diverse tree species, including oak, ash, and hornbeam, and is home to rare plants such as the Small-Leaved Lime and the nationally rare Deptford Pink. Public footpaths allow access for walking and nature observation, with a car park located at the end of Calfstock Lane.

Name: Farthing Downs
Description: Farthing Downs, a chalk grassland and ancient woodland site, stretches 3km across Greater London and Surrey. Popular for walking and horse riding, it offers views across the North Downs and is a Site of Special Scientific Interest for its rare chalk grassland plants.

Name: Fedian
Description: Fedian is a 12.5-hectare nature reserve in County Fermanagh, Northern Ireland. It features species-rich wet grassland and rush pasture, with an area of deciduous woodland. The site supports notable birdlife and various wildflowers, including several orchid species.

Name: Felbrigg Hall
Description: Felbrigg Hall boasts diverse grounds featuring Felbrigg Woods, a significant Site of Special Scientific Interest, plus walled gardens, an orangery, and orchards.

Name: Fell Foot Park
Description: Enjoy stunning lakeside views and open parkland at the southern end of Windermere, England's largest lake.

Name: Fen Drayton Lakes
Description: Fen Drayton Lakes is an RSPB nature reserve in Cambridgeshire, a network of lakes, meadows, and wetlands within the Great Ouse valley. Formerly a sand and gravel quarry, it is now an important habitat for a huge variety of wildlife, including overwintering wildfowl, wading birds, otters, dragonflies, and common terns. Reedbeds support warblers and bearded tits.

Name: Fens Pools Nature Reserve
Description: Fens Pools Nature Reserve, part of the larger Buckpool and Fens Pool Local Nature Reserve, is a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) in the West Midlands. It comprises three main pools (Grove, Middle, and Fens Pool) originally constructed by the Stourbridge Canal Company as reservoirs. The reserve is renowned for its diverse habitats, including open water, swamps, fens, and grasslands, supporting a significant population of great crested newts, amphibians, and various bird and insect species. It is situated between Pensnett and Brierley Hill.

Name: Fenton House
Description: Fenton House boasts a large walled garden in London, featuring a sunken garden, orchard, and productive kitchen garden.

Name: Fermyn Woods
Description: This ancient woodland in South East England offers a haven for wildlife, with ancient oak and ash trees forming a rich canopy. Explore winding trails through dappled sunlight, listening for the songs of woodland birds and searching for elusive deer. It's a perfect place to reconnect with nature, offering tranquil walks and cycling routes amidst a thriving natural environment.

Name: Fermyn Woods Country Park
Description: Fermyn Woods Country Park is a Green Flag award-winning park in Northamptonshire, near Brigstock. It features woodland and meadows, walking trails, cycling routes, a play area, and a cafe. Managed by Fermyn Wood Trust and North Northamptonshire Council.

Name: Fernworthy Forest
Description: Wander through ancient oaks and vibrant coniferous trees, where sunlight dapples the forest floor and the air hums with life. Explore winding trails perfect for walking or cycling, encountering a diverse array of wildlife from soaring birds to elusive mammals. This extensive woodland offers a tranquil escape into the heart of nature.

Name: Figsbury Ring
Description: Figsbury Ring is an important biological Site of Special Scientific Interest, home to diverse wildlife and habitats.

Name: Filsham Reedbed
Description: Filsham Reedbed is an 18.5-hectare Local Nature Reserve on the western outskirts of St Leonards-on-Sea in East Sussex.

Name: Findhorn Hinterland
Description: Findhorn Hinterland Trust manages land, woods, dunes, and wetlands near Findhorn, Moray, Scotland. It restores biodiversity and connects people with nature through education and land-based skills. The Trust promotes conservation and community engagement within the local environment.

Name: Finemere Wood
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Finemere Wood is a 45.7-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest near Quainton in Buckinghamshire.

Name: Fineshade Wood
Description: This expansive woodland offers a haven for diverse wildlife, from ancient oaks to shy deer, within its serene, natural setting. Explore winding paths perfect for walking and cycling, immersing yourself in the sights and sounds of a thriving woodland ecosystem. Discover a peaceful escape where nature's beauty and gentle adventures await.

Name: Fingringhoe Wick
Description: Fingringhoe Wick is a 48.6-hectare nature reserve in Fingringhoe in Essex.

Name: Fir and Pond Woods
Description: Fir and Pond Woods is a 29 hectare nature reserve in Potters Bar in Hertfordshire.  It is managed by the Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust.

Name: Fir Tree Copse
Description: Fir Tree Copse is a 6-hectare nature reserve south-east of Dunsfold in Surrey.  It is managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust and is part of the Chiddingfold Forest Site of Special Scientific Interest This is oak and ash woodland, with hazel coppice.

Name: Firestone Copse
Description: Wander through a vibrant tapestry of ancient trees and flourishing undergrowth, where sunlight dapples the woodland floor. This haven teems with diverse wildlife, offering a tranquil escape for walkers and cyclists to immerse themselves in nature's embrace. Discover a rich natural environment perfect for exploring on foot or by bike, and connect with the beauty of the countryside.

Name: Firs Farm Wetlands
Description: Firs Farm Wetlands, in Winchmore Hill, Enfield, transformed an under-used playing field into an award-winning wetland. It provides a vital wildlife habitat, natural flood defence, and a community space. Regular volunteer days connect people with the river.

Name: Fivehead Arable Fields
Description: Fivehead Arable Fields is a 10.3 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest near the village of Fivehead in Somerset, notified in 1990.

Name: Flamborough Head
Description: Flamborough Head is a promontory, 8 miles long on the Yorkshire coast of England, between the Filey and Bridlington bays of the North Sea.  It is a chalk headland, with sheer white cliffs.

Name: Flanders Moss NNR
Description: Flanders Moss is a raised bog, a rare habitat in Europe. It provides a home for a wide range of plants and animals. Boardwalks and a viewing tower allow visitors to explore the moss and observe wildlife. It is an internationally important site for nature conservation.

Name: Flashdown Wood at Eggesford
Description: Discover a haven of ancient oaks and vibrant woodlands in this Forestry England gem, where dappled sunlight filters through the canopy, illuminating a rich tapestry of life. Explore winding trails perfect for walkers and cyclists, offering glimpses of diverse wildlife amidst the tranquil beauty of the South West. Immerse yourself in nature's embrace and experience the serene atmosphere of this captivating woodland.

Name: Flatropers Wood
Description: Flatropers Wood is a 38-hectare nature reserve in Rye in East Sussex.  It is managed by the Sussex Wildlife Trust.

Name: Flexford
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Flexford Nature Reserve is a 18-hectare nature reserve in Chandler's Ford in Hampshire.  It is managed by the Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust.

Name: Fobbing Marsh
Description: Fobbing Marsh is a 75.7-hectare nature reserve east of Fobbing in Essex.

Name: Folkes Lane Woodland
Description: This expansive woodland offers a haven for diverse wildlife, from ancient trees teeming with birdlife to hidden glades where you might spot deer. Explore winding trails perfect for invigorating walks or cycling adventures, immersing yourself in the sights and sounds of a thriving South East England ecosystem. It's a place to connect with nature and discover the quiet beauty of a well-loved forest.

Name: Folkestone Warren
Description: Folkestone Warren is a geological SSSI within the Kent Downs AONB, managed by White Cliffs Countryside Partnership. This significant coastal landslip habitat features cliffs, boulder fields, and rare species, attracting walkers and naturalists. It is home to unique invertebrates, plants, and lichens.

Name: Folly Farm
Description: Folly Farm is a traditionally managed working farm and nature reserve run by the Avon Wildlife Trust.  It is located between Stowey, Clutton and Stanton Wick in the civil parish of Stowey in the English county of Somerset.

Name: Forest of Dean Cycle Centre
Description: Nestled within ancient woodlands, this Forestry England site offers a vibrant tapestry of natural beauty, where ancient trees provide a haven for diverse wildlife. Visitors can immerse themselves in the tranquil surroundings, enjoying invigorating walks and exhilarating cycles amidst the sights and sounds of a thriving ecosystem. It's a place to connect with nature and discover the wild heart of the forest.

Name: Forests of Rothbury
Description: This expansive woodland in North England offers a haven of natural beauty, where ancient trees create a dappled canopy for diverse wildlife to thrive. Wander through peaceful glades, cycle along winding trails, and immerse yourself in the vibrant sights and sounds of the countryside. It's a perfect place to reconnect with nature and explore the wild heart of the region.

Name: Formby
Description: Formby boasts stunning beaches, expansive sand dunes, and vital habitats for endangered red squirrels and natterjack toads.

Name: Formonthills
Description: Formonthills features a diverse woodland, integrating mature and younger trees with open grasslands. A network of paths provides public access. The site offers views over the Firth of Forth and is actively managed for wildlife conservation and recreation.

Name: Forsinard Flows
Description: Forsinard Flows is a vast blanket bog in the north of Scotland, home to rare plants, insects, and breeding birds like red-throated divers and golden plovers. It features trails, an observation tower, and a 'flows lookout' viewing point.

Name: Forth River Ecological Corridor
Description: The Forth River Ecological Corridor is a West Belfast regeneration project. It enhances natural habitats, promotes biodiversity, and develops a community pathway along the river. Environmental initiatives offer training and volunteering for local residents.

Name: Forty Hall Estate
Description: Forty Hall Estate in Enfield, London, is a historic estate featuring significant ancient woodland, a medieval fishing lake, and an organic farm. It serves as a crucial green space, supporting diverse habitats and biodiversity within the borough, and is managed by the London Borough of Enfield.

Name: Forvie NNR
Description: Forvie NNR features dynamic shifting sands and a significant dune system along the Scottish coast. It hosts Britain's largest eider duck breeding colony and an internationally important grey seal colony. The reserve is home to various seabirds and provides a wild coastal landscape.

Name: Fountains Abbey
Description: Fountains Abbey is set within Studley Royal Park, an 18th-century landscaped garden.

Name: Fourlaws
Description: This expansive woodland in North England offers a vibrant tapestry of ancient trees and open glades, providing a haven for diverse wildlife. Visitors can immerse themselves in nature, exploring winding paths perfect for walking and cycling, and discovering the rich biodiversity that thrives within its verdant embrace. It's a place to connect with the wild, breathe in the fresh air, and witness the beauty of the natural world.

Name: Fowlsheugh
Description: Fowlsheugh is a clifftop nature reserve south of Stonehaven, Aberdeenshire. It supports thousands of breeding seabirds including kittiwakes, guillemots, razorbills, and puffins. Fulmars and shags also nest here, offering spectacular cliff views.

Name: Fox Covert
Description: Fox Covert is a 2.9-hectare nature reserve near Royston in North Hertfordshire.

Name: Fox Fritillary Meadow
Description: Fox Fritillary Meadow is a 2.4-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north of Framsden in Suffolk.

Name: Fox Hagg
HostOrg: Wildlife Trust for Sheffield and Rotherham
Description: Fox Hagg is a small) nature reserve in the Rivelin Valley area of Sheffield, England.  The Allen Sike flows along the north edge of the reserve and the River Rivelin flows through the reserve from Rivelin Dams to the west.

Name: Foxburrow Farm
Description: Foxburrow Farm is a 67 hectare nature reserve north of Melton in Suffolk.  It is managed by the Suffolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Foxcote Reservoir
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Foxcote Reservoir and Wood is a 48.3-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest between Akeley and Maids Moreton in Buckinghamshire, England.

Name: Foxearth Meadows
Description: Foxearth Meadows is an 11-acre (approximately 4.45-hectare) nature reserve located on the River Stour floodplain, in a quiet corner of Essex on the border with Suffolk. It is owned and managed by A Rocha UK. The site features a variety of habitats including river and riverbank, wetlands, woodland, ancient hedgerows, ponds, and marshy flower-rich grassland. It is particularly noted for its importance to dragonflies and damselflies, with 21 species recorded, and also supports other wildlife such as otter, kingfisher, harvest mouse, common lizard, and grass snake.

Name: Foxes Bridge Bog
Description: Foxes Bridge Bog is a 5.3-hectare nature reserve in Gloucestershire.

Name: Foxholes
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Bould Wood is a 58.2-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north of Shipton-under-Wychwood in Oxfordshire.

Name: Foxley Wood
Description: Foxley Wood is a nature reserve in Foxley, Norfolk, England, the largest ancient woodland and coppice in Norfolk.  The Norfolk Wildlife Trust, which manages this reserve, bought it in 1998.

Name: Frampton Marsh
Description: Frampton Marsh is a nature reserve in Lincolnshire, England.  The reserve is situated on the coast of The Wash, 4 miles from the town of Boston, between the outfalls of the Rivers Welland and Witham, and near the village of Frampton in an area known as the “Fosdyke Wash”.

Name: Fraser Down
Description: Fraser Down is a 10-hectare nature reserve north of Betchworth in Surrey.  It is managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Frays Farm Meadows
Description: Frays Farm Meadows is a 28.2-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest near Denham in the London Borough of Hillingdon.

Name: Freiston Shore
Description: Freiston Shore is an RSPB nature reserve on the Lincolnshire coast. It comprises lagoons, saltmarsh, and intertidal mudflats, providing crucial habitats for wading birds like avocets and redshanks, and supporting migratory species. Visitors can explore walking trails and use bird hides.

Name: Frillinghurst Wood
Description: Discover a vibrant tapestry of ancient oak and beech trees, where dappled sunlight filters through the canopy, creating a serene atmosphere. This expansive woodland teems with life, from the rustling of unseen creatures in the undergrowth to the soaring of birds overhead. Explore winding paths that invite leisurely walks and exhilarating bike rides, immersing yourself in the sights and sounds of nature's embrace.

Name: Friston Forest
Description: Discover a vibrant tapestry of ancient woodland and open glades, alive with the calls of diverse birdlife and the rustle of unseen creatures. Explore winding paths perfect for invigorating walks or exhilarating cycles, immersing yourself in the sights and sounds of this thriving natural haven. This expansive woodland offers a peaceful escape, inviting you to connect with nature and witness its enduring beauty.

Name: Fritham and Eyeworth Pond
Description: This ancient woodland offers a serene escape where ancient oaks and beeches create a dappled canopy, alive with the calls of woodland birds and the rustle of unseen creatures. Explore meandering trails perfect for walking and cycling, immersing yourself in the rich biodiversity and tranquil beauty of this special place. Discover hidden ponds reflecting the sky, offering peaceful spots to observe nature at its finest.

Name: Frogmore Meadow
Description: Frogmore Meadows is a 4.6-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Hertfordshire and Buckinghamshire, north of the village of Chenies.

Name: Frome Banks
Description: Frome Banks is a 1.3-hectare nature reserve in Gloucestershire.

Name: Fryent Country Park
Description: Fryent Country Park, located in Kingsbury, North West London, covers 103 hectares (254 acres). This extensive green space is a designated Local Nature Reserve and a Site of Importance for Nature Conservation, managed primarily for wildlife. It features a diverse mix of uncultivated hay meadows (some with Soil Association Organic Standard), ancient woodlands, hedgerows, and ponds, supporting over 800 species of wildlife. The park offers extensive views across London, particularly from Barn Hill.

Name: Fylde Sand Dunes Project
Description: The Fylde Sand Dunes Project is a partnership project to improve the dunes on the coast of the Fylde as a sea defence, conserve the coastal environment, and improve public awareness of the dunes.  The project is a partnership between the Lancashire Wildlife Trust, Fylde Council and Blackpool Council, and is funded by the Environment Agency until 2027.

Name: Fyne Court
Description: This nature reserve offers a diverse landscape of woodland, ponds, and meadows for wildlife.

Name: Gailey Reservoirs
Description: Gailey Reservoirs are two linked bodies of water by the Shropshire Union Canal near Gailey. The site is a popular destination for birdwatchers, known for its significant populations of winter wildfowl, gulls, and various wader species.

Name: Gait Barrows NNR
Description: Gait Barrows National Nature Reserve protects extensive limestone pavement, ancient woodland, and mires in Lancashire. It supports rare plants and insects, including the high brown fritillary butterfly. Management focuses on grazing and woodland restoration.

Name: Gaps Hill
Description: Duddas Wood is a broadleaved woodland in Derrington, Staffordshire, created and planted by the local community. It offers excellent views of Stafford Castle and features public access with walking paths. The wood is also located on the Sustrans national cycleway.

Name: Gatton Park
Description: Gatton Park's 500 acres of tranquil parkland and gardens provide an important refuge for local wildlife and diverse plant life.

Name: Gawthorpe Hall
Description: Gawthorpe Hall is set within scenic landscapes on the banks of the River Calder.

Name: Geilston Garden
Description: This garden features a towering Wellingtonia, vibrant walled and kitchen gardens with seasonal produce, and the meandering Geilston burn.

Name: Gelt Woods
Description: Gelt Woods is an ancient woodland ravine in Cumbria, known for its diverse flora and fauna. The River Gelt carves through the sandstone, creating unique habitats. Part of the area is managed as an RSPB nature reserve, supporting ancient trees, wildflowers, and various bird species. It also features a remarkable Roman quarry, where stone was extracted for Hadrian's Wall.

Name: George Henry Wood
Description: George Henry Wood is a recently established woodland in Rutland, managed by the Woodland Trust. It was planted over four years from 2007, made possible by the legacy of George Henry Sellars, and offers a new habitat for local wildlife.

Name: George's Hayes
Description: George's Hayes is a nature reserve of the Staffordshire Wildlife Trust.  It is an ancient woodland, about a mile south-west of the village of Longdon, between Rugeley and Lichfield in Staffordshire, England.

Name: Gernon Bushes
Description: Gernon Bushes is a 32 hectare nature reserve north-east of Epping in Essex, England, which is managed by the Essex Wildlife Trust.  It is part of the Epping Forest Site of Special Scientific Interest and Nature Conservation Review site.

Name: Gibraltar Point National Nature Reserve
Description: Gibraltar Point is a headland on the coast of Lincolnshire, England, 3.5 miles south of Skegness, where the North Sea coast turns southwest towards Boston and enters The Wash.

Name: Gibside
Description: Discover extensive Georgian landscaped parkland in the scenic River Derwent valley, rich in diverse natural beauty.

Name: Gillham Wood
Description: Gillham Wood is a 3-hectare nature reserve west of Bexhill-on-Sea in East Sussex.  It is managed by the Sussex Wildlife Trust.

Name: Gillingham Royal Forest
Description: Stour Meadows is a Local Nature Reserve in Gillingham, Dorset, managed by Dorset Council. It comprises riverside meadows along the River Stour, providing habitats for diverse wildlife and offering opportunities for walking and enjoying nature.

Name: Gisburn Forest and Stocks
Description: This expansive woodland in the heart of Lancashire offers a vibrant tapestry of ancient oak, towering conifers, and open moorland, providing a haven for diverse wildlife. Explore winding trails perfect for both peaceful ambles and exhilarating cycling adventures, immersing yourself in the sights and sounds of nature. Discover hidden streams, expansive views, and the quiet beauty of a thriving natural landscape.

Name: Glasswater Wood
Description: Glasswater Wood is a broadleaf woodland near Crossgar in County Down, Northern Ireland. Originally planted in 2000, it has been expanded and now covers almost 10 hectares (24 acres). The site features walking trails and is popular with local walkers.

Name: Glastonbury Tor
Description: This distinctive conical hill of clay and Blue Lias rises dramatically from the flat Somerset Levels, showcasing unique geological erosion.

Name: Glen Auldyn
Description: Glen Auldyn is a narrow valley about 6 kilometres long on the Isle of Man, with a river of the same name.  This flows in a NNE direction and flows into the River Sulby not far from its estuary, near Ramsey.

Name: Glen Coe
Description: Glen Coe is a dramatic glacial glen carved through volcanic rock in the Scottish Highlands, offering soaring mountain scenery for mountaineering and hillwalking.

Name: Glen Finglas
Description: Glen Finglas is a Highland estate within Loch Lomond & The Trossachs National Park, part of the Great Trossachs Forest National Nature Reserve. It features ancient woodlands, heathland, and open ground, managed for conservation and public access. The site protects significant habitats and species.

Name: Glen Roy NNR
Description: Glen Roy National Nature Reserve in the Scottish Highlands is renowned for its 'Parallel Roads', a unique geological feature. These three distinct shorelines were formed by an ancient ice-dammed loch, providing a clear record of glacial lake levels and processes.

Name: Glenarm
Description: Glenarm Nature Reserve protects ancient woodland and a salmon river near Glenarm village. The site features steep slopes with oak and ash trees. Spring sees carpets of bluebells and wild garlic. Red squirrels and otters are present, reflecting its biodiversity.

Name: Glenborrodale
