Description: Glenborrodale RSPB reserve lies on the Ardnamurchan peninsula, featuring ancient oak woodlands and coastal habitats. The site overlooks Loch Sunart and supports golden eagles, white-tailed eagles, red deer, and otters. Walking trails are accessible.

Name: Glenbrook Wetlands
Description: Glenbrook Wetlands is a new wetland in Glenbrook Park, Enfield, created by Thames21 as part of the "Restoring Enfield's Rivers" project. It involved de-culverting and re-naturalising the Glenbrook, enhancing local amenity and providing flood attenuation benefits.

Name: Glendun Nature Reserve
Description: Glendun (John McSparran Memorial Farm) is a traditional hill farm in the spectacular Glens of Antrim, managed by Ulster Wildlife. It aims to demonstrate the benefits of farming for nature. The 80-hectare reserve features diverse habitats including peatlands, species-rich grasslands, scrub, mixed ash woodland, rough moorland, and blanket bog, supporting a variety of wildlife such as red grouse, emperor moth, small heath butterflies, otters, red squirrels, and Irish hares.

Name: Glendurgan Garden
Description: Nestled in a 'deep valley of otters' by the Helford River, this garden offers rich plant diversity and wildlife habitat.

Name: Glenfeshie Estate
Description: Glenfeshie Estate spans over 44,000 acres in the Scottish Highlands, actively engaged in ecological restoration and rewilding. It restores native woodlands and supports diverse wildlife populations through ongoing conservation and research efforts.

Name: Glentress
Description: Glentress, near Peebles, is a 7stanes mountain biking centre within Tweed Valley Forest Park. It offers walking trails, a cafe, bike hire, and Go Ape. This site provides diverse outdoor activities for visitors.

Name: Glory Wood and Devil's Den
Description: Glory Wood and Devil's Den is a 13-hectare nature reserve south-east of Dorking in Surrey. It is an area of semi-natural woodland on sandstone hills, featuring diverse tree species like oak and sweet chestnut. The site supports various mammals including bats, roe deer, badgers, and foxes, and offers views over the North and South Downs.

Name: Glyme Valley
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Glyme Valley is a 28.9-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest east of Chipping Norton in Oxfordshire.

Name: Goat Fell
Description: Arran's highest mountain, Goat Fell provides breathtaking vistas of the island's rugged highland landscapes.

Name: Gobions Wood
Description: Gobions Wood is a 36 hectare nature reserve managed by the Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust in Brookmans Park in Hertfordshire.  The site was formerly owned by the Gobions Woodland Trust, a registered charity which was closed down in 2013 because it had ceased to exist.

Name: Goblin Combe
Description: Goblin Combe is a dry valley in North Somerset which stretches for approximately 3½ km from Redhill, near Bristol International Airport on the A38, through to Cleeve on the A370.  The combe is located at, and is a 52-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest originally notified in 1999, with 9 hectares being managed as a nature reserve by the Avon Wildlife Trust.

Name: Godrevy
Description: Godrevy is a dramatic Cornish promontory and Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, with stunning Atlantic coastline, offshore island, surfing beaches, and the South West Coast Path.

Name: Gogar Wood
Description: Gogar Wood is a young, developing woodland on the western outskirts of Edinburgh. It features a range of native broadleaf species. Pathways allow for exploration and wildlife observation. The site is managed for biodiversity and public access.

Name: Golitha Falls
Description: Golitha Falls is a National Nature Reserve and Site of Special Scientific Interest in Cornwall, South West England. This ancient woodland features a series of spectacular cascades along the River Fowey and is recognized as a temperate rainforest, supporting a rich diversity of mosses, lichens, and ferns.

Name: Gomm Valley
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Gomm Valley is a 4-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Micklefield, a district of High Wycombe in Buckinghamshire.  It is managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust and is part of the Chilterns Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty.

Name: Gondola (steam yacht)
Description: Sail Coniston Water to experience the serene beauty of its expansive waters and the dramatic fells of the Lake District National Park.

Name: Goonhilly Downs
Description: Goonhilly Downs is a Site of Special Scientific Interest that forms a raised plateau in the central western area of the Lizard peninsula in southern Cornwall, England.  It is one of 229 English national nature reserves designated by Natural England with an area of almost 1,270 hectares.

Name: Gordano Valley
Description: Gordano is an area of North Somerset, in England.  It has been designated as a National Nature Reserve.

Name: Goscote Reedbed
Description: Goscote Reedbed, a former landfill site along the Wyrley & Essington Canal in Walsall, West Midlands, has been transformed into a thriving wildlife haven. It features newly created reedbeds and wetland habitats, alongside a specific kingfisher nesting bank, enhancing biodiversity.

Name: Gowy Meadows Nature Reserve
Description: Gowy Meadows Nature Reserve is a 165.8-hectare nature reserve near Ellesmere Port, Cheshire, England.

Name: Goyt Valley
Description: This expansive woodland in the heart of the Midlands offers a haven for diverse wildlife amidst rolling hills and ancient trees. Miles of trails invite exploration by foot or bike, leading through tranquil glades and alongside sparkling waterways, perfect for immersing yourself in the natural beauty. Discover a rich tapestry of flora and fauna as you wander through this captivating landscape.

Name: Gracious Pond
Description: Gracious Pond is a 14-hectare nature reserve in Chobham in Surrey.  It is managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Graeme Hendrey Wood
Description: Graeme Hendrey Wood is a 10-hectare nature reserve east of Bletchingley in Surrey.  It is managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Graffham Common
Description: Graffham Common is a 38-hectare nature reserve between Midhurst and Petworth in West Sussex.  It is owned and managed by the Sussex Wildlife Trust.

Name: Grafham Water
Description: Grafham Water is a large reservoir and an 806.3-hectare Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI). The site includes a 114-hectare (280-acre) nature reserve, managed by Anglian Water, featuring extensive reedbeds, woodlands, and grasslands, providing habitat for diverse wildlife including overwintering birds and otters. The reserve offers hides for birdwatching.

Name: Graig Wood
Description: Graig Wood is a Site of Special Scientific Interest, noted for its biological characteristics, in Monmouthshire, south east Wales.  It forms part of the wider Hael Woods complex.

Name: Grange Farm
Description: Grange Farm is an RSPB nature reserve near Honington, Suffolk, actively undergoing restoration from former arable land. It features a mix of newly created grasslands, wetlands, and hedgerows. The reserve provides vital habitats for a variety of bird species and local wildlife, focusing on ecological recovery.

Name: Grangelands and Pulpit Hill
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Grangelands and Pulpit Hill is a 25 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Cadsden in Buckinghamshire. It lies within the Chilterns Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty.

Name: Granville Country Park
Description: Granville Country Park is a local nature reserve near Telford in Shropshire, England.  It is owned by Telford and Wrekin Council, who work in partnership with the Shropshire Wildlife Trust and Friends of Granville.

Name: Granville Nature Reserve
Description: Granville Country Park is a Local Nature Reserve near Telford, Shropshire, covering approximately 85.5 hectares of former industrial land. It features diverse habitats including wildflower meadows, woodlands, ponds, and marshland, supporting a variety of wildlife. The reserve is owned by Telford and Wrekin Council and managed in partnership with Shropshire Wildlife Trust and the Friends of Granville, offering accessible walking trails and showcasing its rich industrial heritage.

Name: Grasmere (lake)
Description: Grasmere is a Lake District lake, fed and drained by the River Rothay, forming a key part of the region's interconnected water system, and featuring a single island.

Name: Grays Thurrock Chalk Pit
Description: Grays Thurrock Chalk Pit is a 17.3-hectare Site of Special Scientific Interest in Grays in Essex.

Name: Great Breach and Copley Woods
Description: Great Breach and Copley Woods is a 64.8 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest 1 km south of Compton Dundon and 5 km south-east of Street in Somerset, England, notified in 1972.

Name: Great Casterton Road Banks
Description: Great Casterton Road Banks is a 0.4-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest on the western outskirts of Stamford in Lincolnshire.

Name: Great Cornard Country Park
HostOrg: Great Cornard Parish Council (Owner) and Sudbury Common Lands Charity (Manager)
Description: Great Cornard Country Park is located along the River Stour Valley, forming part of the Stour Valley Path. It features meadows, woodland, and ponds, providing habitats for diverse wildlife and offering recreational space for visitors.

Name: Great Hockham
Description: This expansive woodland offers a haven for diverse wildlife, with ancient trees creating a dappled canopy under which walkers and cyclists can explore. Discover winding trails through a rich tapestry of natural habitats, perfect for immersing yourself in the sights and sounds of the English countryside.  It's a place to reconnect with nature, observe woodland creatures, and enjoy the simple pleasures of a peaceful outdoor adventure.

Name: Great Holland Pits
Description: Great Holland Pits is a 16.2-hectare nature reserve east of Great Holland in Essex.

Name: Great Merrible Wood
Description: Great Merrible Wood is a 12 hectare nature reserve east of Hallaton in Leicestershire.  It is owned and managed by the Leicestershire and Rutland Wildlife Trust, and is part of the Eye Brook Valley Woods Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Great Plantation
Description: Wander through a tapestry of ancient trees and vibrant undergrowth, where sunlight dapples the forest floor and the air hums with the buzz of insects. This South West woodland is a haven for diverse wildlife, from shy woodland creatures to a symphony of bird song, offering peaceful walks and exhilarating cycling trails through its natural beauty. Discover a place to immerse yourself in nature, breathe in the fresh air, and connect with the living heart of the forest.

Name: Great Wood
Description: This expansive woodland offers a haven for diverse wildlife, from soaring birds to shy woodland mammals, thriving amidst ancient trees and vibrant undergrowth. Visitors can explore miles of winding trails, perfect for invigorating walks or cycling adventures, immersing themselves in the sights and sounds of a flourishing natural landscape. It's a place to connect with nature, breathe fresh air, and discover the beauty of a thriving forest ecosystem.

Name: Greatstone Dunes
Description: Greatstone Dunes is a Site of Special Scientific Interest in Kent, known for its unique habitat. It features mobile and fixed dunes, dune slacks, shingle, and saltmarsh. The site supports many rare plants and invertebrates, including the nationally rare sandhill rustic moth.

Name: Green Lane Wood
Description: Green Lane Wood, an ancient woodland in Cambridgeshire, is managed by the Woodland Trust. The site features mature trees, diverse flora, and a network of paths for visitors, providing a habitat for local wildlife and offering a tranquil setting.

Name: Green Park - Meadow Restoration Areas
Description: Green Park's meadow restoration areas enhance biodiversity in central London. Located near The Mall and Constitution Hill, these designated zones support pollinators and various wildlife, creating diverse habitats within the park's landscape.

Name: Greenbank Garden
Description: Greenbank Garden features a vibrant 2.5-acre walled garden, a rich horticultural landscape providing diverse plantings and supporting local wildlife.

Name: Greenham and Crookham Commons
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Greenham and Crookham Commons are two adjoining public park areas of 280.5-hectare common land designated as a biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in the civil parishes of Greenham and Thatcham, on the southern outskirts of Newbury in the English county of Berkshire, home to a variety of rare wildlife.

Name: Greenway Estate
Description: Discover serene woodlands and riverside paths offering breathtaking views of the River Dart estuary.

Name: Greenwich Peninsula Ecology Park
Description: Greenwich Peninsula Ecology Park is a four-acre nature reserve in London, a designated Site of Borough Importance for Nature Conservation, Grade I. It features diverse freshwater habitats including two lakes, marshland, reedbeds, and meadows, supporting a rich variety of wildlife such as amphibians, fish, insects, and birds. The Conservation Volunteers (TCV) manages the site, offering environmental education and community events.

Name: Greno Woods
HostOrg: Wildlife Trust for Sheffield and Rotherham
Description: Greno Woods is a 178 hectares area of ancient woodland and nature reserve located north of Grenoside village, a suburb of Sheffield, South Yorkshire, England.  Previously used as a quarry, hunting ground, and for commercial forestry; it is now used for recreational walking, jogging and mountain biking.

Name: Gresley, Swainspark and Tunnel Woods
Description: Explore a vibrant mosaic of ancient woodland and open meadows teeming with diverse wildlife, from soaring birds to elusive mammals. Wander through dappled sunlight on well-trodden paths, or cycle along scenic routes that wind through this expansive natural haven. Discover a place where the beauty of the natural world unfolds at every turn, offering a refreshing escape for walkers and nature enthusiasts alike.

Name: Grey Hope Bay
Description: Greyhope Bay is an award-winning community-led marine experience at the mouth of Aberdeen Harbour. It offers views of bottlenose dolphins, harbour porpoise, grey seals, and various seabirds. The site features a repurposed shipping container visitor centre and cafe.

Name: Grey Mare's Tail, Moffat Hills
Description: Discover a dramatic waterfall, upland loch, and rare plants within this botanically diverse Southern Uplands landscape, home to unique wildlife like wild goats.

Name: Greyfield Wood
Description: Greyfield Wood is a 36.23-hectare (89.5-acre) ancient woodland situated on the outskirts of High Littleton in north-east Somerset, approximately 16 km from Bath and 19 km from Bristol. Managed by the Woodland Trust, it features a diverse mix of ancient broadleaf trees, naturally regenerated areas, and conifer plantations, supporting a rich array of flora and fauna. It offers extensive permissive paths for public access, including circular walks.

Name: Greylake
Description: Greylake is an RSPB nature reserve situated on the Somerset Levels. The site features an accessible hide and boardwalk, offering views of wetland birds such as lapwings, snipe, and various duck species. It provides habitat for diverse wildlife, with seasonal highlights including breeding waders and wintering wildfowl.

Name: Greys Court
Description: Nestled in the southern Chiltern Hills, explore tranquil gardens and the surrounding natural beauty.

Name: Greywell Moors
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Greywell Fen is a 38-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Greywell in Hampshire.  It is a Nature Conservation Review site, Grade 2, and an area of 13 hectares is a nature reserve called Greywell Moors, which is managed by the Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust.

Name: Griffin Wood
Description: Griffin Wood is a 12-hectare community woodland in Bold, south St. Helens, Merseyside, managed by The Mersey Forest in partnership with the Friends of Griffin Wood. It comprises both mature and newly planted broadleaved trees and pines, along with wildflower meadows. The site features meandering paths, a community orchard, and a sculpture trail, offering green space for recreation and nature observation. It is part of the larger Bold Forest Park.

Name: Grime’s Graves
Description: Grime’s Graves is a unique Neolithic flint mine site and Scheduled Monument, managed by English Heritage. It features diverse chalk grassland and woodland, supporting rare plants like the military orchid and various invertebrate species, important for its archaeology and biodiversity, with ecological input from Norfolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Grimwith Reservoir
Description: Grimwith Reservoir, a large upland reservoir in the Yorkshire Dales National Park near Pateley Bridge, supplies drinking water. It features extensive peat bogs, heather moorland, and grasslands, supporting diverse wildlife and critical habitats for wading birds.

Name: Grizedale
Description: This expansive woodland in the heart of the Lake District offers a captivating blend of ancient trees and rugged landscapes, alive with the calls of diverse birdlife and the rustle of unseen creatures. Visitors can immerse themselves in nature by exploring miles of winding trails perfect for walking and cycling, discovering hidden waterfalls, and enjoying the tranquility of this wild Northern English setting. It's a place to breathe deep, connect with the natural world, and experience the beauty of the fells and forests.

Name: Groton Wood
Description: Groton Wood is a 20.2-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north-east of Groton in Suffolk.

Name: Grovelands Park
Description: Grovelands Park is a Grade II* listed Green Flag park in Enfield, London. It features extensive woodlands, a formal garden, and a large lake. The lake has undergone enhancements to boost its biodiversity, supporting local wildlife.

Name: Gugh
Description: Gugh could be described as the sixth inhabited island of the Isles of Scilly, but is usually included with St Agnes with which it is joined by a sandy tombolo known as "The Bar" when exposed at low tide.  The island is only about 1 km long and about 0.

Name: Guisborough Forest
Description: Discover a vibrant tapestry of ancient woodland and rolling hills, alive with the chatter of birds and the rustle of unseen creatures. Immerse yourself in this expansive natural playground, where winding trails invite exploration by foot or cycle, offering breathtaking views and a chance to connect with the wild heart of North England. From majestic trees to diverse wildlife, this Forestry England woodland provides an unforgettable sensory experience.

Name: Gullivers Farm
Description: Gullivers Farm is a 90-acre organic and biodynamic working farm and social enterprise in West Moors, Dorset, managed by Sturts Community Trust. It provides support and opportunities to adults with varying support needs, alongside sustainable farming practices and a farm shop and cafe.

Name: Gunby Hall
Description: Gunby Hall is set within a substantial 1,500-acre estate, offering expansive countryside and diverse habitats crucial for regional wildlife.

Name: Gunners Park and Shoebury Ranges
Description: Gunners Park and Shoebury Ranges is a 25 hectare nature reserve in Shoeburyness in Essex.  It is managed by the Essex Wildlife Trust.

Name: Gunnersbury Triangle
Description: Gunnersbury Triangle is a 2.57-hectare local nature reserve in Chiswick, in the London boroughs of Ealing and Hounslow, immediately to the east of Gunnersbury.

Name: Gunpowder Park
Description: Gunpowder Park, a Green Flag site in Lee Valley Regional Park, was transformed from a former testing ground. It offers 100 acres of meadows and woods, providing habitats for diverse wildlife. The park features trails for walking and cycling.

Name: Gunton Meadow
Description: Gunton Meadow is a 2-hectare nature reserve in Lowestoft in Suffolk.  It is managed by the Suffolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Gunton Warren
Description: Gunton Warren and Corton Woods is a 31.9 hectare Local Nature Reserve in Lowestoft in Suffolk.

Name: Gwaith Powdwr
Description: Gwaith Powdwr,, situated in Penrhyndeudraeth, Wales, is a decommissioned explosives works now managed as a Nature Reserve by the North Wales Wildlife Trust.  The explosives factory was initially opened in 1865 and changed hands several times before being bought by Ralph Cooke in 1922.

Name: Gwen and Vera's Fields
Description: Gwen and Vera's Fields is a 0.28-hectare nature reserve in Gloucestershire.

Name: Gwenffrwd-Dinas
Description: Ancient oak woodlands in the Tywi valley, Carmarthenshire, Wales. A Special Area of Conservation, home to pied flycatchers, redstarts, and wood warblers. Bluebells carpet the valley floor. Features rocky river stretches and waterfalls, managed by RSPB.

Name: Hackhurst Downs
Description: Hackhurst and White Downs is a 185.1-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest west of Dorking in Surrey.

Name: Hadrian's Wall Wetlands Landscape Recovery Project
Description: Hadrian's Wall Wetlands is an 11,000-acre Landscape Recovery Project. It restores and enhances peatlands and wetlands across the Hadrian's Wall area in Northumberland, aiming to improve biodiversity, water quality, and carbon storage within the national park.

Name: Hagg Wood
Description: This ancient woodland in Northern England offers a haven for diverse wildlife, from soaring birds of prey to elusive woodland creatures that call its mature trees home. Miles of winding paths invite exploration, perfect for walkers and cyclists to immerse themselves in the tranquil beauty and discover the secrets of this thriving natural environment. Visitors can enjoy the simple pleasures of a peaceful stroll or an invigorating bike ride amidst the captivating sights and sounds of nature.

Name: Hainault Forest
Description: Hainault Forest spans 335 acres in northeast London, featuring ancient woodland, grasslands, a lake, and a zoo. Visitors can explore various walking trails, engage with wildlife, and enjoy open spaces for recreation. The site is a significant green lung.

Name: Haldon Forest Park
Description: Explore a vast expanse of ancient woodland and vibrant coniferous trees in this stunning natural playground. Discover a haven for diverse wildlife, from elusive deer to a symphony of birdsong, as you wander or cycle through its beautiful trails. Immerse yourself in the tranquility of nature, breathing in fresh air and experiencing the simple joy of the outdoors.

Name: Halesworth Millennium Green
Description: Halesworth Millennium Green is a 55-acre nature reserve on the River Blyth flood plain in Suffolk, offering diverse habitats from meadows to woodlands. The site provides walking trails and focuses on conservation, with ongoing river restoration work, and is managed by the Halesworth Millennium Green CIO.

Name: Ham Hill, Wiltshire
Description: Ham Hill is a hill and area of chalk downland in Wiltshire, England, on the steep banks running alongside the road from the village of Ham to Buttermere, close to the Berkshire border.  A biological Site of Special Scientific Interest, notified in 1971, covers 1.

Name: Ham House
Description: Its formal gardens and location on the bank of the River Thames offer a unique blend of cultivated beauty and riverside nature.

Name: Ham Street Woods
Description: Ham Street Woods is a 97-hectare ancient woodland National Nature Reserve (NNR) and Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) near Hamstreet, Ashford, Kent. It is a remnant of the extensive oak forests that once covered the Weald, featuring diverse habitats including oak and hornbeam stands, supporting varied flora and fauna. The reserve is actively managed by Natural England for conservation, scientific research, education, and public access, offering waymarked trails.

Name: Ham Wall
Description: Ham Wall is a Somerset wetland nature reserve managed by the RSPB. It features extensive reedbeds, open water, and wet woodland, providing habitat for diverse wildlife including bitterns, marsh harriers, and otters. Visitors can explore a network of trails and viewing hides.

Name: Hambledon Hill
Description: This chalk outcrop offers panoramic views across the Blackmore Vale and River Stour, supporting rare wildflowers and butterflies on its species-rich grasslands.

Name: Hamford Water National Nature Reserve
Description: Hamford Water is an internationally important wetland, encompassing creeks, saltmarsh, and mudflats. It supports significant populations of overwintering and breeding birds, including avocets and dark-bellied brent geese. This estuarine site is also home to seals and diverse marine life.

Name: Hampstead Heath
Description: Hampstead Heath is a large, ancient parkland in north London, offering diverse habitats, natural swimming ponds, and panoramic city views. It features extensive woodlands, meadows, and sports facilities, managed for public access and conservation.

Name: Hamsterley Forest
Description: This expansive woodland in the heart of County Durham offers a haven for diverse wildlife, from soaring birds of prey to shy woodland creatures. Visitors can immerse themselves in nature's embrace, exploring miles of scenic walking and cycling trails that wind through ancient trees and open glades, revealing breathtaking views and opportunities for quiet contemplation. It's a place to reconnect with the natural world, breathing in fresh, forest air and discovering the beauty of the North East's wild landscapes.

Name: Hanbury Hall
Description: Hanbury Hall is set within extensive parkland featuring veteran trees and grassland habitats in the Worcestershire countryside.

Name: Handa, Scotland
Description: Handa Island or usually Handa, is an island in Eddrachillis Bay off the west coast of Sutherland, Scotland.  It is 309 hectares and 123 metres at its highest point.

Name: Hannah's Meadows

Description: Howell Hill is a 5-hectare nature reserve east of Ewell in Surrey.  It is owned by Surrey County Council and managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Howlands Marsh
Description: Howlands Marsh is a 29.9-hectare nature reserve north-east of St Osyth in Essex.

Name: Howsham Mill Island
Description: Howsham Mill Island is a wooded island in the River Derwent near Malton, North Yorkshire. It provides habitat for otters, kingfishers, and various invertebrates. The island is part of the River Derwent Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and is managed for biodiversity by the Renewable Heritage Trust. The island is publicly accessible, though the mill building has specific opening hours.

Name: Huckerby's Meadows
Description: Huckerby's Meadows is a 13 hectare nature reserve adjacent to Heathrow Airport in the London Borough of Hillingdon.  It is managed by the London Wildlife Trust, and is part of the Crane Corridor Site of Metropolitan Importance for Nature Conservation.

Name: Hucking Estate
Description: Hucking Estate offers a mosaic of ancient woodland, grassland, orchards, and arable land in the Kent Downs Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. This wildlife haven supports varied flora and fauna, including dormice and many bird species. Walking trails are present.

Name: Hucking Estate
Description: Hucking Estate is a large woodland and open space mosaic in Kent, South East England. It features ancient woodland, recently planted areas, and meadows, providing diverse habitats for wildlife. The site offers numerous walking trails and is part of a landscape restoration project.

Name: Hughenden Manor
Description: Enjoy elevated views and the surrounding landscape from this country estate.

Name: Humberhead Peatlands National Nature Reserve
Description: Humberhead Peatlands National Nature Reserve is England's largest lowland raised bog, encompassing Thorne, Hatfield, and Crowle Moors across 2,800 hectares. It is a Special Area of Conservation, vital for its unique peatland habitats and rare wildlife. Restoration efforts are ongoing.

Name: Hunsdon and Eastwick Meads
Description: Hunsdon Mead is a 34 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest west of Harlow and east of Roydon in Essex.  The site is partly in Essex and partly in Hertfordshire, and it is jointly owned and managed by the Essex Wildlife Trust and the Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust.

Name: Hunsdon Mead
Description: Hunsdon Mead is a 34 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest west of Harlow and east of Roydon in Essex.  The site is partly in Essex and partly in Hertfordshire, and it is jointly owned and managed by the Essex Wildlife Trust and the Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust.

Name: Hunter's Hill
Description: Hunter's Hill is a woodland reserve overlooking the Douglas Valley near Parbold. Mixed oak and birch woodlands support diverse wildlife along a network of paths. The site also features the remains of a Victorian folly, offering historical interest to visitors.

Name: Hunter's Wood Nature Reserve
Description: Hunter's Wood Nature Reserve is a nature reserve near Kingsley, Cheshire, England, managed by the Cheshire Wildlife Trust.  Hunter's Wood is a relatively new piece of woodland, originally planted on what was rough pasture on the southern bank of the River Weaver in 1999.

Name: Hunthouse Wood
Description: Hunthouse Wood is a nature reserve of the Worcestershire Wildlife Trust, situated near the villages of Clows Top and Mamble, in Worcestershire, England.

Name: Hurley Chalk Pit
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Hurley Chalk Pit is a 1-hectare nature reserve west of Maidenhead in Berkshire.  It is managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Hurn Forest
Description: Explore a vast expanse of ancient woodland, alive with the rustle of leaves and the songs of diverse birdlife. Wander through sun-dappled trails, perfect for invigorating walks or cycling adventures, and discover the tranquil beauty of this natural haven teeming with wildlife. Immerse yourself in the sights and sounds of nature, from towering trees to the secrets hidden within the undergrowth.

Name: Hutchinson's Bank
Description: Hutchinson's Bank is 21.8 hectare Local Nature Reserve and Site of Metropolitan Importance for Nature Conservation in New Addington in the London Borough of Croydon.

Name: Hutchison's Meadow
Description: Hutchison's Meadow is a one hectare nature reserve in Melton in Suffolk.  It is owned and managed by the Suffolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Hutton Roof Crags
Description: Hutton Roof Crags is a hill in southeastern Cumbria in northwest England, located near to the village of Hutton Roof.  It has extensive areas of limestone pavement as well as grassland and woodland.

Name: Hyde Park
Description: Hyde Park in central London features The Dell, a picturesque rock garden, and the Serpentine lake, which supports diverse wildlife. It is one of the capital's eight Royal Parks, offering both natural habitats and recreational spaces for visitors.

Name: Hydon's Ball
Description: Hydon's Ball is a prominent hill crowned by the ecologically valuable Hydon Heath, supporting unique flora and fauna.

Name: Hythe Spartina Marsh
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 10 hectares.

Name: Ickworth House
Description: Ickworth House is set within extensive parkland, featuring ancient trees and open landscapes that support a variety of local wildlife.

Name: Idle Valley Nature Reserve
Description: The Idle Valley Nature Reserve, also known as Lound Gravel Pits or Sutton and Lound Gravel Pits, is a wetland Site of Special Scientific Interest situated north-west of the town of Retford in the Bassetlaw district of north Nottinghamshire.  The nature reserve is situated along the western bank of the River Idle and east of the villages of Sutton cum Lound and Lound.

Name: Idless Woods
Description: Venture into a realm of ancient oaks and whispering pines, where dappled sunlight filters through a vibrant canopy. This South West haven teems with diverse wildlife, offering tranquil walking and cycling trails that wind through its captivating natural beauty. Immerse yourself in the sights and sounds of a thriving woodland ecosystem, perfect for exploration and peaceful contemplation.

Name: Iffley Meadows
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Iffley Meadows is a 36.1-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Oxford in Oxfordshire.

Name: Ilam Park
Description: Ilam Park is a country park with ancient semi-natural woodlands, including an SSSI noted for rare lime tree hybrids, alongside the River Manifold.

Name: Ilkley Integrated Constructed Wetland
Description: The Ilkley Integrated Constructed Wetland is a nature-based solution designed to provide a final stage of wastewater treatment for the upgraded Ilkley Wastewater Treatment Works. It features six interconnected lagoons with specially chosen wetland plants that naturally treat water before its safe return to the River Wharfe. This project also creates new habitats, enhances biodiversity, and provides public access, contributing to the ecological health and natural flood management of the Lower Wharfe Valley.

Name: Inchnadamph NNR Bone Caves
Description: Inchnadamph NNR in the Scottish Highlands is a landscape of limestone hills, caves, and gorges. Its famous Bone Caves contain unique remains of arctic animals from the last Ice Age, including lynx and polar bear. The reserve supports ancient woodlands and diverse plant life.

Name: Inchree Waterfall & Wood
Description: Inchree, near Fort William, features a spectacular multi-tiered waterfall and accessible woodland trails for walking and cycling. Visitors enjoy nature and wildlife watching opportunities within the Scottish Highlands.

Name: Ingleborough
Description: Ingleborough is the second-highest mountain in the Yorkshire Dales, England.  It is one of the Yorkshire Three Peaks, and is frequently climbed as part of the Three Peaks walk.

Name: Ingrebourne Hill
Description: Discover a haven of ancient woodlands and rolling hills, where diverse habitats teem with wildlife. Wander scenic trails through mature trees, spot native animals, or explore by bicycle amidst the tranquil beauty of this South East England gem. It's a place to reconnect with nature and breathe in the fresh air.

Name: Ingrebourne Valley
Description: Ingrebourne Valley, a nature reserve in Havering, offers diverse habitats including woodlands, grasslands, and wetlands. Part of Ingrebourne Marshes SSSI, it runs south from Upminster to Hornchurch, supporting various wildlife species and providing public recreation.

Name: Ingrebourne Valley
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 261 hectares.

Name: Inkpen Common
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Inkpen Common or Inkpen Great Common is a 12.8-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest east of Inkpen in Berkshire.

Name: Inkpen Crocus Field
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Inkpen Crocus Fields is a 3.1-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest near Inkpen in Berkshire.

Name: Inner Forth
Description: The Inner Forth Wetlands are a significant landscape project in Central Scotland, focused on restoring and connecting vital habitats for migratory birds and local wildlife. It encompasses a network of nature reserves and coastal areas.

Name: Insh Marshes
HostOrg: Royal Society for the Protection of Birds
Description: Insh Marshes is one of Europe's most important wetlands, a vast flood plain alongside the River Spey. Thousands of migratory birds stop here seasonally, and many species of waders, ducks, and geese breed in summer. The reserve supports diverse wildlife, including otters and ospreys. Accessible trails and hides offer viewing opportunities.

Name: Invereshie and Inshriach NNR
Description: Invereshie and Inshriach NNR spans a vast Highland landscape between Strathspey and Speyside. It features extensive Caledonian pinewoods, open moorland, montane habitats, and the River Feshie. This reserve supports rare species including capercaillie, Scottish crossbill, red squirrel, and wildcat.

Name: Inveresk Lodge Garden
Description: Explore this garden's cultivated beauty, offering diverse plant life and a green space for local wildlife.

Name: Inverewe Garden
Description: Inverewe Garden is a diverse botanical collection in the Scottish Highlands, featuring over 2,500 exotic plants and renowned rhododendron collections, cultivated from barren land.

Name: Iona
Description: Iona is a tranquil Inner Hebridean island, celebrated for its peaceful natural environments and stunning coastal landscapes.

Name: Iping and Stedham Commons
Description: Iping and Stedham Commons is a nature reserve owned and managed by the Sussex Wildlife Trust.  It is a 125.

Name: Iron Latch
Description: Iron Latch is a 4.3-hectare nature reserve in Eight Ash Green, west of Colchester in Essex.

Name: Isabella Plantation
Description: Isabella Plantation is a 40-acre ornamental woodland garden located within Richmond Park in London. It is renowned for its evergreen azaleas, rhododendrons, and other acid-loving plants. The garden features diverse seasonal displays, streams, and ponds, providing a habitat for native wildlife.

Name: Isleworth Ait
Description: Isleworth Ait is a wooded island in the River Thames near Isleworth, West London, close to where the River Crane meets the Thames. The Conservation Volunteers (TCV) supports habitat management work in the wider River Crane Project area to enhance local biodiversity and natural habitats.

Name: Isleworth Ait
Description: Isleworth Ait is a London Wildlife Trust nature reserve, and is a teardrop-shaped island in the River Thames in England, between 3.5-hectare and 9.

Name: Iver Environment Centre
Description: Iver Environment Centre, located in the Colne Valley between Uxbridge and Slough, is a 2.4-acre site featuring diverse habitats including ponds, meadows, a community orchard, woodland, and a poly tunnel rainforest. Managed by Groundwork South, it serves as a local hub for environmental education, outdoor learning, and community activities, supporting wildlife and engaging people of all ages and abilities.

Name: Ivy Hatch
Description: Ivy Hatch Nature Reserve in Ivy Hatch, north of Tonbridge in Kent, is a 0.5-hectare reserve managed by the Kent Wildlife Trust.

Name: Jackson’s Bank
Description: Jackson’s Bank is a community woodland near Swadlincote within the National Forest, featuring mixed broadleaf trees and a network of footpaths. The site offers opportunities for local residents and visitors to explore nature and enjoy woodland walks, supporting local biodiversity.

Name: Jackson's Coppice and Marsh
Description: Jackson's Coppice and Marsh is a nature reserve of the Staffordshire Wildlife Trust.  It is along the River Sow, near the village of Bishop's Offley and about 2.

Name: Jeskyns Community Woodland
Description: This expansive woodland offers a haven for diverse wildlife, from soaring birds of prey to the rustle of small mammals in the undergrowth. Miles of trails wind through ancient trees and open meadows, perfect for leisurely walks, invigorating bike rides, or simply immersing yourself in the sights and sounds of nature. Discover a vibrant ecosystem teeming with life and enjoy a refreshing escape into the great outdoors.

Name: Joe's Pond
Description: Joe's Pond is a 4-hectare Site of Special Scientific Interest that lies to the east of, and adjacent to, the Rainton Meadows nature reserve in Tyne and Wear, England.

Name: John Weston Nature Reserve
Description: John Weston Nature Reserve is a 3.6-hectare nature reserve north of Walton-on-the-Naze in Essex.

Name: Jones's Mill
Description: Jones's Mill is an 11.6 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest near Pewsey in Wiltshire, notified in 1975.

Name: Kedington Meadow
Description: Kedington Meadow is a species-rich grassland near Kedington in Suffolk, managed for its wildflowers and insects. Traditional hay cutting and grazing maintain this vital habitat. The reserve offers an important green space for local wildlife.

Name: Kelham Bridge
Description: Kelham Bridge is a 8.1 hectares nature reserve north of Ibstock in Leicestershire.

Name: Kellie Castle
Description: Nestled below the dominant Kellie Law, Kellie Castle sits amidst the rolling countryside of Fife's East Neuk.

Name: Kemsing Down
Description: Kemsing Down is a 16-hectare nature reserve north of Sevenoaks in Kent.  It is managed by the Kent Wildlife Trust.

Name: Ken-Dee Marshes
Description: Ken-Dee Marshes is an RSPB nature reserve in Dumfries and Galloway, Scotland. It features a mosaic of wetlands, woodlands, and grasslands, supporting ospreys, red kites, and other diverse wildlife. The site offers trails and hides for visitors.

Name: Kenley Common
Description: Kenley Common is a 55-hectare site in Croydon, South London. It features chalk grassland, ancient woodland, and neutral grassland, offering extensive views and supporting diverse wildlife. The common includes elements of the historic Kenley Airfield.

Name: Kennet and Avon Canal
Description: The Kennet and Avon Canal is a waterway in southern England with an overall length of 87 miles, made up of two lengths of navigable river linked by a canal.  The name is used to refer to the entire length of the navigation rather than solely to the central canal section.

Name: Kennisham Hill
Description: This expansive woodland in South East England offers a haven for nature lovers, with ancient trees forming a verdant canopy where diverse wildlife thrives. Visitors can explore miles of trails, ideal for walking and cycling, immersing themselves in the sights and sounds of a vibrant natural landscape. It's a place to connect with the wild, discover hidden glades, and breathe in the fresh country air.

Name: Kensington Gardens - The Long Water
Description: The Long Water in Kensington Gardens, shared with Hyde Park, serves as a significant bird sanctuary. It provides a haven for diverse waterfowl species including mute swans, greylag geese, and tufted ducks, supporting local wildlife populations.

Name: Kenton Common
Description: Discover a haven of ancient oak and beech woodland in the heart of South West England, where sunlight dapples through a verdant canopy, creating a truly magical atmosphere. This vibrant ecosystem teems with life, offering opportunities to spot elusive woodland birds, admire diverse fungi, and wander along peaceful trails that invite exploration by foot or bike. Immerse yourself in the sights and sounds of nature, breathing in the fresh, woodland air.

Name: Kersal Dale
Description: Kersal Dale is a local nature reserve in Salford, part of the Irwell Valley. It features diverse habitats including woodlands, grasslands, and wetlands, supporting a variety of wildlife. The site is popular for walks and nature observation.

Name: Ketford Bank
Description: Ketford Bank is a 0.69-hectare nature reserve in Gloucestershire.

Name: Ketton Quarry
Description: Ketton Quarries is a 115.6-hectare biological and geological Site of Special Scientific Interest east of Ketton in Rutland.

Name: Kew Woods
Description: Discover a haven of ancient trees and vibrant wildlife nestled in the heart of Northern England. Wander through dappled sunlight on winding paths, keeping an eye out for elusive deer and a chorus of birdsong. This expansive woodland offers tranquil spaces for walkers and cyclists to immerse themselves in the beauty of the natural world.

Name: Kidland Forest
Description: Ancient woodlands and rolling hills create a haven for diverse wildlife in this expansive North English forest. Wander through dappled sunlight, keeping an eye out for elusive forest creatures, or explore miles of trails perfect for walking and cycling adventures amidst breathtaking natural beauty. This is a place to connect with the wild heart of England.

Name: Kielder Forest
Description: Vast expanses of coniferous woodland blanket this North England landscape, creating a haven for diverse wildlife, including red squirrels and soaring birds of prey. Explore miles of trails winding through ancient trees, perfect for invigorating walks and exhilarating cycling adventures amidst breathtaking natural beauty. Immerse yourself in the tranquility and discover the rich tapestry of life that thrives within this expansive Forestry England woodland.

Name: Kilburn Woods
Description: Explore a haven of ancient trees and vibrant wildlife in this expansive Northern English woodland. Wander through dappled sunlight, listening to the chorus of birdsong, or cycle along winding trails that reveal hidden glades and breathtaking views. This Forestry England woodland offers an immersive natural experience, inviting you to connect with the beauty of the countryside and discover its diverse inhabitants.

Name: Killaloo Wood
Description: Killaloo Wood is a mature broadleaved woodland near Derry. It features a circular path, offering views of the Sperrin Mountains and the River Faughan. Species include oak, ash, and hazel, with a diverse ground flora.

Name: Killiecrankie
Description: Explore the dramatic Pass of Killiecrankie, renowned for its ancient aspen woods and the scenic River Garry flowing through this stunning gorge.

Name: Kilminorth Woods
Description: Kilminorth Woods, an ancient woodland owned by Cornwall Council, is a designated Local Nature Reserve and County Wildlife Site by the West Looe River in Cornwall. It hosts diverse flora like wild garlic and bluebells, alongside fauna such as bats, otters, roe deer, foxes, and badgers. Well-maintained walking trails provide access to the Looe Valley Line.

Name: Kiln Wood
Description: Kiln Wood is a 6-hectare nature reserve south of Lenham in Kent.  It is managed by Kent Wildlife Trust.

Name: Kinclaven Bluebell Wood
Description: Kinclaven Bluebell Wood, Perthshire, Scotland, is an ancient woodland known for its stunning bluebell displays each spring. It features native trees like oak and birch, supporting diverse wildlife. Managed by the Woodland Trust, the site offers walking routes.

Name: King Alfred's Tower
Description: Stands on Kingsettle Hill, offering expansive views across the verdant countryside of Somerset and Wiltshire.

Name: King's Forest
Description: This expansive woodland in the South East offers a rich tapestry of ancient trees and diverse habitats, providing a haven for a variety of wildlife. Visitors can explore its meandering paths and trails, perfect for invigorating walks or cycling adventures amidst the serene natural beauty. It's a place to reconnect with nature, observe wildlife in its element, and breathe in the fresh forest air.

Name: King's Meads
Description: King's Meads is a nature reserve between the towns of Hertford and Ware in Hertfordshire.  It is managed by the Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust, and with an area of 96 hectares it is the largest of the Trust's reserves.

Name: King's Wood
Description: This expansive woodland in South East England offers a haven for diverse wildlife, from ancient oaks to shy deer, creating a vibrant natural tapestry. Visitors can explore winding trails through dappled sunlight, perfect for invigorating walks or cycling adventures, immersing themselves in the sights and sounds of a thriving forest ecosystem. It's a place to reconnect with nature, breathe in fresh air, and discover the quiet beauty of the English countryside.

Name: Kings Cliff
Description: Discover a haven of ancient woodland in South East England, where towering trees create a dappled canopy and a rich tapestry of wildlife thrives. Wander scenic trails, perfect for walking and cycling, and immerse yourself in the peaceful beauty of this natural landscape, spotting diverse flora and fauna along the way. This Forestry England woodland offers a true escape into nature's embrace.

Name: Kingston Lacy
Description: Kingston Lacy boasts beautiful gardens, extensive parkland, and ancient specimen trees.

Name: Kinsley Wood
Description: Discover a haven of ancient trees and thriving wildlife in this South East England woodland. Wander through diverse habitats, from open glades to dense woodland, where you might spot deer or a variety of bird species. It's a perfect escape for walkers and cyclists to immerse themselves in the beauty of nature and breathe in the fresh, woodland air.

Name: Kintail
Description: Kintail is a stunning mountainous area at the head of Loch Duich, showcasing the dramatic landscapes of the Northwest Highlands.

Name: Kintbury Newt Ponds
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Kintbury Newt Ponds is a 3-hectare nature reserve in Kintbury in Berkshire.  It is managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Kinver Edge
Description: Kinver Edge features a high heath and woodland escarpment offering panoramic views and diverse habitats.

Name: Kinver Edge Hillfort
Description: Discover the dramatic landscape of Kinver Edge, with its rich woodlands, unique sandstone formations, and diverse wildlife.

Name: Kinver Rock Houses
Description: Explore a dramatic sandstone escarpment at Kinver Edge, revealing striking rock formations and panoramic views.

Name: Kirkby Moor
Description: Kirkby Moor is an elevated area of lowland heath, woodland and farmland in central Lincolnshire between the villages of Woodhall Spa to the west and Kirkby on Bain to the east.  Roughton Moor lies to the north and the former RAF Woodhall Spa and the Lincolnshire Fens beyond to the south.

Name: Kitchen Copse
Description: Kitchen Copse is a 7-hectare nature reserve north of Bletchingley in Surrey.  It is managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Kiveton Community Woodland
Description: Kiveton Community Woodland, a former colliery, now provides varied woodland, ponds, meadows, and paths near Kiveton Park, Sheffield. TCV South Yorkshire manages the site, offering regular volunteering opportunities for habitat creation and woodland management.

Name: Knapdale
Description: Knapdale Forest, in Argyll, Scotland, hosts a pioneering beaver reintroduction project. Visitors can explore ancient woodlands, temperate rainforest remnants, and lochside trails. The area is rich in biodiversity, offering numerous walking opportunities through diverse habitats.

Name: Knapdale Forest
Description: Knapdale Forest, a National Nature Reserve in Argyll, Scotland, hosts the Scottish Beaver Reintroduction Project. The site's diverse woodlands and lochs allow visitors to explore trails and observe beaver activity and environmental impact.

Name: Knettishall Heath
Description: Knettishall Heath is a 91.7-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest west of Knettishall in Suffolk, England.

Name: Knighton Down
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 15 hectares.

Name: Knightshayes Court
Description: Knightshayes Court's acclaimed gardens are a living landscape, rich in botanical diversity and a haven for local wildlife.

Name: Knightwood Oak
Description: This ancient woodland, a haven for wildlife in South East England, offers a tranquil escape where sunlight dapples through a canopy of majestic oak trees. Visitors can wander along winding paths, breathing in the fresh air and listening to the symphony of birdsong, or explore by bicycle, discovering hidden glades and the rich biodiversity that thrives within its embrace. It's a place to reconnect with nature, spotting diverse flora and fauna in a truly inspiring setting.

Name: Knole
Description: Knole features a sprawling 1,000-acre historic deer park, offering ancient landscapes and important wildlife habitat for its resident deer and diverse species.

Name: Knowles Mill
Description: Located in the Wyre Forest, Knowles Mill is home to notable populations of adders and wood cranesbill.

Name: Kynance Cove
Description: Kynance Cove, on the Lizard peninsula, is a breathtaking stretch of coastline, renowned for its beauty and designated a Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Lackford Lakes
Description: Lackford Lakes is a 105.8-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north and east of Lackford in Suffolk.

Name: Lady's Wood
Description: Lady's Wood is a 7.1-hectare nature reserve west of Upwood in Cambridgeshire.

Name: Ladybelt Country Park
HostOrg: East Carleton and Ketteringham Parish Council
Description: Ladybelt Country Park is an extensive area of parkland and woodland in south-west Norfolk, managed by East Carleton and Ketteringham Parish Council. It is important for its mature trees, including sweet chestnut coppice, and supports a variety of birds and invertebrates. The park offers waymarked routes for enjoyable walks and has a car park.

Name: Ladywalk Nature Reserve
Description: Ladywalk Nature Reserve is a wildlife haven situated in the Tame Valley, near Birmingham, and managed by the West Midland Bird Club. It encompasses diverse habitats including wetlands, pools, and reedbeds, supporting a wide array of bird species, notably wintering Eurasian Bittern. Access to the reserve is restricted to members of the West Midland Bird Club or by permit.

Name: Ladywalk Reserve
Description: Ladywalk Reserve, a 51-hectare nature reserve in Warwickshire's Tame Valley, is managed by the West Midland Bird Club. It features diverse habitats like pools, marshland, and reedbeds, supporting a variety of bird species. Hides offer viewing access.

Name: Ladywell Fields
Description: Ladywell Fields features over 1000m of river restoration work on the Ravensbourne, including naturalisation and new backwater channels. This increases biodiversity by creating habitats for fish, invertebrates, and plants. Volunteers maintain the river and its banks.

Name: Lambert's Castle
Description: Lambert's Castle SSSI sits atop a high hill with steep natural slopes, renowned for its geology and ecology and benefiting from habitat conservation.

Name: Landford Bog
Description: Landford Bog is an 11.6 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest at Landford in southeast Wiltshire, England.

Name: Laneskin Wood
Description: Discover a vibrant tapestry of ancient oaks and native trees in this expansive woodland, a haven for diverse wildlife. Wander through sun-dappled paths, perfect for exploring on foot or by bike, and immerse yourself in the sights and sounds of nature. Keep an eye out for woodland birds and the subtle signs of other creatures that call this beautiful corner of South West England home.

Name: Lang Craigs
Description: Lang Craigs is a Woodland Trust site within the Kilpatrick Hills, featuring ancient oakwoods, grassland, and newly planted areas. It offers a network of paths with views over the Clyde and Dumbarton Rock, providing accessible walks for wildlife enthusiasts.

Name: Langdon Nature Reserve
Description: Langdon Nature Reserve is a 210 hectare nature reserve west of Basildon in Essex.  It is managed by the Essex Wildlife Trust, and forms part of the Langdon Ridge Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Langford Heathfield
Description: Langford Heathfield is a 95.4 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest at Langford Budville, 3 km north west of Wellington in Somerset, notified in 1966.

Name: Langstone Harbour
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Langstone Harbour is a 2,085.4-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Hampshire.

Name: Lanhydrock House
Description: Lanhydrock offers extensive grounds, including formal gardens and a hillside planted with a fine selection of shrubs and trees, overlooking the River Fowey.

Name: Lardon Chase, the Holies and Lough Down
Description: An outstanding area of downland, woodland, and one of Berkshire's largest chalk grasslands, supporting diverse chalk-loving plant species with sweeping views.

Name: Lashford Lane Fen
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Lashford Lane Fen is a 7-hectare nature reserve north of Dry Sandford in Oxfordshire.  It is managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Lassington Wood
HostOrg: Tewkesbury Borough Council and Highnam Parish Council
Description: Lassington Wood is a mature, mixed woodland nature reserve near Highnam, Gloucestershire. Historically part of the Guise family estate since the 13th century, it was acquired by Gloucester County Borough Council in 1921. It is now managed jointly by Tewkesbury Borough Council and Highnam Parish Council. The wood is renowned for its spectacular display of bluebells in spring and features a network of public footpaths. It was also formerly home to the notable Lassington Oak.

Name: Launde Woods
Description: Launde Woods is a 99 hectares nature reserve north of Launde in Leicestershire.  It is owned by the Leicester Diocesan Board of Finance and leased to the Leicestershire and Rutland Wildlife Trust.

Name: Lavender Pond Nature Park
Description: Lavender Pond Nature Park, part of Russia Dock Woodlands in Rotherhithe, Southwark, is a peaceful oasis, formerly a working dock. It features woodland, meadows, and ponds, providing vital habitats for diverse wildlife. Conservation tasks and wildlife surveys occur regularly.

Name: Lavington Common
Description: Lavington Common offers a mosaic of wet and dry heath, acid grassland, and woodlands, renowned for its rich community of invertebrates, including spiders.

Name: Lawrence Weston Moor
Description: Lawrence Weston is a post-war housing estate in northwest Bristol, England, between Henbury and Shirehampton.  The estate is bounded in the east by the Blaise Castle estate and woods.

Name: Laymoor Quag
Description: Laymoor Quag is a 3.5-hectare nature reserve within the Forest of Dean in Gloucestershire.

Name: Lea Meadows
Description: Lea Meadows is a 12-hectare nature reserve east of Markfield in Leicestershire.  It is owned and managed by the Leicestershire and Rutland Wildlife Trust.

Name: Lee Navigation Reedbeds
Description: Lee Navigation Reedbeds, near Tottenham Hale, are artificial floating reedbeds created to improve water quality and increase biodiversity. They provide crucial habitats for wildlife in an urban waterway setting. This project enhances ecological resilience.

Name: Leigh Woods
Description: This Avon Gorge woodland shelters rare Sorbus trees and unique Bristol rockcress, showcasing exceptional biodiversity and landscape beauty.

Name: Leigh Woods
Description: This expansive woodland, managed by Forestry England, offers a haven of ancient trees and diverse habitats teeming with wildlife. Visitors can explore winding trails perfect for walking and cycling, immersing themselves in the sights and sounds of nature, from elusive birdsong to the rustle of unseen creatures in the undergrowth. It's a place to connect with the natural world, breathe fresh air, and discover the beauty of a thriving woodland ecosystem.

Name: Leith Hall
Description: Explore the expansive 286-acre estate of Leith Hall, featuring diverse gardens and surrounding landscapes in Aberdeenshire.

Name: Leith Hill
Description: Leith Hill is the highest point of the Greensand Ridge, surrounded by extensive woodlands designated as a Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Lemsford Springs
Description: Lemsford Springs is a 4 hectare nature reserve in Lemsford, Hertfordshire, England.  It is managed by the Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust, which purchased the site in 1970.

Name: Letcombe Valley
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Letcombe Valley is a 7.5-hectare nature reserve south of Letcombe Regis in Oxfordshire.

Name: Levant Mine & Beam Engine
Description: Explore dramatic coastal cliffs and the South West Coast Path, offering stunning views and linking to Botallack Mine.

Name: Levin Down
Description: Levin Down is a 25.6-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south of Midhurst in West Sussex.

Name: Levington Lagoon
Description: Levington Lagoon is a 5 hectare nature reserve south-east of Levington in Suffolk.  It is owned by Suffolk Yacht Harbour Ltd and managed by the Suffolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Lewesdon Hill
Description: Lewesdon Hill is Dorset's highest point, offering expansive views across the significant Dorset National Landscape.

Name: Lexden Gathering Grounds
Description: Lexden Gathering Grounds is an 8.9-hectare nature reserve in Lexden, a suburb of Colchester in Essex.

Name: Leyburn Old Glebe
Description: Leyburn Old Glebe Nature Reserve is a nature reserve and Site of Special Scientific Interest managed by the Yorkshire Wildlife Trust.  It is about 440 yards east of the village of Wensley and 0.

Name: Leyton Jubilee Park
Description: Leyton Jubilee Park hosts the Waltham Forest Green Gym, offering weekly conservation tasks. Activities include tree and shrub maintenance, gardening, habitat management, and litter picking, suitable for all abilities.

Name: Lightwater Country Park
Description: Lightwater Country Park, owned by Surrey Heath Borough Council, encompasses heathland, woodland, and grassland. Its heathland sections, part of the Thames Basin Heaths Special Protection Area, protect ground-nesting birds. The site is open to the public.

Name: Ligoniel Dams & Park
Description: Ligoniel Dams and Park is an urban oasis in north Belfast, managed by the Belfast Hills Partnership. Two man-made dams, fed by the Ligoneil River, support waterbirds and amphibians. Walking paths explore former printworks and mill race remains.

Name: Limekiln Wood Nature Reserve
Description: Limekiln Wood Nature Reserve is a 13.1-hectare nature reserve in Cheshire, England, north of the village of Mow Cop.

Name: Lincomb Fish Pass
Description: Lincomb Fish Pass, near Stourport-on-Severn on the River Severn, aids migrating fish like salmon and eels in bypassing Lincomb Weir. Part of the Unlocking the Severn project, it uses a Larinier super active baffle design for easier upstream passage.

Name: Lindean Loch
Description: Lindean Loch is a shallow loch in a natural hollow, surrounded by sedge and reed swamp, with open water. It supports diverse bird life, including wildfowl and waders, acting as an important breeding ground. The site is a Site of Special Scientific Interest, with limited visitor access.

Name: Lindisfarne Castle
Description: Explore the unique coastal landscape of this tidal island, famed for its dynamic causeway access and rich marine environment.

Name: Lindisfarne National Nature Reserve
Description: Lindisfarne National Nature Reserve is a 3,541-hectare UK national nature reserve located on Holy Island, a tidal island off the Northumberland coast. Managed by Natural England, it safeguards internationally important wintering bird populations, including pale-bellied brent geese, pink-footed geese, and wigeons. The reserve encompasses diverse habitats such as sand dunes, intertidal mudflats, rocky shores, and salt marshes, making it a Ramsar site of international significance.

Name: Lindsey House
Description: Lindsey House features Grade II listed gardens, a green oasis providing respite in urban Chelsea.

Name: Lineover Wood
Description: Lineover Wood is an ancient woodland on the Cotswold scarp, featuring mature beech and ash trees. It is home to diverse wildlife, including various bird species and dormice. The site offers walking trails and scenic views over the surrounding countryside.

Name: Linhope Spout
Description: Linhope Spout is a waterfall located within Northumberland National Park, North East England. It currently hosts a temperate rainforest pilot project. This initiative focuses on restoring and expanding vital rainforest habitats around the spout and the adjacent Bizzle Burn.

Name: Linn of Tummel
Description: Woodlands at the confluence of the Rivers Garry and Tummel, supporting pine martens, otters, and diverse flora.

Name: Lion Creek and Lower Raypits
Description: Lion Creek and Lower Raypits is a 65.2-hectare nature reserve east of Canewdon in Essex.

Name: Lion Pit
Description: Lion Pit is a 2.5-hectare geological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Grays in Essex.

Name: Lippets Grove
Description: Lippets Grove is a 5-hectare nature reserve in Gloucestershire.  The site was leased from the Forestry Commission in 1987 and is managed by the Gloucestershire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Litlington White Horse
Description: Explore this striking chalk hill within the South Downs, offering expansive views over the Cuckmere River valley and its unique downland habitat.

Name: Little Haven
Description: Little Haven is a 37.2-hectare nature reserve in Thundersley in Essex, England.

Name: Little Linford Wood
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Little Linford Wood is a 42.5-hectare nature reserve in Little Linford in the City of Milton Keynes, Buckinghamshire, England.

Name: Little Moreton Hall
Description: Discover the restored historic gardens and wildlife-rich moat surrounding this distinctive Cheshire property.

Name: Little Waltham Meadows
Description: Little Waltham Meadows is an 8.9-hectare nature reserve south of Little Waltham in Essex.

Name: Littlefield Common
Description: Littlefield Common is a 17-hectare nature reserve south-west of Worplesdon in Surrey.  It is owned by Surrey County Council and managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Lloyd Park
Description: Lloyd Park in Walthamstow, London, is a Green Flag Award-winning park and a designated Local Wildlife Site, featuring woodland, a medieval ornamental moat, and diverse habitats supporting birds and bats. The TCV (The Conservation Volunteers) Green Gym meets weekly here, engaging volunteers in practical conservation tasks such as tree planting, wildflower meadow maintenance, wetland management, and habitat creation, offering free outdoor exercise and contributing to the park's biodiversity.

Name: Llyn Tegid (Bala Lake)
Description: Llyn Tegid (Bala Lake) is Wales' largest natural lake, found within Snowdonia National Park, Gwynedd. This glacial lake is a Special Area of Conservation, known for its clear waters and rare gwyniad fish, supporting diverse habitats.

Name: Llyn Tegid NNR
Description: Llyn Tegid (Bala Lake) is Wales’ largest natural lake. A National Nature Reserve (NNR) protecting rare wildlife like the gwyniad fish, it is popular for water sports, walking, and its scenic railway.

Name: Llyn y Fan Fach
Description: Llyn y Fan Fach is a stunning glacial lake on Mynydd Du, within Bannau Brycheiniog National Park. It is considered the southernmost montane lake in the UK, surrounded by moorland and home to unique aquatic flora and fauna. The site supports important bird species.

Name: Loch Arkaig Pine Forest
Description: Loch Arkaig Pine Forest is a surviving fragment of ancient Caledonian Forest in the Scottish Highlands. The site features ancient Scots pine, hosting diverse wildlife including red squirrels, pine martens, and ospreys. Woodland Trust and Arkaig Community Forest manage the area for conservation.

Name: Loch Fleet
Description: Loch Fleet is a large, shallow, tidal basin and National Nature Reserve in Sutherland, Scotland. The site features saltmarsh, dunes, coastal heath, and pine woods. It provides habitat for wading birds, wildfowl, otters, seals, and ospreys.

Name: Loch Garten Nature Centre
Description: Loch Garten Nature Centre is within RSPB Abernethy, a significant Caledonian pinewood in the Cairngorms National Park. It is renowned for returning ospreys, red squirrels, capercaillie, and crested tits, offering visitor viewing facilities.

Name: Loch Gruinart
Description: Loch Gruinart is an RSPB nature reserve on Islay, known for its diverse birdlife including wintering barnacle geese. The reserve features wetlands, woodlands, and farmland habitats, offering hides for wildlife viewing and marked walking trails.

Name: Loch Leven National Nature Reserve
Description: Loch Leven NNR, a freshwater loch in Perth and Kinross, Scotland, is a vital wintering ground and breeding site for wildfowl and birds. It serves as a crucial migratory stopover for many bird populations. NatureScot manages this important wetland.

Name: Loch Lomond
Description: RSPB Loch Lomond reserve protects vital habitats on Scotland's largest freshwater loch. It supports diverse wildlife, including geese, ducks, and waders. Visitors can explore trails, hides, and learn about conservation at the Nature Hub.

Name: Loch of Kinnordy
HostOrg: Royal Society for the Protection of Birds
Description: Loch of Kinnordy is a shallow freshwater loch and fen wetland in Strathmore, Scotland. It supports breeding and wintering wildfowl and waders like osprey, pintail, and whooper swans. The fen and reedbeds provide habitat for rare plants and insects.

Name: Loch of Spiggie
Description: Loch of Spiggie is a large freshwater loch in south-west Mainland Shetland. It is important for wintering wildfowl, including wigeon, teal, mallard, pintail, tufted duck, pochard, and whooper swans. Surrounding habitats feature reedbeds and fen areas. The site is notable for great northern divers and Slavonian grebes, managed by RSPB.

Name: Loch of Strathbeg
Description: Loch of Strathbeg is Scotland's largest coastal wetland, situated in Aberdeenshire. It serves as a crucial wintering ground for thousands of migrating wildfowl, including geese, swans, and ducks. The reserve features diverse habitats like reeds, dunes, and farmland.

Name: Loch of the Lowes
Description: Loch of the Lowes is a loch near Dunkeld in Perth and Kinross, Scotland.  The loch and the surrounding area are designated as a wildlife reserve, run by the Scottish Wildlife Trust.

Name: Loch Ruthven
Description: Loch Ruthven is a remote, tranquil upland freshwater loch in the Scottish Highlands. It hosts over a quarter of the UK's Slavonian grebe population, which breed here each spring before moving to sea for winter. The site is an important habitat for these birds.

Name: Lochwinnoch
Description: RSPB Lochwinnoch is a nature reserve in West Scotland, situated on the shores of Castle Semple Loch. It features open water, reedbed, and wet woodland habitats, supporting diverse wildlife. Visitors can use nature trails, bird hides, and a visitor centre.

Name: Loddon Nature Reserve
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 14 hectares.

Name: Lodge Park and Sherborne Estate
Description: Explore the expansive open landscape of the Sherborne Estate, offering public footpaths and potential wildlife encounters.

Name: Loggans Moor
Description: Loggans Moor is a nature reserve and Site of Special Scientific Interest, noted for its biological characteristics, in west Cornwall, England, UK.  It is located 1 mile north-east of the town of Hayle, off the A30 road.

Name: Lolly Moor
Description: Lolly Moor is a 3-hectare nature reserve south of Dereham in Norfolk.  It is managed by the Norfolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Long Deans
Description: Long Deans is a 15 hectare nature reserve managed by the Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust in Nash Mills, between Kings Langley and Hemel Hempstead in Hertfordshire.  It is neutral and chalk grassland and woodland with beech, ash, oak and wild cherry.

Name: Long Dole Wood and Meadows SSSI
Description: Long Dole Wood and Meadows SSSI is a 9.8 hectares biological Site of Special Scientific Interest between the villages of Farrington Gurney and Hinton Blewitt in Bath and North East Somerset, notified in 1987.

Name: Long Grove Wood
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Long Grove Wood is a 1.5-hectare nature reserve managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust in Seer Green in Buckinghamshire.

Name: Longburnford Quarry
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 1 hectares.

Name: Longford River, Bushy Park
Description: The Longford River is a man-made watercourse, constructed in the 1630s to supply water to Hampton Court Palace. It flows through Bushy Park, feeding ponds and water gardens before reaching the palace grounds. It supports diverse wildlife and habitats.

Name: Longshaw Estate
Description: Explore Longshaw Estate's diverse landscapes of moorland, woodland, and farmland, offering rich wildlife habitats within the stunning Peak District National Park.

Name: Longspring Wood
Description: Longspring Wood is a 1.2-hectare nature reserve managed by the Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust in Kings Langley in Hertfordshire.

Name: Lord's Lot Forest
Description: This expansive woodland in Northern England offers a haven for diverse wildlife amidst ancient trees and rolling hills. Visitors can wander through peaceful trails, breathe in the fresh, earthy air, and discover the rich tapestry of nature unfolding around them. It's a perfect place for leisurely walks or invigorating cycles, immersing oneself in the beauty and tranquility of the natural landscape.

Name: Lough Foyle
Description: Lough Foyle is a large, shallow estuary on the border of Northern Ireland, internationally important for wintering wildfowl and wading birds. It provides vital feeding and roosting grounds for species like whooper swans and light-bellied brent geese.

Name: Lough Foyle Native Oyster Recovery
Description: Lough Foyle, Northern Ireland, hosts a native oyster recovery project. It reintroduces oysters to restore populations, enhance marine biodiversity, and improve water quality within the lough's ecosystem, working with local communities.

Name: Loughborough Big Meadow
Description: Loughborough Meadows is a 60.5 hectares biological Site of Special Scientific Interest on the northern outskirts of Loughborough in Leicestershire, England.

Name: Lound Lakes
Description: Lound Lakes is a 113 hectares nature reserve and series of reservoirs on the border between the English counties of Norfolk and Suffolk.  It is 2 miles south-west of Gorleston-on-Sea, 5 miles north-west of Lowestoft and around 1.

Name: Love Your River Cole
Description: The Love Your River Cole project improves a 2.5km stretch of the River Cole within Birmingham's Kingfisher Country Park, specifically in the Shard End and Stechford areas. It focuses on enhancing river access, boosting biodiversity, and offering community engagement opportunities. The project is managed by the Tame Valley Wetlands Landscape Partnership.

Name: Low Barns
Description: Witton-le-Wear is a Site of Special Scientific Interest located in the valley of the River Wear, immediately east of the village of Witton-le-Wear in County Durham, England.  It is important as the only extensive body of biologically significant open water in West Durham.

Name: Lower Common
Description: Lower Common near Verwood, Dorset, is a 30-hectare nature reserve. It features mixed woodland, coniferous plantations, and wet and dry heathland. The site supports nightjar, woodcock, sand lizard, and smooth snake. Grazing ponies maintain habitats.

Name: Lower Lough Erne Islands
Description: Lower Lough Erne Islands, located in County Fermanagh, Northern Ireland, comprise numerous small islands and the mainland site of Hare Island. This site is a stronghold for breeding waders, particularly curlews. Conservation efforts focus on managing grazing and scrub to maintain suitable habitats.

Name: Lower Test
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Lower Test Valley is a 142-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest near Totton in Hampshire.  It is part of Solent and Southampton Water Ramsar site and Special Protection Area, and of Solent Maritime Special Area of Conservation.

Name: Lower Wood, Ashwellthorpe
Description: Lower Wood, Ashwellthorpe is a 37.9-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south-east of Wymondham in Norfolk, England.

Name: Lower Woods
Description: Lower Woods is a 280.1-hectare biological and geological Site of Special Scientific Interest near the village of Wickwar, South Gloucestershire, notified in 1966 and renotified in 1985.

Name: Lower Wye Gorge SSSI
Description: Lower Wye Gorge is a 65-hectare biological and geological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Gloucestershire, notified in 1954 and renotified 1987.  The site includes two Gloucestershire Wildlife Trust nature reserves being Ban-y-gor Wood and Lancaut.

Name: Loynton Moss
Description: Loynton Moss is a nature reserve of the Staffordshire Wildlife Trust, near the village of Woodseaves, in Staffordshire, England.  It is adjacent to the Shropshire Union Canal, as it runs from nearby Norbury to High Offley.

Name: Lucas Marsh
Description: Lucas Marsh is a 1.5 hectare Local Nature Reserve in Oadby in Leicestershire.

Name: Ludshott Common and Waggoners Wells
Description: Ludshott Common offers expansive heathland, while Waggoners Wells provides tranquil ponds and a stream, creating diverse habitats.

Name: Ludwell Valley Park
Description: Ludwell Valley Park is wildlife-focused public park in Exeter, Devon, United Kingdom.  The park is owned by Exeter City Council and managed by Devon Wildlife Trust.

Name: Lullingstone Country Park
Description: Lullingstone Country Park is a Green Flag award-winning park near Eynsford, Kent. It is internationally important for its collection of ancient trees, including over 300 veteran oak, beech, ash, hornbeam, and sweet chestnut, some estimated to be 800 years old. The park features chalk grasslands with spectacular displays of orchids and other wildflowers, supporting diverse wildlife. The River Darent flows through the park, and the Darent Valley Path offers walking routes and scenic views. It is owned and managed by Kent County Council.

Name: Lundy
Description: This steep, rocky island in the Bristol Channel boasts a rich bird life, lying on major migration routes and hosting many vagrant species.

Name: Lydden Meadows
Description: Lydden Meadows, also known as RSPB Lydden Valley Reserve or Worth Marshes, is a Kent nature reserve managed by the RSPB. It features damp meadows, ditches, and woodland, with ongoing work to create new scrapes and wetlands. It provides habitat for diverse wildlife, including a nationally important population of the rare marsh fritillary butterfly, waders, and wildfowl. Public access is limited to existing public footpaths.

Name: Lydden Temple Ewell
Description: Lydden and Temple Ewell Downs is a 63.2-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north-west of Dover in Kent.

Name: Lydford Forest
Description: This ancient woodland in the heart of Devon offers a haven for diverse wildlife, from soaring birds of prey to shy woodland mammals. Wander through a tapestry of mature trees, explore winding trails perfect for walking and cycling, and immerse yourself in the serene beauty of this vibrant natural landscape.
