It's a place to connect with the wild, breathing in the fresh air and discovering the hidden wonders of the South West.

Name: Lydford Gorge
Description: Experience the deepest river gorge in South West England, carved by the River Lyd through the dramatic Dartmoor landscape.

Name: Lyme Park
Description: Lyme Park features an extensive deer park, a haven for wildlife, set amidst the dramatic landscapes of the Peak District National Park.

Name: Lymington and Keyhaven Marshes
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Lymington and Keyhaven Marshes is a 738-hectare nature reserve which stretches from Keyhaven along the south coast across the Lymington River in Hampshire.  It is managed by the Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust.

Name: Lymington Reedbeds
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Lymington River Reedbeds is a 41.7-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Lymington in Hampshire.

Name: Lynford Arboretum
Description: This beautiful Forestry England woodland in the heart of the Midlands offers a tranquil escape into nature. Wander through diverse trees, listen to the songs of abundant birdlife, and keep an eye out for elusive mammals. It's a perfect place for walkers and cyclists to immerse themselves in the sights and sounds of the natural world.

Name: Lynford Stag
Description: Discover a vibrant tapestry of ancient woodland and open heathland, teeming with diverse wildlife like soaring birds of prey and elusive deer. Miles of winding paths invite exploration on foot or by bike, offering immersive experiences amidst the sights and sounds of nature. This expansive forest provides a sanctuary for both quiet contemplation and active adventure.

Name: Lynford Water
Description: This expansive woodland in the heart of the Midlands offers a haven for wildlife, with ancient trees providing a canopy for diverse birdlife and a tranquil setting for walkers and cyclists. Explore winding trails that reveal hidden glades and open spaces, perfect for immersing yourself in nature and spotting elusive woodland creatures. It's a place to connect with the natural world, breathe in fresh air, and enjoy the simple pleasures of the great outdoors.

Name: Lytes Cary Manor
Description: Explore tranquil Arts and Crafts gardens set within a gentle, sunny Somerset landscape surrounding Lytes Cary Manor.

Name: Lyveden New Bield
Description: Explore a tranquil Elizabethan landscape featuring moats, ancient woodlands, and traditional orchards, providing a rich haven for diverse wildlife.

Name: Mab Lane Community Woodland
Description: Mab Lane Community Woodland is a 1.5-hectare site in Liverpool, established around 2008-2010 as part of Liverpool's Capital of Culture year. It features native trees and shrubs, wildflower meadows, a community orchard, and seasonal wetland areas, creating valuable wildlife habitats. The woodland offers walking paths and green space for local residents to enjoy nature and was developed through a partnership including The Mersey Forest and Woodland Trust.

Name: Macclesfield Forest
Description: Macclesfield Forest is an upland woodland and reservoir complex on the western edge of the Peak District, Cheshire. Owned and primarily managed by United Utilities, with a section including Trentabank Reservoir managed as a nature reserve by Cheshire Wildlife Trust, it features diverse habitats including conifer plantations and broadleaf woodlands, supporting varied wildlife such as red deer and a large heronry.

Name: Maer Lake
Description: Maer Lake is a nature reserve adjacent to Bude, in Cornwall, England.  It is a wetland meadow with open water, and is an important site for over-wintering birds.

Name: Magog Down
Description: Magog Down is 163.5 acres of former arable land on the Gog Magog Hills, south of Cambridge. Transformed since 1989, it is now a habitat for wildlife, supports species diversity, and offers quiet recreation and educational visits.

Name: Magor Marsh
Description: Magor Marsh is a 36-hectare wetland reserve, located on the Welsh side of the Severn Estuary.  It is managed by the Gwent Wildlife Trust.

Name: Maldon Wick
Description: Maldon Wick is a 6.1-hectare nature reserve in Maldon in Essex.

Name: Malham Tarn Estate
Description: This Pennine estate features a glacial lake, internationally important wetlands, and woodlands, designated a National Nature Reserve for its diverse wildlife.

Name: Mallards Pike
Description: This expansive woodland offers a haven for diverse wildlife, from soaring birds of prey to shy woodland mammals, thriving amidst ancient trees and open glades. Visitors can immerse themselves in nature by exploring winding walking trails, enjoying scenic cycling routes, and simply soaking in the tranquil atmosphere of this beautiful natural landscape. It's a place where the rustling leaves and the calls of wildlife create a truly unforgettable outdoor experience.

Name: Malleny House and Garden
Description: Malleny Garden boasts ancient yew trees and Scotland's national collection of heritage shrub roses, a botanical treasure trove southwest of Edinburgh.

Name: Malling Down
Description: Malling Down is an 85-hectare nature reserve on the eastern outskirts of Lewes in East Sussex.  It is managed by the Sussex Wildlife Trust.

Name: Malton NR
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 5 hectares.

Name: Mamhead
Description: This ancient woodland in the heart of South West England offers a haven for diverse wildlife, from woodland birds to elusive deer, amidst a tapestry of mature trees. Visitors can explore winding trails that invite leisurely walks and invigorating cycles, immersing themselves in the sights and sounds of a thriving natural environment. It's a place to connect with nature, breathe in the fresh air, and discover the subtle beauty of the forest.

Name: Manor Farm
Description: Manor Farm is a 25-hectare nature reserve in Byfleet, Surrey.  It is owned and managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Mapledurwell Fen and the Hatch
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 3 hectares.

Name: Mar Lodge
Description: A jewel of the Cairngorms, Mar Lodge Estate protects ancient pine forests, rugged mountains, and a haven for diverse Scottish wildlife.

Name: Mar Lodge Estate
Description: Mar Lodge Estate is an immensely important conservation landscape within the Cairngorms, featuring magnificent mountains, glacial valleys, and the headwaters of the River Dee.

Name: Marbury Reedbed Nature Reserve
Description: Marbury Reedbed Nature Reserve is a 6-hectare nature reserve located at the western end of Budworth Mere, north of Northwich, Cheshire, England.  It is managed by the Cheshire Wildlife Trust under lease from the Royal Society for Nature Conservation, which purchased the land by public subscription in 1934 as a memorial to the Cheshire naturalist Thomas Coward.

Name: Marden Meadow
Description: Marden Meadows is a 3.7-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest east of Marden in Kent.

Name: Marden Park
Description: Marden Park is a scenic valley reserve near Woldingham, featuring ancient woodland and chalk grassland. Home to pyramidal orchids and common blue butterflies, the site offers extensive views and supports diverse wildlife habitats. Managed for conservation.

Name: Mardyke Woods
Description: Venture into this beautiful South East England woodland and discover a haven for diverse wildlife, from woodland birds to shy mammals. Explore winding paths and trails that invite you to wander through ancient trees, soak in the peaceful atmosphere, and connect with nature. Whether you're seeking a gentle stroll or an invigorating cycle, this Forestry England woodland offers a refreshing escape into the heart of the countryside.

Name: Market Weston Fen
Description: Weston Fen is a 49.7-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Hopton in Suffolk.

Name: Marks Hall
Description: Markshall Estate is a charitable trust near Coggeshall, Essex, featuring ancient woodlands, ponds, and meadows. It manages its own conservation efforts, supporting diverse wildlife, including various bird species, bats, and invertebrates. Visitors can explore walking trails through different habitats, including an arboretum and walled garden.

Name: Marks Hall Estate
Description: Marks Hall Estate in Essex features an internationally important arboretum, ancient woodlands, and a historic walled garden. The site encompasses lakes, botanical collections, and is designated as a Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Markstakes Common
Description: Markstakes Common, owned by the Woodland Trust, is an ancient woodland and heathland site in Chailey, East Sussex. Its mosaic of habitats supports diverse flora and fauna. The common is actively managed for conservation.

Name: Marline Valley
Description: Marline Valley Woods is a 55.1-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest on the western outskirts of Hastings in East Sussex.

Name: Marsden Moor Estate
Description: Vast South Pennine moorland, featuring rugged valleys, peaks, and crags, supports significant populations of moorland birds like golden plover and curlew.

Name: Marsland Valley
Description: Marsland Valley is a nature reserve situated in two large valleys which straddle the northern end of the Devon-Cornwall border.  It is a designated nature reserve jointly managed by the Devon Wildlife Trust and the Cornwall Wildlife Trust.

Name: Martham Broad
Description: Martham Broad is a 60-hectare national nature reserve north of Great Yarmouth in Norfolk.  It is managed by the Norfolk Wildlife Trust, and is part of the Upper Thurne Broads and Marshes Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Martins' Meadows
Description: Monewden Meadows is a 3.7-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south-west of Monewden in Suffolk.

Name: Martlesham Wilds
Description: Martlesham Wilds is a nature reserve of Suffolk Wildlife Trust, a rewilding site on the banks of the River Deben near Martlesham in Suffolk, England.  It is designated a Ramsar site, and a Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Maryculter Community Woods
Description: Maryculter Community Woods is a woodland reserve near Maryculter, 10 miles west of Aberdeen, managed by the Maryculter Woodlands Trust. It features Scots pine, birch, and oak, supporting tits, finches, woodpeckers, and red squirrels. A network of paths allows for walks through the site, situated on the south side of the River Dee valley.

Name: Matlock Moors
Description: This expansive woodland in the Midlands offers a haven for diverse wildlife, with ancient trees forming a dappled canopy over winding paths. Visitors can immerse themselves in nature, enjoying invigorating walks or cycles through the serene landscape, spotting woodland birds and other creatures. It's a place to connect with the natural world and breathe in the fresh, forest air.

Name: Max Bog
Description: Max Bog is a 10.6 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in North Somerset, notified in 1988.

Name: May Hill, Gloucestershire
Description: This prominent hill, distinguished by its summit trees, is also an important Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Mayesbrook Park
HostOrg: London Borough of Barking and Dagenham
Description: Thames21 transforms Mayes Brook Park into an urban wetland, improving water quality, enhancing biodiversity, and increasing flood resilience. This project creates new green spaces for the local Barking community.

Name: Maze Park Nature Reserve
Description: Maze Park is a 42-acre urban nature reserve in Middlesbrough, England on the south bank of the Tees on part of the former Tees Marshalling Yard.  It was created by the Teesside Development Corporation and is owned and run by the Tees Valley Wildlife Trust.

Name: Meddon Plantation
Description: This sprawling Forestry England woodland in the South West offers a haven for wildlife, with ancient trees providing a canopy for diverse birdlife and a peaceful habitat for woodland creatures. Visitors can immerse themselves in nature, enjoying tranquil walks and invigorating cycles through its scenic beauty, discovering the rich biodiversity at every turn. It's a place to connect with the natural world, breathing in the fresh air and experiencing the restorative power of the forest.

Name: Mellis Common
Description: Mellis Common is a 59 hectare nature reserve in Mellis in Suffolk.  It is managed by the Suffolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Mereway Nature Park and Orchard
Description: Mereway Nature Park and Orchard is one of several West London sites where The Conservation Volunteers Biodiversity Action Teams improve wildlife habitats. Activities include tree and hedge planting, woodland management, and pond work.

Name: Merry's Meadows
Description: Merry's Meadows is a 12.4-hectare nature reserve west of Stretton in Rutland.

Name: Mersehead
Description: RSPB Mersehead is a wetland reserve on the Solway Coast in Dumfries and Galloway, Scotland. It hosts a significant wintering population of barnacle geese. The reserve features saltmarsh, wetlands, and farmland, with hides available for wildlife observation.

Name: Merthyr Mawr NNR
Description: Merthyr Mawr National Nature Reserve is a vast area of sand dunes in South Wales, featuring the second-highest dune in Europe, known as the 'Big Dipper'. This diverse landscape includes coastal habitats, woodland, and the River Ogmore, supporting a variety of rare plants and wildlife, including specialist dune species.

Name: Micheldever Wood
Description: This expansive Forestry England woodland in South East England offers a haven of ancient trees and diverse habitats, alive with the sights and sounds of wildlife. Explore miles of trails winding through dappled sunlight, perfect for walking and cycling amidst the natural beauty, or simply find a quiet spot to observe the woodland's inhabitants. It's a place to reconnect with nature and discover the rich tapestry of life within its leafy embrace.

Name: Mickfield Meadow
Description: Mickfield Meadow is a 1.9-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north of Mickfield in Suffolk.

Name: Mickle Mere
Description: Mickle Mere is a 17-hectare nature reserve south of Ixworth in Suffolk.  It is managed by the Suffolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Middlebriars Wood
Description: Middlebriars Wood is a 1-hectare nature reserve in Hurtmore, west of Farncombe in Surrey.  It is managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Middlethorpe Hall
Description: Middlethorpe Hall is nestled within 20 acres of grounds, contributing valuable green space.

Name: Midger
Description: Midger is a 65.7-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest straddling the border of Gloucestershire and South Gloucestershire, notified in 1966 and renotified in 1984.

Name: Milborne Port Community Conservation
Description: Milborne Port Community Conservation manages local green spaces, enhancing biodiversity and creating wildlife habitats. The team organises tree planting and other ecological projects, collaborating with local residents and volunteers.

Name: Mildenhall Warren
Description: This extensive woodland in South East England offers a haven for diverse wildlife amidst a landscape of mature trees and open heathland. Visitors can explore miles of trails, ideal for walking and cycling, immersing themselves in the sights and sounds of nature. It's a place to discover the beauty of the English countryside and encounter a variety of flora and fauna.

Name: Mile End Park
Description: Mile End Park is a 32-hectare linear park in East London, created on former industrial land and a WWII bomb site. It features an Ecology Park, Children's Park, and sports facilities. The Eco Pavilion serves as an educational and community hub within the park.

Name: Milford Cutting
Description: Milford Cuttings is a former railway line near Lough Neagh, now a nature reserve managed by Ulster Wildlife. It features diverse wildflowers and grasses, supporting a range of insects and birds. The site provides a valuable wildlife corridor and a quiet space for visitors.

Name: Milford Green and Coxhill Green
Description: Milford Green and Coxhill Green is a 15-hectare nature reserve south-east of Chobham in Surrey.  It is owned by Surrey County Council and managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Milkwellburn Wood
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 79 hectares.

Name: Mill Dam
Description: Mill Dam on Shapinsay is an RSPB reserve featuring a small freshwater loch and adjacent marshland. It provides a vital breeding and feeding ground for a variety of wetland birds, including lapwings, redshanks, and waders. The site is important for local biodiversity.

Name: Mill Meadows
Description: Mill Meadows, Billericay, is a diverse nature reserve in Essex, featuring ancient unimproved grassland, woodland, and a pond. This site supports a rich variety of wildflowers, butterflies, and birds, including scarce species. It is actively managed to preserve its unique habitats and biodiversity.

Name: Millennium Country Park, Forest of Marston Vale
Description: Millennium Country Park, part of the Forest of Marston Vale, features extensive wetlands, lakes, and woodlands. Visitors can explore 8km of trails, observe diverse birdlife in the wetlands, and enjoy the varied habitats created from former brickmaking areas.

Name: Millfield Wood
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Millfield Wood is a 9.5-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north of High Wycombe in Buckinghamshire.

Name: Millington Wood
Description: Millington Wood is a large ancient woodland and local nature reserve in the Yorkshire Wolds. It features diverse flora and fauna, including notable butterfly populations. Managed for conservation and public access, it offers walking trails within its varied habitats.

Name: Millisons Wood
Description: Millisons Wood is an ancient woodland near Coventry, dominated by oak and hazel coppice. It features diverse ground flora including bluebells, wood anemone, and yellow archangel. The reserve supports a range of woodland birds and insects. Paths are flat, suitable for most visitors.

Name: Millook Valley Woods
Description: Millook Valley Woods is a Woodland Trust site in a deep coastal valley near Bude, Cornwall. This large area features ancient woodland and lush meadows, offering diverse habitats for visitors to explore via footpaths. It is known for its rich natural history and wildflowers.

Name: Milton Creek Country Park
Description: Milton Creek Country Park in Sittingbourne, Kent, is an urban coastal park with diverse habitats including saltmarsh and reedbeds. It offers walking, cycling, and nature observation along the Swale Estuary. The site is popular for community events.

Name: Milton Locks
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Milton Locks is a 1-hectare nature reserve in Milton in Hampshire.  It is managed by the Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust.

Name: Minchinhampton Common
Description: Minchinhampton Common is a large, biologically and geologically important SSSI, featuring extensive unimproved, herb-rich grassland atop a Jurassic limestone plateau.

Name: Minera Limeworks
Description: The Minera Limeworks were extensive lime quarries and kilns at Minera in Wrexham, Wales.  It was located at grid reference SJ253520, near the villages of Gwynfryn, Minera, and Coedpoeth and was locally referred to as The Calch.

Name: Mingulay
Description: Mingulay boasts towering sea-cliffs, among the highest in Britain, providing a vital nesting site for important seabird populations including puffins and razorbills.

Name: Minsmere
Description: Minsmere is an RSPB nature reserve on the Suffolk coast, featuring diverse habitats like reedbeds, woodlands, and heathland. Visitors can explore trails, hides, and an accessible discovery area, observing marsh harriers, bitterns, and avocets.

Name: Minsterley Meadows
Description: Minsterley Meadows is a nationally important Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) owned by the Middle Marches Community Land Trust, located near Minsterley, Shropshire. It features flower-rich grasslands, including the largest colony of Green-winged orchids in Shropshire, and provides vital habitat for diverse plant and wildlife species.

Name: Mitcheldean Meend Marsh
Description: Mitcheldean Meend Marsh is a 0.7-hectare nature reserve in Gloucestershire in the Forest of Dean.

Name: Moirlanich Longhouse
Description: Set within Glen Lochay, this site offers visitors a glimpse into the natural beauty and tranquil landscape of a Scottish glen.

Name: Moncreiffe Hill
Description: Moncreiffe Hill features mature woodland with walking trails, an Iron Age hill fort, and panoramic views over Perth, the River Tay, and the Earn valley. It is home to diverse wildlife and offers clear routes.

Name: Monks Dale
Description: Monks Dale is a limestone ash woodland within the Derbyshire Dales National Nature Reserve. It features species-rich grassland and ancient ash woodland. The dale is part of the Peak District National Park and home to several rare plant species.

Name: Monkstown Wood
Description: Monkstown Wood is a Local Nature Reserve in Newtownabbey, Northern Ireland, managed by the Woodland Trust. This urban green space features access pathways, way-markers, and life-like oak sculptures, offering a calm haven for nature and recreation alongside the Three Mile Water river.

Name: Montacute House
Description: Its highly-graded historic gardens offer a significant example of designed landscape conservation.

Name: Montrose Basin
Description: Montrose Basin is a nearly circular tidal basin which makes up part of the estuary of the River South Esk and which sits just inland of the town of Montrose in Angus on the east coast of Scotland.  The basin is protected by a number of designations; it is managed by the Scottish Wildlife Trust as a Wildlife Reserve, as well as being designated as a Local Nature Reserve, Site of Special Scientific Interest, a Special Protection Area and a Ramsar Site.

Name: Moor Copse
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Moor Copse is a 65-hectare nature reserve west of Reading in Berkshire.  It is managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Moors Valley Country Park and Forest
Description: This expansive Forestry England woodland in South East England offers a haven of natural beauty, where ancient trees shelter a vibrant ecosystem teeming with diverse wildlife. Visitors can immerse themselves in this picturesque landscape through a network of walking and cycling trails, perfect for exploring the serene environment and spotting local flora and fauna. It's a place to connect with nature, breathe in the fresh air, and discover the tranquility of the forest.

Name: Morden Hall Park
Description: Spanning 125 acres, this south London parkland features the River Wandle meandering through diverse channels, creating varied green spaces and habitats for wildlife.

Name: Moreton Forest
Description: This expansive Forestry England woodland in the South East offers a haven of ancient trees and diverse habitats, echoing with the calls of woodland birds and home to elusive deer. Visitors can explore winding trails, perfect for invigorating walks and cycling adventures, immersing themselves in the sights and sounds of nature. It's a place to connect with the wild, breathing in the fresh air and discovering the rich tapestry of life beneath the canopy.

Name: Morfa Mawddach
Description: Morfa Mawddach National Nature Reserve is a vast area of saltmarsh and sand dunes on the Mawddach estuary in Gwynedd, North West Wales. Located opposite Barmouth, it supports diverse birdlife like oystercatchers and curlews, alongside various coastal plant species.

Name: Morgan's Hill
Description: Morgan's Hill is a 12.6-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest between Calne and Devizes in Wiltshire, England.

Name: Morte Point
Description: Discover Morte Point, a dramatic coastal peninsula in Devon known for its rugged beauty and resident seal colonies.

Name: Mortimer Forest
Description: Discover a haven of ancient woodland, where towering trees create a dappled canopy and carpets of bluebells emerge in spring. This vast expanse is alive with the rustle of wildlife, from shy deer to chattering woodland birds, offering walkers and cyclists tranquil trails to explore its natural beauty. Immerse yourself in the peaceful atmosphere and reconnect with nature in this enchanting Forestry England woodland.

Name: Morvich, Highland
Description: A gateway to dramatic Highland landscapes, featuring towering mountains like the Five Sisters of Kintail, the stunning Falls of Glomach, and expansive glens.

Name: Moseley Bog
HostOrg: Birmingham and Black Country Wildlife Trust
Description: Moseley Bog and Joy's Wood Local Nature Reserve, formerly The Dell, is a Local Nature Reserve in the Moseley area of Birmingham, England, with an area of about 12 ha.  Along with the nearby Sarehole Mill, and a number of other sites, it forms part of the Shire Country Park.

Name: Moss Side Farm
Description: Moss Side Farm is a significant peatland restoration project in Greater Manchester, part of Natural England's pilot scheme within the Risley, Holcroft and Chat Moss National Nature Reserve. It focuses on rewetting and restoring degraded peat bogs, enhancing biodiversity, and sequestering carbon. The site actively contributes to wider landscape-scale conservation efforts in the Great Manchester Wetlands.

Name: Moss Valley Woodlands
HostOrg: Wildlife Trust for Sheffield and Rotherham
Description: The Moss is a brook in North East Derbyshire, England.  When Rother Valley Country Park was built in the 1980s, constructors used water from The Moss to fill the lakes.

Name: Mote Park
Description: Mote Park is a large country park in Maidstone, Kent, featuring diverse habitats including grassland, woodland, and a significant lake. It supports various wildlife and offers recreational opportunities for visitors.

Name: Mottisfont Abbey
Description: Nestled in the River Test valley, explore a beautiful walled rose garden, home to a National Plant Collection, and enjoy tranquil riverside walks.

Name: Mount Grace Priory
Description: Mount Grace Priory is nestled within the extensive woodlands of the North York Moors National Park.

Name: Mountsorrel Meadows
Description: Mountsorrel Meadows is a 12.6-hectare nature reserve on the eastern outskirts of Mountsorrel in Leicestershire.

Name: Mourne Mountains SAC
Description: The Mourne Mountains SAC is a special area in Northern Ireland, encompassing approximately 270 hectares of blanket bog. The PeatPLUS Project, funded by INTERREG VA, focuses on enhancing degraded peatlands through restoration work, re-wetting, and monitoring.

Name: Mousa
Description: Mousa is a small, uninhabited island south-east of Mainland Shetland, known for its Iron Age broch, a well-preserved drystone tower. The island is an RSPB nature reserve, a vital breeding ground for storm petrels, Arctic terns, and common terns. Grey seals often haul out on its shores.

Name: Mudchute Park and Farm
Description: Mudchute Park and Farm is a 32-acre community charity on London's Isle of Dogs. It offers a unique countryside oasis in the city, housing British rare breed animals. The site provides educational, recreational, and therapeutic opportunities for the local community and visitors.

Name: Muir of Dinnet NNR
Description: Muir of Dinnet NNR is an Aberdeenshire reserve, preserving Ice Age landscapes and diverse habitats. It features lochs, heath, and ancient woodlands, supporting rare birds, insects, and plants. Visitor facilities include waymarked trails and a car park.

Name: Mull of Galloway
Description: Mull of Galloway is Scotland's most southerly point, home to an RSPB nature reserve. Dramatic cliffs support thousands of nesting seabirds, including guillemots, razorbills, and kittiwakes during spring and summer. Visitors enjoy panoramic views across the Irish Sea and can spot marine wildlife.

Name: Murray Isles
Description: Murray Isles is a small, tidal island located within the nationally important Borgue Coast Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Mythe Railway Nature Reserve
Description: Mythe Railway Nature Reserve is a 2.8-hectare nature reserve in Gloucestershire.

Name: Nagshead Nature Reserve
Description: Explore a haven of ancient woodland and diverse habitats, where towering trees shelter a vibrant array of wildlife. Wander through sun-dappled paths, breathe in the fresh forest air, and keep an eye out for elusive woodland creatures. This sprawling woodland offers endless opportunities for walking and cycling amidst breathtaking natural beauty.

Name: Naphill Common
Description: Naphill Common is an ancient woodland, home to veteran trees, diverse fungi, and a variety of bird species. The site features open clearings and ponds, supporting a rich biodiversity within the Chilterns Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty.

Name: Narborough Bog
Description: Narborough Bog is an 8.5-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest east of Narborough in Leicestershire.

Name: Narborough Railway Line
Description: Narborough Railway Line or Narborough Railway Embankment is a 7.9-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south-east of King's Lynn in Norfolk, England.

Name: Nashenden Down
Description: Nashenden Down is a 55-hectare nature reserve on the southern outskirts of Rochester in Kent.  It is managed by the Kent Wildlife Trust, and is in the Kent Downs Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty.

Name: Nature Discovery Centre
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: The Nature Discovery Centre is a 35-hectare nature reserve in Thatcham in Berkshire.  It is managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Netherton Braes
Description: Netherton Braes is a natural area located within Linn Park, an urban Local Nature Reserve on Glasgow's outskirts, managed by Glasgow City Council. It provides a vital green space for local wildlife and people. Woodland, scrub, and grassland habitats support birds, insects, and small mammals. The site offers views across the city and Clyde Valley.

Name: Neu-Lindsey Nature Reserve
Description: Neu-Lindsey Nature Reserve is a 0.4-hectare nature reserve in Gloucestershire.

Name: New Buckenham Common
Description: New Buckenham Common is a common of which 20.9 hectares is a biological Site of Special Scientific Interest, located in New Buckenham, Norfolk, England.

Name: New Cross Gate Cutting
Description: New Cross Gate Cutting is a 4.2 hectare nature reserve in Brockley in the London Borough of Lewisham.

Name: New Fancy
Description: Discover a haven of ancient woodland in South East England, where towering trees create a dappled canopy for a diverse array of wildlife, from elusive deer to vibrant birdlife. Explore winding trails perfect for walking and cycling, immersing yourself in the sights and sounds of nature. This tranquil setting offers a refreshing escape, inviting you to connect with the natural world at your own pace.

Name: New Ferry Butterfly Park
Description: New Ferry Butterfly Park is a 2-hectare urban nature reserve in New Ferry, on the Wirral Peninsula, England.  It is managed by the Cheshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: New Forest
Description: This vast expanse of ancient woodland in South East England offers a haven for diverse wildlife, from soaring birds of prey to roaming ponies and deer. Explore winding trails perfect for walking and cycling, immersing yourself in the tranquility of ancient trees and heathland. Discover the raw beauty of the natural environment and connect with nature at its finest.

Name: New Forest National Park
Description: The New Forest National Park is a historic landscape in Hampshire, featuring extensive woodlands, heathlands, and coastline. It hosts diverse wildlife, including wild ponies, and offers visitor recreation. The National Park is governed by the New Forest National Park Authority.

Name: New Forest Reptile Centre
Description: Discover a haven of ancient woodlands and heathlands where rare reptiles and amphibians thrive in their natural habitat. Explore winding trails perfect for walking and cycling, immersing yourself in the sights and sounds of this vibrant ecosystem. This Forestry England woodland offers a unique opportunity to connect with nature and witness its fascinating wildlife up close.

Name: New Park
Description: Discover a vibrant tapestry of ancient trees and thriving wildlife within this expansive South East woodland. Wander winding trails through diverse habitats, perfect for invigorating walks and cycling adventures, or simply immerse yourself in the tranquility of nature. Keep an eye out for the diverse birdlife and other creatures that call this beautiful forest home.

Name: New Romney Warren
HostOrg: Romney Marsh Countryside Partnership (on behalf of Folkestone & Hythe District Council)
Description: Romney Warren, also known as New Romney Warren Country Park, is a Local Nature Reserve and Site of Special Scientific Interest on the Kent coast. It preserves a rare sand dune and acidic grassland habitat, home to diverse invertebrates, reptiles, and wildflowers, including nationally important populations of great crested newts. The site is part of the Dungeness, Romney Marsh and Rye Bay Ramsar internationally important wetland site and Dungeness Special Area of Conservation.

Name: Newark Park
Description: Discover 700 acres nestled on the Cotswold escarpment, offering sweeping views down the Severn Valley to the Severn Estuary.

Name: Newbourne Springs
Description: Newbourne Springs is a 15.7-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Newbourne in Suffolk.

Name: Newbridge Wood
Description: Step into a vibrant tapestry of ancient oaks and diverse wildlife within this expansive South West woodland. Discover winding trails perfect for leisurely walks and exhilarating cycles, offering opportunities to spot native birds and admire the changing seasons. Immerse yourself in the tranquility of nature, breathe in the fresh woodland air, and create lasting memories amidst the beauty of this Forestry England treasure.

Name: Newchurch Moors
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 50 hectares.

Name: Newdigate Brickworks
Description: Newdigate Brickworks is a 24-hectare nature reserve in Newdigate in Surrey, England.  It is managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Newhailes
Description: Explore 80 acres of tranquil parkland at Newhailes, a green oasis offering a valuable habitat on the edge of Musselburgh.

Name: Newland Grove
Description: Newland Grove is a 3.2-hectare nature reserve north of Chelmsford in Essex.

Name: Newton Coppice
Description: Newton Coppice is an ancient Herefordshire woodland near Leominster, dominated by oak and hazel. It supports woodland birds and wildflowers like early purple orchid. The site is actively managed, including coppicing, to enhance its biodiversity.

Name: Nidd Gorge
Description: Nidd Gorge is an ancient woodland and local conservation site nestled between Harrogate and Knaresborough, North Yorkshire. It comprises five distinct woods: Coalpits Wood, Bilton Banks, Spring Wood, Scotton Banks, and Gates Wood. The River Nidd flows through a dramatic, steep-sided ravine, offering diverse habitats for a wealth of wildlife, including over 80 species of birds and 30 different kinds of mammals, reptiles, and amphibians. The site features accessible paths and is known for stunning bluebell displays in spring.

Name: Nightingale Wood
Description: Wander through ancient trees and discover a haven for diverse wildlife in this South East England woodland. Explore winding paths perfect for walking and cycling, immersing yourself in the sights and sounds of nature. This vibrant forest offers a peaceful escape, inviting you to connect with the natural world.

Name: Nind Nature Reserve
Description: Nind Nature Reserve is a 3.75-hectare nature reserve in Gloucestershire.

Name: Ningwood Common
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 11 hectares.

Name: Noar Hill
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Noar Hill is a 63-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south of Selborne in Hampshire.  It is a Nature Conservation Review site, Grade 2, and part of East Hampshire Hangers Special Area of Conservation.

Name: Noddle Hill
Description: Noddle Hill Nature Reserve is an urban wetland on the eastern edge of Hull, transformed from arable land. It features ponds, ditches, and reedbeds, providing habitats for waterfowl, warblers, and insects. This quiet oasis supports local wildlife and offers community recreation.

Name: Nomadic Community Garden
Description: Nomadic Community Garden is a green space in East London, established on former railway sidings. It operates as a public park and community-run garden. The garden features diverse flora, unique structures, and is home to local wildlife. It encourages biodiversity and sustainable urban living.

Name: Norah Hanbury-Kelk Meadows
Description: Norah Hanbury-Kelk Meadows is an eight hectare nature reserve in Barton Mills in Suffolk.  It is managed by the Suffolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Norbury Park
Description: Norbury Park is an area of mixed wooded and agricultural land surrounding a privately owned Georgian manor house near Leatherhead and Dorking, Surrey.  On the west bank of the River Mole, it is close to the village of Mickleham.

Name: North Cave Wetlands
Description: North Cave Wetlands is a nature reserve at North Cave, East Riding of Yorkshire, England, managed by the Yorkshire Wildlife Trust.  The reserve based at Dryham Lane is 40 hectares in size and comprises six lakes, restored from a former sand and gravel quarry.

Name: North Cove
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 16 hectares.

Name: North East England
Description: North East England, often referred to as simply the North East within England, is one of nine official regions of England.  It consists of County Durham, Northumberland, Tyne and Wear and part of North Yorkshire.

Name: North Hill
Description: North Hill, on Papa Westray, is a remote RSPB reserve renowned for its seabird colonies, including puffins, guillemots, and Arctic terns during breeding season. Rich in wildflowers and home to grey seals and otters, it offers dramatic clifftop walks with expansive views.

Name: North Pennines National Landscape Peatland Heart
Description: The North Pennines National Landscape is home to 20% of England's blanket bog. Its Peatland Programme, celebrating 20 years, restores degraded peatlands across the region. This internationally recognised conservation work has been ongoing for 30 years.

Name: Northcombe
Description: This expansive woodland in the South West of England is a haven for wildlife, with ancient trees providing a rich habitat for diverse species. Visitors can immerse themselves in nature, exploring winding trails perfect for walking and cycling adventures amidst the tranquil beauty of the forest. Discover the sights and sounds of a thriving natural environment, offering a peaceful escape and opportunities for discovery.

Name: Northey Island
Description: This tidal island in the Blackwater Estuary is a Site of Special Scientific Interest, cherished for its diverse birdlife and vital saltmarsh habitats.

Name: Northwood Community Woodland
Description: Northwood Community Woodland, also known as Northwood Forest Hills, in Kirkby, Merseyside, offers a significant green space for local residents. The site features woodland areas, a fishing pond, wetland areas, and accessible footpath routes, suitable for walking and recreation. Managed with active community involvement, it focuses on enhancing local biodiversity and providing public enjoyment, including activities like pond dipping, bug hunts, and forest school sessions.

Name: Nower Wood
Description: Nower Wood is a 33-hectare nature reserve south-west of Leatherhead in Surrey.  It is owned and managed by Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Nunnery Wood
Description: Nunnery Wood is a 21-hectare Local Nature Reserve located within Worcester Woods Country Park in Worcester. It is an ancient semi-natural woodland, predominantly featuring pedunculate oak with an understorey of coppiced hazel. The wood is home to a variety of wildlife, including great crested newts, pond snails, water beetles, and dragonfly larvae, and is known for its bluebells in spring. It forms part of the Woodland Trail at the Country Park.

Name: Nunnington Hall
Description: Nunnington Hall lies by the River Rye, backed by Caulkley's Bank, and nestled between the Vale of York and the North York Moors.

Name: Nutcombe Bottom
Description: Discover a haven of ancient trees and vibrant wildlife within this expansive Forestry England woodland. Wander through peaceful glades, keeping an eye out for elusive deer and a symphony of birdsong. This natural playground invites you to explore its winding paths, perfect for invigorating walks and cycling adventures amidst the beauty of nature.

Name: Nutfield Marshes
Description: Nutfield Marshes is a 62-hectare nature reserve near Nutfield in Surrey.  It is managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Nymans
Description: Nymans is a renowned English garden famous for originating many unique plant varieties, hybrids, and selections, including several familiar shrubs.

Name: Oak Tree Heath
Description: Oak Tree Heath is a Local Nature Reserve near Mansfield, Nottinghamshire. This scarce lowland heath and acid grassland habitat supports heather, gorse, insects, reptiles, and birds. Managed through grazing by cattle and sheep to preserve its unique biodiversity.

Name: Oakfield Wood
Description: Oakfield Wood is a 2.8-hectare nature reserve west of Wrabness in Essex.

Name: Oakhill Nature Reserve
HostOrg: Countryside Access Team and Friends of Oakhill
Description: Oakhill Nature Reserve near Goole is a wetland site managed by the Countryside Access Team and Friends of Oakhill. It features an open water scrape, reedbeds, and wet grassland, supporting diverse birdlife like sedge warblers and kingfishers, plus amphibians. A surfaced path and hide offer visitor access.

Name: Oakley Hill
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Oakley Hill is a 13-hectare nature reserve south of Chinnor in Oxfordshire, England.  It is managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Oare Marshes
Description: Oare Marshes is a 71.4-hectare Local Nature Reserve north of Faversham in Kent.

Name: Oare Meadow
Description: Oare Meadow is a 2-hectare nature reserve in Oare, north of Faversham in Kent.  It is managed by the Kent Wildlife Trust.

Name: Old Broom
Description: Old Broom is a 6.5-hectare nature reserve north of Risby in Suffolk.

Name: Old Dungeon Ghyll
Description: Experience breathtaking Lake District fells, iconic peaks, and the impressive cascades of Dungeon Ghyll Force waterfall.

Name: Old Hall Marshes
Description: Old Hall Marshes is an RSPB nature reserve, forming part of the Blackwater Estuary National Nature Reserve. Its varied habitats include extensive grazing marshes, brackish water fleets, reedbeds, and saltmarsh, supporting significant bird populations year-round, including avocets, lapwings, redshanks, and wintering brent geese.

Name: Old Harry Rocks
Description: Iconic chalk stacks and stumps at Handfast Point mark the eastern end of the Jurassic Coast, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Dorset.

Name: Old Lodge
Description: Old Lodge is a 103.1-hectare Local Nature Reserve west of Crowborough in East Sussex.

Name: Old Moor
HostOrg: Royal Society for the Protection of Birds (RSPB)
Description: Old Moor Nature Reserve, near Barnsley, South Yorkshire, is a wetland habitat managed for diverse wildlife. It features lagoons, reedbeds, and grasslands, providing refuge for birds. Visitor facilities include hides and a visitor centre.

Name: Old Park Hill
Description: Old Park Hill is a 40-hectare nature reserve north of Dover in Kent.  It is managed by the Kent Wildlife Trust.

Name: Old Park Wood
Description: Old Park Wood is a 16.7-hectare Site of Special Scientific Interest in Harefield in the London Borough of Hillingdon.

Name: Oldbury Camp
Description: Vast woodlands cloak this Kentish hilltop, providing a haven for wildlife and stunning views across the Weald.

Name: Oldbury-on-Severn Wood
Description: Oldbury-on-Severn Wood is a small, developing woodland. Planted in 2000, it features mixed broadleaves and conifer species. The site offers views of the River Severn estuary and is accessible via public footpaths.

Name: Ollerton Pit Wood
Description: This ancient woodland in the heart of the Midlands offers a vibrant tapestry of natural beauty, where diverse wildlife thrives amidst a mature canopy. Visitors can immerse themselves in the tranquility of the forest, exploring winding trails perfect for walking and cycling, and discovering the rich biodiversity that calls this special place home. It's an ideal destination for anyone seeking a connection with nature and a breath of fresh air.

Name: One Tree Hill and Bitchet Common
Description: Explore diverse ancient woodlands and varied habitats across this Site of Special Scientific Interest, home to rare plants and invertebrates within an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty.

Name: Onziebust
Description: Onziebust is an RSPB nature reserve on Egilsay, Orkney. It features a mosaic of wildflower meadows, grassland fields, and extensive wetland areas, including wet grassland and reedbeds. These habitats support breeding waders such as curlews, lapwings, and snipe, and are home to the nationally scarce Great Yellow Bumblebee. The reserve's tranquil lochs, rocky coast, and sandy beaches provide important feeding grounds for wintering waders and wildfowl like Redshanks and Wigeons. Raptors such as hen harriers also hunt here.

Name: Orford Ness
Description: Orford Ness is a dynamic shingle spit on the Suffolk coast, uniquely shaped by longshore drift and divided by the River Alde, creating a distinct coastal landscape.

Name: Ormesby Beck
Description: Ormesby Beck Nature Reserve in Middlesbrough is a linear wetland habitat along the beck. It supports species like water vole, kingfisher, and various dragonflies. The reserve features reedbeds, ponds, and wet grassland, providing a vital green corridor.

Name: Osterley Park
Description: Osterley Park offers vast green spaces and mature parkland within west London.

Name: Ostlers Plantation
Description: Discover a haven of ancient oaks and vibrant wildlife nestled in the heart of the Midlands. Wander through sun-dappled paths, keeping an eye out for elusive deer and a symphony of birdsong. This expansive woodland offers a perfect escape for walkers and cyclists to immerse themselves in the beauty of nature.

Name: Oughtonhead
Description: Oughtonhead Common is a 17.4 hectare Local Nature Reserve in the Westmill district of Hitchin, Hertfordshire.

Name: Oughtonhead Common
Description: Oughtonhead Common is a nature reserve near Hitchin, featuring wet woodland, fen, and grassland habitats fed by the River Oughton. The River Oughton originates from Oughtonhead Spring, a SSSI. Wildlife includes kingfishers, water voles, otters, and Daubenton's bats.

Name: Ouse Estuary Nature Reserve
Description: The Ouse Estuary Nature Reserve, near Newhaven, is managed by East Sussex County Council. This site offers public footpaths and a cycle track, forming a vital wildlife corridor along the River Ouse. It is managed primarily for wildlife benefit and flood management, forming part of a wider conservation effort in the area.

Name: Overbeck's
Description: Perched on a sheltered Devon hillside, Overbeck's features a rare subtropical garden, home to an array of exotic plant species.

Name: Overscourt Wood
Description: This extensive Forestry England woodland in South East England offers a haven of ancient trees and diverse habitats, teeming with wildlife that flits through the canopy and rustles in the undergrowth. Visitors can immerse themselves in nature, enjoying peaceful walks or invigorating cycles along winding trails, discovering the vibrant flora and fauna that call this special place home. It's an ideal destination for those seeking to connect with the natural world and experience the tranquility of a thriving woodland ecosystem.

Name: Oversley Wood
Description: This expansive Forestry England woodland in South East England is a haven for nature lovers, offering a tapestry of ancient trees and diverse habitats. Wander through sun-dappled paths, cycle along winding trails, and keep an eye out for the abundant wildlife that calls this place home, from shy deer to vibrant birdlife. It's a perfect escape to reconnect with the natural world and enjoy the simple pleasures of walking amidst beautiful woodland scenery.

Name: Oxburgh Hall
Description: Explore Oxburgh Hall's historic moat and surrounding parkland, providing habitats for diverse wetland plants and local wildlife.

Name: Oxclose Wood
Description: This extensive woodland invites exploration with its diverse mix of trees, offering a haven for woodland birds and small mammals.  Wander along peaceful trails, breathe in the fresh forest air, and discover the quiet beauty of nature unfolding around you. It's a perfect place to enjoy a walk or cycle through a vibrant natural landscape.

Name: Oxey Mead
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 8 hectares.

Name: Oxford Island NNR
Description: Oxford Island NNR is a National Nature Reserve on Lough Neagh's southern shore. It features diverse habitats including woodlands, reedbeds, and meadows, supporting significant bird populations. Owned and managed by Armagh City, Banbridge & Craigavon Council, the site offers visitor facilities and walking trails.

Name: Oxley Meadow
Description: Oxley Meadow is a 3.2-hectare nature reserve in Tolleshunt Knights, near Tiptree in Essex.

Name: Oxshott Heath & Woods
Description: Oxshott Heath and Woods is a mosaic of woodland and heathland in Surrey, featuring ancient oak and Scots pine trees. The site supports diverse wildlife including birds, invertebrates, and reptiles, with ponds and streams adding ecological value.

Name: Oxwich National Nature Reserve
Description: Oxwich National Nature Reserve, located within the Gower AONB, is a mosaic of diverse habitats. It features extensive sand dunes, saltmarsh, woodland, and a freshwater lake. The reserve supports a rich array of wildlife, including rare insects and plants. Public footpaths offer access for visitors.

Name: Pabbay, Barra, Scotland
Description: This remote Outer Hebridean island is a vital summer sanctuary for many ground-nesting birds, thriving in the absence of predators.

Name: Packwood House
Description: Known for its distinctive garden of yews, Packwood House offers a unique and sculpted natural landscape.

Name: Padworth Common
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Padworth Common Local Nature Reserve is a 28-hectare Local Nature Reserve on the edge of the hamlet of Padworth Common, between Reading and Newbury in Berkshire.  It is owned by West Berkshire Council and managed by Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Pages Wood
Description: Venture into a tranquil haven of ancient oaks and vibrant woodland flora, alive with the buzz of insects and the songs of diverse birdlife. Miles of winding paths invite exploration on foot or by bike, offering immersive experiences amidst the beauty of nature. Discover a peaceful escape where you can reconnect with the natural world and witness its delicate ecosystems firsthand.

Name: Pagham Harbour
Description: Pagham Harbour, a West Sussex Site of Special Scientific Interest, is a protected wildlife haven. It features extensive mudflats, saltmarshes, and shingle beaches, supporting diverse bird species. Hides and walking trails are available.

Name: Paices Wood Country Parkland
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 35 hectares.

Name: Pamber Forest and Upper Inhams
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Pamber Forest and Silchester Common is a 341.7-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Tadley in Hampshire.

Name: Pant-y-Sais
Description: Panty-Sais is a valuable wetland site in north Pembrokeshire, featuring fen and reedbed habitats. It supports diverse wildlife, including otters, water voles, and various bird species. The reserve contributes to local biodiversity conservation.

Name: Papercourt Marshes
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 10 hectares.

Name: Park Gate Down
Description: Park Gate Down or Parkgate Down is a 7-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south-east of Stelling Minnis in Kent.

Name: Park Hall Nature Reserve
HostOrg: Birmingham and Black Country Wildlife Trust
Description: Park Hall was a Wildlife Trust nature reserve in Birmingham, England, until it was taken possession of by HS2.  The 40-hectare site lies between the M6 motorway and Castle Vale in the east of Birmingham.

Name: Parkhurst Forest
Description: Venture into a vibrant tapestry of ancient oaks and whispering pines, where sunlight dapples through the canopy, illuminating a haven for diverse wildlife. This expansive woodland offers tranquil walking trails and exhilarating cycling routes, inviting you to immerse yourself in the sights and sounds of nature. Discover a place alive with birdsong, buzzing insects, and the rustle of unseen creatures, perfect for exploring on foot or by bike.

Name: Parndon Wood
HostOrg: Harlow District Council (managed in partnership with ECCO and volunteers)
Description: Parndon Wood Nature Reserve is an ancient woodland spanning over 50 acres, designated a Local Nature Reserve in Harlow, Essex. It features mature hornbeam coppice and oak standards, supporting diverse flora and fauna including deer and various bird species. The reserve offers tranquil walking paths, three bird-watching hides, a large pond, and a conservation centre with a café. It is managed by Harlow District Council in partnership with local charity ECCO and volunteers.

Name: Parrot's Drumble
Description: Parrot's Drumble is a nature reserve of the Staffordshire Wildlife Trust.  It is an area of woodland next to the village of Talke Pits, and about 4 miles north of Newcastle-under-Lyme, in Staffordshire, England.

Name: Parsonage Moor
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Parsonage Moor is a 6-hectare nature reserve north-west of Abingdon-on-Thames in Oxfordshire, United Kingdom.  It is managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Parsonage Wood
Description: Parsonage Wood is a 9.7-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south-east of Cranbrook in Kent.

Name: Pasturefields Saltmarsh
Description: Pasturefields Saltmarsh is nature reserve of Staffordshire Wildlife Trust, a salt marsh near Stafford, in Staffordshire, England.  It is designated a Site of Special Scientific Interest and a Special Area of Conservation.

Name: Patmore Heath
Description: Patmore Heath is a 7.6 hectares biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in East Hertfordshire, England, 2 kilometres north-east of Albury.

Name: Paxton Pits Nature Reserve
HostOrg: Huntingdonshire District Council (in partnership with the Friends of Paxton Pits)
Description: Paxton Pits Nature Reserve is a 77-hectare site in the Great Ouse valley, near Little Paxton, Cambridgeshire. It is a former sand and gravel quarry, now a rich mosaic of habitats including lakes, meadows, reedbed, scrub, and woodland, offering diverse wildlife year-round. It is designated as a Local Nature Reserve and a Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Peascroft Wood
HostOrg: Birmingham and Black Country Wildlife Trust
Description: Peascroft Wood is a nature reserve of the Wildlife Trust for Birmingham and the Black Country, in Bilston, West Midlands, England.

Name: Pease Dean
Description: Pease Dean is a nature reserve at Pease Bay, in the Scottish Borders area of Scotland, near the Anglo-Scottish border and Cockburnspath, Cove, and Dunglass.  OS 67 NT794707.

Name: Peckover House & Garden
Description: Discover lush gardens blooming with diverse plant life, offering a peaceful haven for local wildlife.

Name: Pen Ponds, Richmond Park
Description: Pen Ponds are two large, man-made ponds in the centre of Richmond Park, created in 1746. Fed by a spring, they host diverse birdlife like Grey Herons and Great Crested Grebes. Fishing is permitted with a permit acquired from the Roehampton Gate office.

Name: Penlee Battery
Description: Penlee Battery is a nature reserve lying on the coastal headland of Penlee Point on the Rame Peninsula, in southeast Cornwall, England.  The site was formerly the location of a gun battery, constructed between 1889 and 1892.

Name: Pennington Flash
Description: Pennington Flash, near Leigh, is a significant nature reserve managed by Wigan Council. It offers diverse habitats for wildlife, including many rare bird species, and provides opportunities for walking, cycling, and fishing. The site operates as a key nature recovery hub.

Name: Pennytown Ponds Local Nature Reserve
Description: Pennytown Ponds is a Local Nature Reserve near Somercotes, Ripley, Derbyshire, managed by Amber Valley Borough Council. It features a mosaic of four ponds, woodland, marshland, and grassland meadows, providing diverse habitats. The reserve is home to amphibians, numerous insects including damselflies and dragonflies, and a variety of birds such as moorhens, coots, mallards, green woodpeckers, spotted woodpeckers, and kingfishers. It also supports a diverse selection of wildflowers, including orchids, and has received Green Flag status.

Name: Penrose, Cornwall
Description: Discover Penrose's rich coastal scenery, including the stunning Loe Pool and unique Loe Bar, a freshwater lagoon habitat.

Name: Penshaw Monument
Description: Penshaw Monument stands atop Penshaw Hill, providing panoramic views of the surrounding County Durham countryside.

Name: Pensthorpe Natural Park
Description: Pensthorpe Natural Park is an award-winning 700-acre nature reserve and conservation charity in Norfolk, UK. It features diverse habitats, including wetlands, woodlands, and gardens, supporting a variety of wildlife and offering conservation experiences.

Name: Pentwyn Farm Grasslands
Description: Pentwyn Farm Grasslands is a nature reserve, and a series of agricultural fields, in Monmouthshire, southeast Wales.  It was designated a Site of Special Scientific Interest in 1993, noted for its biological characteristics.

Name: Pepperbox Hill
Description: Discover Pepperbox Hill, a prominent chalk ridge offering breathtaking views and distinctive chalk grassland habitats.

Name: Perry Woods
Description: Perry Woods spans 149 acres near Selling, Kent, comprising woodland, orchards, and grassland. It sits on a north-facing chalk escarpment. The site is noted for its spring bluebells and hosts over 50 bird species and 20 butterfly species, including the grizzled skipper.

Name: Peter's Stone
Description: Peter's Stone is a prominent limestone knoll within Cressbrook Dale, part of the Derbyshire Dales National Nature Reserve, near Wardlow Mires in the Peak District. It features species-rich limestone grassland and ancient ash woodland, known for diverse flora including rare orchids. Managed by Natural England, it offers views across the Wye Valley.

Name: Petworth House
Description: Explore Petworth's expansive deer park, home to a large herd of fallow deer, within a stunning Capability Brown landscape.

Name: Pevensey Marshes
Description: Pevensey Levels is a 3,603.2-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest between Bexhill-on-Sea and Hailsham in East Sussex.

Name: Pevensey Road Nature Reserve
Description: Pevensey Road Nature Reserve is a 10.2-hectare Local Nature Reserve in Hanworth, in the London Borough of Hounslow, West London. It is owned and managed by Hounslow Council, with The Conservation Volunteers (TCV) running weekly Green Gym sessions to help manage the site. The reserve lies on the banks of the River Crane and features species-rich wildflower meadows, damp woodland, and wetlands. It is also part of the Crane Corridor Site of Metropolitan Importance for Nature Conservation and connects to Little Park via a wooden bridge.

Name: Philipps House
Description: Set amidst Grade II* historic parkland, Philipps House overlooks the scenic Nadder Valley.

Name: Philips Park
Description: Philips Park is a Victorian Green Flag park and Local Nature Reserve in Whitefield, Bury, Greater Manchester. It features rich woodland and grassland habitats, ancient woodlands, walking trails, and a children's play area. The park is home to diverse wildlife and includes the Barn Countryside Centre.

Name: Phoenix Garden
Description: The Phoenix Garden is a community green space and registered charity in London's West End. Established in 1984 on a former car park, it provides an oasis for urban wildlife and people, featuring frogs, newts, and foxes.

Name: Phoenix Park
Description: Phoenix Park is a community woodland located in Sheffield, South Yorkshire. The Conservation Volunteers (TCV) manage the site, conducting weekly practical conservation sessions every Wednesday. It provides an accessible green space for local residents.

Name: Phyllis Currie
Description: Phyllis Currie Nature Reserve is an 8.9-hectare nature reserve north-west of Great Leighs in Essex.

Name: Pick Triangle Wood
Description: Pick Triangle Wood, opened 2005, is a young woodland near Measham, Leicestershire. It features accessible paths, a small stream, and native broadleaf species. The wood includes an arboretum area and connects to a longer walking route along the Ashby Canal.

Name: Piggledene
Description: Piggledene is a Wiltshire biological and geological Site of Special Scientific Interest, recognised for its significant natural value.

Name: Pigneys Wood
Description: Pigneys Wood or Pigney's Wood is a 20.9-hectare Local Nature Reserve north of North Walsham in Norfolk, England.

Name: Pilch Field
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Pilch Fields is an 11.1-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest west of Great Horwood in Buckinghamshire.

Name: Pilmuir Riparian Project
Description: The Pilmuir Riparian Project, near Peebles in the Scottish Borders, restores riverbanks along the Eddleston Water. It involves planting native trees and improving biodiversity. This is a collaboration between SP Energy Networks, Borders Forest Trust, and Tweed Forum.

Name: Pilsdon Pen
Description: Pilsdon Pen, Dorset's prominent second highest point, provides extensive panoramic views across the beautiful Marshwood Vale.

Name: Pitmedden Garden
Description: Pitmedden Garden nurtures vibrant herbaceous borders and a fruitful orchard.

Name: Pity Me Carrs
Description: Pity Me Carrs is a wetland nature reserve situated near Pity Me in County Durham. It encompasses diverse marshland and grassland habitats, providing a vital home for various bird species and plant life.

Name: Pleasley Park
Description: This beautiful Forestry England woodland in the Midlands invites exploration through its diverse natural environment. Wander or cycle along scenic trails, keeping an eye out for the abundant wildlife that calls this expansive area home. It's a perfect place to reconnect with nature and enjoy the simple pleasures of the outdoors.

Name: Pleasley Pit Country Park
Description: Pleasley Pit Country Park, a former Nottinghamshire coal mine, has been transformed into a vibrant nature reserve. It features a preserved working steam winding engine and heritage centre, offering visitors walking trails and rich wildlife habitats. The park uniquely combines industrial history with diverse biodiversity for public enjoyment.

Name: Plymbridge Woods
Description: Plymbridge Woods features woodlands alongside the River Plym, home to a rich range of wildlife, birds, and flora.

Name: Polesden Lacey
Description: Explore 1,400 acres of ancient woodland, sprawling lawns, and beautiful rose gardens on the scenic North Downs.

Name: Polhill Bank
Description: Polhill Bank is a 4-hectare nature reserve south of Shoreham, which is north of Sevenoaks in Kent.  It is managed by Kent Wildlife Trust.

Name: Pollok House
Description: Pollok House is located in Pollok Country Park, featuring extensive woodlands and diverse wildlife habitats.

Name: Poor's Allotment
Description: Poor's Allotment is a 28.57-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Gloucestershire, notified in 1954.

Name: Poors Allotment
Description: Poors Allotment is a 76-hectare nature reserve north of Camberley in Surrey.  It is owned by Windlesham United Charities and managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Poppy Wood
Description: This extensive woodland in the heart of the Midlands offers a sanctuary for diverse wildlife, from ancient oaks to the rustling undergrowth where woodland birds and mammals make their home. Visitors can immerse themselves in nature, exploring winding paths perfect for invigorating walks and cycling, all while breathing in the fresh air and enjoying the peaceful surroundings. It's a place to connect with the natural world, spotting shy creatures and experiencing the beauty of a thriving forest ecosystem.

Name: Portbury Wharf
Description: Portbury Wharf Nature Reserve, a key coastal wetland in North Somerset, features salt marsh, open water, and reedbeds. It supports diverse bird species, including waterfowl and waders. The reserve offers walking trails and bird hides.

Name: Portbury Wharf Nature Reserve
Description: Portbury Ashlands which is now known as Portbury Wharf Nature Reserve is a nature reserve between Portishead and the Royal Portbury Dock in Somerset, England.  It was formed from the redevelopment of the area of Portishead formerly occupied by two power stations.

Name: Portmore Lough
Description: Portmore Lough is an important area of lowland wet grassland with open water, reedbeds and scrub, supporting many wetland birds. Significant for wintering wildfowl and breeding waders, it also hosts a range of invertebrates and plant species.

Name: Portrack Marsh Nature Reserve
Description: Portrack Marsh Nature Reserve is a 50 acres reserve by the northern bank of the River Tees between the Tees Barrage and the Tees Viaduct, near Portrack housing estate in Stockton-on-Tees borough, County Durham.  It is the last remaining wetland on the lower Tees.

Name: Portrack Meadows Wildlife Reserve
Description: The Portrack Incinerator was a municipal waste incinerator and waste-to-energy power station situated on the River Tees at Portrack in Stockton-on-Tees in County Durham, England.

Name: Portway Hill
HostOrg: Birmingham and Black Country Wildlife Trust
Description: Portway Hill is part of the Rowley Hills, near Rowley Regis in West Midlands, England.  It is the site of a nature reserve of the Wildlife Trust for Birmingham and the Black Country.

Name: Pot of Doan
Description: Pot of Doan is a peatland restoration site in the Mourne Mountains, Northern Ireland. It is part of the PEATLANDS+ cross-border project, led by Ulster Wildlife. This initiative restores degraded peatlands to enhance carbon storage, biodiversity, and water quality.

Name: Potteric Carr
Description: Potteric Carr is a large area of land to the southeast of Doncaster, in Yorkshire, England, over 3,000 acres in size.

Name: Poulter Country Park
Description: Poulter Country Park is a reclaimed colliery site offering walking trails, wildlife habitats, and historical remnants. Located near Bolsover, it features diverse woodlands, wetlands, and open grassland areas, providing recreational and educational opportunities.

Name: Pound Farm
Description: Pound Farm is a diverse Woodland Trust site in Suffolk, located between Great Glenham and Framlingham. This 90-hectare woodland features a mix of young and ancient woodland, wide rides, wildflower meadows, and five ponds, offering splendid views and diverse habitats for wildlife.

Name: Pound Wood
Description: Pound Wood is a 22.3 nature reserve in Thundersley in Essex.

Name: Prees Heath
Description: Prees Heath is a crucial refuge for the rare silver-studded blue butterfly, one of only three sites in England. This lowland heathland, part of a former WWII airfield, supports diverse flora and fauna, including rare birds and reptiles. Managed for conservation.

Name: Prehen Wood
Description: Prehen Wood, an ancient woodland overlooking the River Foyle, is a crucial urban green space in Derry/Londonderry. It hosts a rich diversity of native trees including oak, ash, and hazel, supporting various wildlife species. Managed for conservation and public access.

Name: Pressmennan Wood
Description: Pressmennan Wood is an 86-hectare (212-acre) ancient woodland in East Lothian, managed by the Woodland Trust. It is known for its veteran trees, diverse flora and fauna including deer, owls, otters, and bats, and overlooks Pressmennan Lake. The wood features an extensive network of paths, including a child-friendly 'Glingbobs and Tootflits' sculpture trail.

Name: Preston Mill
Description: This picturesque watermill, powered by the River Tyne, sits amidst a tranquil waterside landscape featuring a mill pond and nearby Smeaton Lake.

Name: Priest Hill
Description: Priest Hill is a 35-hectare nature reserve on the eastern outskirts of Ewell, near Epsom in north Surrey.  It is managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Priestley Wood
Description: Priestley Wood is an ancient woodland, once part of the deer park of Priestley House. It features a diverse range of tree species, including oak, ash, and field maple, along with a rich ground flora. Public access is available.

Name: Prince's Community Wood
Description: Prince's Community Wood is a small community woodland within The National Forest, near Tatenhill, Staffordshire. The site was formerly used for sand and gravel extraction and was bought by Tatenhill and Rangemore Parish Council in 2013. Planting of 10,000 trees was completed in 2014, and it now offers broadleaf trees, ponds, and open areas, supporting diverse wildlife habitats and providing recreational opportunities for visitors.

Name: Prior Park Landscape Garden
Description: Discover a captivating landscape garden featuring a picturesque lake and expansive green parkland.

Name: Prior's Coppice
Description: Prior's Coppice is a 27.4-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south of Oakham in Rutland.

Name: Priorwood Garden
Description: Priorwood Garden cultivates an orchard of unusual apple varieties and a vibrant flower garden providing blooms for dried arrangements.

Name: Pryor's Wood
Description: Pryor's Wood is an ancient woodland in Hertfordshire, featuring mature oak, hornbeam, and hazel coppice. The reserve supports diverse flora including bluebells, wood anemones, and wild daffodils. Birdlife thrives here, alongside various butterfly species.

Name: Pryor's Wood
Description: Pryor's Wood is an 8.7-hectare nature reserve in Great Ashby, near Stevenage in Hertfordshire.

Name: Pucks Oak Barn and McAlmont Reserves
Description: Pucks Oak Barn and McAlmont Reserves is a 4-hectare nature reserve near Compton, west of Guildford in Surrey.  It is managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Puddletown Forest
Description: This ancient woodland in South East England offers a vibrant tapestry of native trees, creating a haven for diverse wildlife like woodland birds and deer. Visitors can explore winding paths perfect for walking and cycling, immersing themselves in the sights and sounds of nature. It's a wonderful place to connect with the natural world and enjoy the tranquility of the forest.

Name: Purwell Ninesprings
Description: Purwell Ninesprings is a 6.4-hectare nature reserve managed by the Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust on the edge of Hitchin, Hertfordshire, England.

Name: Putney Heath
Description: Putney Heath is a significant open space in South West London, managed by the Wimbledon and Putney Commons Conservators. It comprises heathland, woodland, and ponds, providing public access for recreation and supporting diverse wildlife within a protected landscape.

Name: Puttenham Common
Description: Puttenham Common is a large nature reserve near Guildford, owned and managed by Hampton Estate, with Surrey County Council managing public access and car parks. Surrey Wildlife Trust is also involved in conservation projects on the common. It features extensive lowland heath, woodland, ponds, and acidic grassland, supporting diverse flora and fauna, including rare species. Visitors can explore numerous walking trails and observe various bird species and invertebrates.

Name: Puxton Moor
Description: Puxton Moor is a 31. 07 ha biological Site of Special Scientific Interest on the North Somerset Levels, near Puxton, North Somerset, notified in 1994.

Name: Pymmes Brook
Description: Thames21 is restoring Pymmes Brook, a highly urbanised river in Enfield. Work focuses on improving river habitats, water quality, and biodiversity through various interventions like natural river features and riparian planting. The project enhances local green spaces.

Name: Pymmes Park
Description: Pymmes Park in Lower Edmonton, Enfield, is a Green Flag Award-winning urban park. It features a restored lake and wetland habitat, play areas, sports facilities, and a café. The park is open 24/7. The Friends of Pymmes Park actively run community events and regular volunteering days.

Name: Quarr Community Woodland
Description: Quarr Community Woodland is a Local Nature Reserve bordering the A30 in Sherborne. Spanning 2.5 hectares, it provides diverse wildlife habitats and recreational space. Managed by Sherborne Town Council, the site offers public access.

Name: Quarry Hangers
Description: Quarry Hangers is a 28.5-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south-west of Caterham in Surrey.

Name: Quarry Wood
Description: Quarry Wood is a 26-hectare nature reserve east of West Farleigh, which is south-west of Maidstone in Kent.  It is managed by the Kent Wildlife Trust.

Name: Quarry Wood, Hinstock
Description: Quarry Wood nature reserve is a 7-acre woodland on the west side of the A41 road at Hinstock in Shropshire that is managed by the Shropshire Wildlife Trust.  Oak, birch and occasional hornbeam grow alongside swathes of rhododendron.

Name: Queen Elizabeth Country Park
Description: Venture into a sprawling expanse of ancient woodland and open heathland, alive with the rustle of diverse wildlife. Explore miles of trails perfect for invigorating walks and exciting cycling adventures, immersing yourself in the beauty of nature. This vibrant landscape offers a sanctuary for both people and animals, inviting exploration and discovery.

Name: Queen's Copse
Description: This sprawling woodland in South East England offers a haven for diverse wildlife, from shy deer to abundant birdlife, amidst a tapestry of ancient trees and vibrant undergrowth. Explore winding paths perfect for leisurely walks and invigorating cycles, immersing yourself in the sights and sounds of a thriving natural environment. Discover the peace and beauty of nature at its finest, with opportunities to observe wildlife and connect with the woodland ecosystem.

Name: Queen's Park
Description: Queen's Park is a Grade II listed historic park in north west London, managed by the City of London Corporation. It features formal gardens, woodlands, ornamental ponds, and sports facilities. The park also includes a children's playground, cafe, and a bandstand. It has received Green Flag status.

Name: Queendown Warren
Description: Queendown Warren is a 22.2-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south-east of Rainham in Kent.

Name: Queensbury Park
Description: Queensbury Park, in Harrow, is a site for river habitat improvements along Kenton Brook. The project engages local residents and schools in environmental activities, enhancing biodiversity and waterway health.

Name: Rabbitbank Wood
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 7 hectares.

Name: Rack Marsh
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Rack Marsh is a 4-hectare nature reserve in Bagnor, on the north-western outskirts of Newbury in Berkshire.  It is managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Rackenford and Knowstone Moors
Description: Rackenford and Knowstone Moors is a nature reserve of the Devon Wildlife Trust, situated about 8 miles north-west of Tiverton, in Devon, England.  The habitat is culm grassland.

Name: Radford Meadows
Description: Radford Meadows is a nature reserve of the Staffordshire Wildlife Trust, on the southern edge of Stafford, in Staffordshire, England.  The reserve is a floodplain situated between the River Penk to the west, and the Staffordshire and Worcestershire Canal.

Name: Ragpath Heath
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 4 hectares.

Name: Railway Fields
Description: Railway Fields is a local nature reserve in Haringey, North London, managed by The Conservation Volunteers. This former railway goods yard now boasts diverse habitats including woodland, meadow, and ponds, supporting various wildlife species. It serves as a vital urban green space and educational resource.

Name: Raincliffe Woods
Description: Raincliffe Woods is a 200-hectare woodland site near Scarborough, North Yorkshire. It comprises three distinct woodlands: Raincliffe, Forge Valley, and Lady Edith's. The site offers diverse habitats and recreational paths. It is managed for biodiversity, recreation, and education.

Name: Rainton Meadows
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 60 hectares.

Name: Raisby Hill Grassland
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 12 hectares.

Name: Rammey Marsh
Description: Rammey Marsh is a significant area of open space in Enfield, bordering the River Lee Navigation. This marshland habitat supports diverse flora and fauna, including water voles and kingfishers. It offers walking routes and connects to the wider Lee Valley Regional Park.

Name: Ramsey Island
Description: Ramsey Island, off the Pembrokeshire coast, is a rugged RSPB reserve. It provides vital habitat for grey seals, seabirds, and peregrine falcons. Its dramatic cliffs and coastline support diverse marine and avian life, managed for conservation.

Name: Ranscombe Farm
Description: Ranscombe Farm Reserve, located on the North Downs in Kent, is one of Kent's largest ancient woodlands and a designated Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI). It features globally important plantlife and wildlife, offering miles of footpaths through diverse habitats.

Name: Ranworth Broad
