Description: Ranworth Broad is a 136-hectare nature reserve on the Norfolk Broads north-east of Norwich in Norfolk, United Kingdom.  It is managed by the Norfolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Rathlin Island - Kebble NNR
HostOrg: Department of Agriculture, Environment and Rural Affairs (DAERA)
Description: Rathlin Island's Kebble NNR hosts significant seabird colonies, including puffins and guillemots, on its dramatic cliffs. The reserve features unique cliff-top flora, providing vital nesting habitats and is a key ecological site in Northern Ireland.

Name: Ravensroost Wood
Description: Ravensroost Wood is a 43.7 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in north Wiltshire, England.

Name: Ray Island
Description: Ray Island is a nature reserve featuring a sandy hill rising from extensive coastal saltmarsh between tidal channels.

Name: Rayleigh Castle
Description: Its large motte-and-bailey earthworks create a distinctive local landscape and valuable habitat for wildlife.

Name: Red Cross Garden
Description: Red Cross Garden is a historic Victorian garden established by Octavia Hill in 1887, located in Southwark, London. It features a tranquil pond, mature trees, and flowerbeds, offering a peaceful green space. The garden is open daily to the public for relaxation and community engagement.

Name: Red Moor (nature reserve)
Description: Red Moor is a nature reserve and Site of Special Scientific Interest, noted for its biological characteristics, near Lanlivery in mid Cornwall, England, UK.

Name: Red River Loscoe Nature Reserve
Description: Red River Loscoe Local Nature Reserve is an important site for nature conservation in north Amber Valley. Owned by Heanor & Loscoe Town Council, the 1.3-hectare site offers grassland, wetland, and woodland habitats. Accessible paths welcome walkers and nature enthusiasts.

Name: Redcar Field
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 0 hectares.

Name: Reddish Vale Country Park
Description: Reddish Vale Country Park spans 161 hectares in Stockport, Greater Manchester. It features woodlands, meadows, and riverside paths along the River Tame. The park offers walking, cycling, and horse riding, and is home to diverse wildlife and historical railway structures.

Name: Redesdale Peatland Pipeline
Description: The Redesdale Peatland Pipeline is a pilot project restoring degraded peatland in Northumberland, with key efforts focused on sites such as Whitelee Moor National Nature Reserve. It is a collaboration between Northumberland National Park Authority and Northumbrian Water. The 2023/24 phase involves contractors making significant progress on the restoration efforts.

Name: Redgrave and Lopham Fens
Description: Redgrave and Lopham Fens is a 127 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest between Thelnetham in Suffolk and Diss in Norfolk.  England.

Name: Redlake Cottage Meadows
Description: Redlake Meadows & Hoggs Moor is a Site of Special Scientific Interest, noted for its biological characteristics, in Cornwall, England, UK.  Within the SSSI is Redlake Cottage Meadows nature reserve owned by the Cornwall Wildlife Trust.

Name: Rendlesham Forest
Description: Venture into a captivating woodland where ancient trees create a dappled canopy, filtering sunlight onto a rich tapestry of flora. This expansive forest offers a haven for diverse wildlife, from shy deer to vibrant birdlife, inviting exploration on foot or by bike. Immerse yourself in the tranquility of nature, breathing in the fresh air and discovering the beauty of the natural world at your own pace.

Name: Reydon Wood
Description: Reydon Wood is a 16 hectare nature reserve west of Wangford in Suffolk, England.  It is managed by the Suffolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Ribble Estuary NNR
Description: The Ribble Estuary National Nature Reserve spans vast wetland, mudflat, and saltmarsh habitats in Lancashire. It provides critical overwintering grounds for thousands of wildfowl and wading birds, making it internationally important. Managed by Natural England and RSPB.

Name: Riddlesdown
Description: Riddlesdown Common or Riddlesdown is a 43 hectare area of green space in Kenley, towards the northern end of the North Downs in the London Borough of Croydon.  It is owned and maintained by the City of London Corporation, apart from two small areas, one of which is operated by the London Wildlife Trust and the other by Croydon Council.

Name: Ridley Bottom, Tidenham
Description: Ridley Bottom is a 1.1-hectare nature reserve in Gloucestershire.

Name: Ridlins Mire
Description: Ridlins Mire is a 1.6-hectare nature reserve managed by the Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust in Stevenage, Hertfordshire, England.

Name: Rievaulx Terrace & Temples
Description: Discover this wooded escarpment in the North York Moors National Park, featuring a grass terrace with panoramic views.

Name: Rimrose Valley Country Park
Description: Rimrose Valley Country Park is a vital green space in Sefton, Merseyside, offering a haven for wildlife and local communities. The Friends group actively works to protect, enhance, and promote this significant natural asset.

Name: Ringstead Downs
Description: Ringstead Downs is a 6.9-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest east of Hunstanton in Norfolk, England.

Name: Risley Moss Local Nature Reserve
Description: Risley Moss Local Nature Reserve, a former Royal Ordnance Factory site in Warrington, features diverse habitats including woodland, heathland, and mossland. It provides a visitor centre, observation tower, and walking trails for public access and wildlife observation.

Name: River Alde
Description: The River Alde and River Ore form a river system in Suffolk, England passing by Snape and Aldeburgh.  The River Alde and River Ore meet northwest of Blaxhall.

Name: River Arrow Nature Reserve
Description: River Arrow Nature Reserve is a local nature reserve located alongside the River Arrow in Alcester, Warwickshire, England.  Established by Stratford-on-Avon District Council and English Nature, the reserve aims to benefit the Alcester community by preserving its habitat and providing an educational resource for local schools to study wildlife.

Name: River Black Bourn
Description: Black Bourn Valley, formerly called Grove Farm, is an 88 hectare nature reserve between Thurston and Elmswell in Suffolk.  It is managed by the Suffolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: River Derwent, Derbyshire
Description: The Derwent is a river in Derbyshire, England.  It is 50 miles long and is a tributary of the River Trent, which it joins south of Derby.

Name: River Lea Regional Park - Waterden
Description: River Lea Regional Park - Waterden forms part of the Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park in East London. It features significant wetland habitats, meadows, and the River Lea, supporting diverse wildlife including birds, insects, and aquatic species. The area contributes to urban biodiversity.

Name: River Lee Country Park
Description: River Lee Country Park, part of the Lee Valley Regional Park, offers diverse habitats like wetlands, grasslands, woodlands, supporting wildlife. The park features trails for walking, cycling, horse riding, watersports and fishing.

Name: River Mimram
Description: The River Mimram is a chalk stream in Hertfordshire, England.  It runs from its source near Whitwell in Hertfordshire to join the River Lea at Hertford.

Name: River Oughton
Description: The River Oughton is a two mile long tributary of the River Hiz in North Hertfordshire, England.  It rises at Oughtonhead and flows north-east between Oughtonhead Common and Oughtonhead Nature Reserve.

Name: River Roding
Description: The River Roding is a river that rises at Molehill Green, Essex, England.  It then flows south through Essex and London, forming Barking Creek as it reaches the River Thames.

Name: River Rom, The Chase LNR
Description: The Rewilding the Rom project focuses on enhancing river habitats and increasing biodiversity along the River Rom. Located within the London Borough of Havering, this initiative undertakes habitat restoration work to improve the ecological health of the river.

Name: River Stour, Suffolk
Description: The River Stour is a major river in eastern England.  It is 47 miles long and forms most of the county boundary between Suffolk to the north, and Essex to the south.

Name: River Waveney
Description: The River Waveney is a river which forms the boundary between Suffolk and Norfolk, England, for much of its length within The Broads.  The earliest attestation of the name is from 1275, Wahenhe, from *wagen + ea, meaning the river by a quagmire.

Name: River Welland
Description: The River Welland is a lowland river in the east of England, some 65 miles long.  It drains part of the Midlands eastwards to The Wash.

Name: Riverside Country Park
Description: Riverside Country Park, Medway Estuary, covers 100 hectares of varied habitats including saltmarsh, coastal grazing marsh, and two Local Nature Reserves. It offers footpaths, cycling, picnic areas, and birdwatching, supporting significant wildlife.

Name: Robert's Field
Description: Lincolnshire Gate is the name given to a corner in the road between Holywell, Lincolnshire and Pickworth, Rutland to the south-west of Castle Bytham, in Lincolnshire, England.  It is situated approximately 5 miles north from Stamford.

Name: Robin Wood
Description: This expansive woodland in the heart of the Midlands offers a haven for diverse wildlife, with ancient trees providing a canopy for birdsong and a habitat for woodland creatures. Visitors can explore a network of trails, perfect for invigorating walks and scenic cycling routes, immersing themselves in the tranquility of nature and discovering its hidden beauty. It's a place to connect with the natural world, breathing in fresh air and experiencing the vibrant life that thrives within its leafy embrace.

Name: Rochdale Woodlands
Description: Explore a vibrant tapestry of ancient woodlands and open meadows in this sprawling Northern English forest. Discover a haven for diverse wildlife, from elusive deer to a symphony of bird songs, as you wander scenic walking trails and winding cycling routes. Immerse yourself in the tranquility of nature and the beauty of the changing seasons.

Name: Rockcliffe, Dumfries and Galloway
Description: This coastal village in Dumfries and Galloway overlooks the Solway Firth and River Urr estuary, with tidal access to Rough Island.

Name: Rocky Plantation
Description: Rocky Plantation is a 3.4-hectare nature reserve north of Markfield in Leicestershire.

Name: Rodborough Common
Description: Rodborough Common is a 62.2-hectare Local Nature Reserve west of Milford in Surrey.

Name: Roding Valley Meadows
Description: Roding Valley Meadows is an 18.9-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Buckhurst Hill in Essex.

Name: Rogate Woods
Description: Ancient trees canopy a network of trails, inviting exploration through a vibrant tapestry of woodlands teeming with diverse wildlife. Discover hidden glades, listen to the songs of woodland birds, and breathe in the fresh, earthy air on a walk or cycle through this special place. It's a haven for nature lovers, offering a chance to reconnect with the natural world.

Name: Roman River Valley
Description: Roman River Valley is a 17.8-hectare nature reserve north of Layer de la Haye in Essex.

Name: Romney Marsh
Description: Romney Warren or Romney Marsh is a 10.9-hectare country park and Local Nature Reserve in New Romney in Kent.

Name: Romney Marsh Visitor Centre and Nature Reserve
Description: Romney Warren Local Nature Reserve is an 11-hectare Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) featuring dune grassland, willow scrub, and seasonal ponds. It is home to nationally important populations of Great Crested Newts and Great Silver Beetles, as well as rare medicinal leeches and diverse dragonfly and damselfly species. The reserve offers accessible pathways and walking trails for visitors to explore its rich biodiversity. The former Romney Marsh Visitor Centre on site is now operated as 'The Nest' (a cafe and retail space), while the nature reserve itself is managed by the Romney Marsh Countryside Partnership.

Name: Romney Warren Local Nature Reserve
Description: Romney Warren Local Nature Reserve, managed by the Romney Marsh Countryside Partnership, offers footpaths, a pond, woods, and wildflower meadows for exploration. The site is adjacent to 'The Nest', a re-opened visitor centre.

Name: Ros Hill
Description: This prominent hill offers sweeping panoramic views across purple heather moorland and the captivating Chillingham cattle park.

Name: Roseberry Topping
Description: Roseberry Topping is a distinctive North Yorkshire hill, famed for its half-cone shape, jagged cliff, and panoramic views across the North York Moors.

Name: Rosenannon Downs
Description: Rosenannon Downs is a nature reserve in mid Cornwall, England, UK, being designated Rosenannon Bog and Downs Site of Special Scientific Interest, noted for its biological characteristics.  The site supports a wide variety of flora and fauna and includes Bronze Age barrows.

Name: Rosliston Forestry Centre
Description: Rosliston Forestry Centre, a gateway site to the National Forest, offers woodlands, ponds, and meadows. Visitors enjoy walking trails, a children's play area, and a café. The centre, owned by South Derbyshire District Council, also hosts various events and educational programmes.

Name: Rosliston Forestry Centre
Description: Explore a vast expanse of ancient woodland and diverse habitats teeming with wildlife, from soaring birds of prey to shy woodland creatures. Wander along miles of scenic trails, perfect for walking and cycling, offering immersive experiences amidst the natural beauty of the Midlands. Discover a peaceful sanctuary where you can connect with nature and enjoy the simple pleasures of the great outdoors.

Name: Roudsea Wood and Mosses NNR
Description: Roudsea Wood and Mosses NNR comprises ancient woodlands, raised bogs, saltmarsh, and intertidal mudflats on the Leven Estuary in Cumbria. This diverse site supports a rich array of wildlife, including rare insects and plants.

Name: Roughtor
Description: This expansive woodland in the South West of England offers a haven for diverse wildlife, from soaring birds of prey to shy woodland mammals, amidst ancient trees and rolling hills. Visitors can explore miles of trails, perfect for invigorating walks or cycling adventures, immersing themselves in the rich natural beauty and peaceful atmosphere. It's a place to connect with nature, breathe in fresh air, and discover the vibrant life that thrives within its depths.

Name: Roundhouse, Birmingham
Description: Experience Birmingham's urban waterways and canal-side landscapes through walking, cycling, kayaking, and paddleboarding tours.

Name: Roundton Hill
Description: Roundton Hill is a rounded, steep sided, 1,210 feet hill, volcanic in origin, in the easternmost part of old Montgomeryshire, Wales, which juts into the English border near Church Stoke.  It is managed as a nature reserve by the Montgomeryshire Wildlife Trust, who acquired it in 1985.

Name: Roxbourne Park
Description: Roxbourne Park in Harrow features diverse habitats, including Yeading Brook, woodland, and open grassland. Thames21 partners with local groups to enhance the park's biodiversity and improve river health within the London Borough of Harrow.

Name: Roydon Common and Grimston Warren
Description: Roydon Common is a 194.9-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest east of King's Lynn in Norfolk, England.

Name: Roydon Fen
Description: Roydon Fen is a 17.2 hectare Local Nature Reserve south of Roydon, on the western outskirts of Diss in Norfolk.

Name: Roydon Woods
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Roydon Woods is a 294.9-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest near Brockenhurst in Hampshire.

Name: RSPB Adur Estuary
Description: Adur Estuary offers important intertidal mudflats and saltmarsh habitats for birds such as turnstone, dunlin, and grey plover. Located near Shoreham-by-Sea, it is a key site for overwintering waders and wildfowl, protected from development. The estuary supports a diverse ecosystem within a dynamic coastal environment.

Name: RSPB Adwick Washlands
Description: Adwick Washland is a developing wetland reserve in South Yorkshire, offering diverse habitats for wildlife. The site features new reedbeds, ponds, and grassland areas, attracting various bird species. It provides accessible trails and hides for visitors.

Name: RSPB Bempton Cliffs
Description: RSPB Bempton Cliffs is a significant seabird colony on the Yorkshire coast, hosting around half a million birds, including gannets, puffins, and kittiwakes, between March and October. Visitors can observe nesting birds from cliff-edge viewpoints.

Name: RSPB Blacktoft Sands
Description: RSPB Blacktoft Sands is England's largest tidal reedbed, on the Humber Estuary. It provides vital habitat for avocets, marsh harriers, and bearded tits. The reserve features hides and accessible trails for birdwatching and observing wetland wildlife.

Name: RSPB Brading Marshes
Description: Brading Marshes is the Isle of Wight's largest wetland, managed by RSPB. It provides a vital habitat for marsh harriers, bitterns, and water voles. Visitors use walking trails and hides to observe diverse wildlife across the former tidal estuary. It offers a significant haven for birds and insects.

Name: RSPB Buckenham Marshes
Description: RSPB Buckenham Marshes, located in the Yare Valley, is a nature reserve known for wintering wildfowl and raptors like marsh harriers and peregrines. The reserve features wet grassland habitats, attracting diverse bird species throughout the year.

Name: RSPB Burton Mere Wetlands
Description: RSPB Burton Mere Wetlands is a wildlife haven on the Dee Estuary, featuring pools, reedbeds, and wet grassland. It hosts avocets, lapwings, and ducks, offering a visitor centre, hides, and trails for nature observation.

Name: RSPB Campfield Marsh
Description: RSPB Campfield Marsh is a vast expanse of saltmarsh, wet grassland, and peatbog on the Solway Estuary in Cumbria. It supports significant populations of breeding waders, wildfowl, and natterjack toads. Visitors can explore various trails and hides, observing diverse birdlife.

Name: RSPB Coombes Valley and Consall Woods
Description: Consall Woods, part of the RSPB Coombes Valley reserve in Staffordshire, features ancient woodland, grasslands, and a stream. The site, with a history of mining, supports diverse wildlife including woodpeckers and flycatchers, offering peaceful walking trails for visitors.

Name: RSPB Dearne Valley - Adwick Sands
Description: RSPB Adwick Washlands, formerly known as Adwick Sands, is a satellite site of the RSPB Dearne Valley reserve in South Yorkshire. This area features managed wetlands and grassland, attracting a variety of birdlife, including wading birds and waterfowl throughout the year.

Name: RSPB Dee Estuary - Parkgate Saltmarsh
Description: The Dee Estuary's Parkgate saltmarsh offers expansive tidal habitats, a key site for wintering raptors like short-eared owls, hen harriers, and peregrines. Waders and geese feed here, making it a prime birdwatching location with easy footpath access.

Name: RSPB Dee Estuary - Point of Ayr
Description: RSPB Dee Estuary - Point of Ayr is a coastal reserve with dunes, saltmarsh, and mudflats. It is a vital habitat for migrant waders, warblers, and raptors. Visitors can also spot natterjack toads and sand lizards within its diverse ecosystems.

Name: RSPB Dove Stone
Description: RSPB Dove Stone, near Greenfield, Oldham, is a partnership site focusing on blanket bog restoration within the Peak District National Park. Conservation work improves water quality, biodiversity, and carbon capture in the South Pennines.

Name: RSPB Fairhaven Lake
Description: Fairhaven Lake is a coastal hub on the Ribble Estuary, Lancashire, known for its diverse bird species, including overwintering waders and wildfowl. While the RSPB previously managed the visitor centre at this site, they continue their vital nature conservation efforts across the wider Ribble Estuary. The area offers various outdoor activities.

Name: RSPB Farnham Heath
Description: RSPB Farnham Heath is a restored heathland site in Surrey, managed by the RSPB. It features a mosaic of open heath, woodland, and ponds, providing habitats for rare birds like woodlark and nightjar, as well as sand lizards and slow worms. Visitors can explore walking trails.

Name: RSPB Fowlmere
Description: RSPB Fowlmere is a chalk stream fed wetland reserve in Cambridgeshire, offering habitats for diverse wildlife. Reedbeds and open water support breeding kingfishers, garganey, and water rails. Water voles thrive here. Accessible trails provide visitor access.

Name: RSPB Frampton Marsh
Description: Frampton Marsh is an RSPB nature reserve on the Lincolnshire coast, part of The Wash estuary. It features saltmarsh, freshwater scrapes, and reedbeds. This site provides vital feeding and breeding grounds for thousands of migratory and resident birds.

Name: RSPB Havergate Island
Description: Havergate Island is the RSPB's only island reserve, home to avocets, terns and gulls. Accessible only by boat, it features saline lagoons and mudflats, providing vital habitat for wading birds and other wildlife. Guided visits are offered.

Name: RSPB Haweswater
Description: RSPB Haweswater is an upland nature reserve in the Lake District, managed with United Utilities. The site focuses on habitat restoration and protecting species such as golden eagles and red squirrels. Various walking trails are available.

Name: RSPB Hazeley Heath
Description: Hazeley Heath is an important area of lowland heathland in Hampshire, providing a home for Dartford warblers, woodlarks, and nightjars. It features heather, gorse, and birch, offering a diverse habitat. The site is actively managed for nature conservation.

Name: RSPB Hesketh Out Marsh
Description: RSPB Hesketh Out Marsh is a managed realignment site on the Ribble Estuary. Formerly farmland, it transformed into intertidal saltmarsh and mudflat, supporting diverse wading birds and wildfowl, especially in winter. Saline lagoons and ditches are present.

Name: RSPB Lakenheath Fen
Description: RSPB Lakenheath Fen is a large wetland reserve in Suffolk, England. Created from arable land, it features reedbeds, wet grasslands, and open water, attracting diverse wildlife including cranes, bitterns, and marsh harriers. Trails and hides are available.

Name: RSPB Langstone Harbour
Description: RSPB Langstone Harbour protects vital islands in South East England for nesting seabirds and waders. This important Ramsar site supports overwintering bird populations. Public access is limited to the harbour's shoreline, offering observation points.

Name: RSPB Leighton Moss
Description: RSPB Leighton Moss is the largest reedbed in north-west England, near Silverdale. It hosts diverse wildlife, including otters, bearded tits, and marsh harriers. The reserve features accessible trails, hides, and a visitor centre. Coastal habitats are present, supporting a variety of bird species.

Name: RSPB Lyddon Meadow
Description: Lyddon Meadow is a chalk grassland reserve near Lydden, Dover, within the Kent Downs AONB. This site supports a rich diversity of wildflowers and insects, including the Adonis blue butterfly. Conservation efforts focus on maintaining its unimproved grassland habitat.

Name: RSPB Marshside
Description: Marshside is a coastal reserve on the Ribble estuary, featuring a mosaic of saltmarsh and wet grassland. It attracts thousands of wintering ducks, geese, and wading birds. Two hides offer views of species like avocets, lapwings, and golden plovers.

Name: RSPB North Warren
Description: North Warren is an RSPB reserve on the Suffolk coast, featuring a mosaic of woodland, reedbed, grassland, and heath habitats. It supports woodlarks, nightjars, Dartford warblers, and diverse invertebrates. Visitors can explore marked trails and observe the wildlife.

Name: RSPB Northward Hill
Description: RSPB Northward Hill hosts the UK's largest heronry, alongside extensive ancient woodland, grazing marsh, and arable land. This Medway Estuary reserve supports diverse wildlife, including breeding herons, egrets, and raptors, offering walking trails.

Name: RSPB Otmoor
Description: RSPB Otmoor is a wetland mosaic in Oxfordshire, created from former arable land. It provides habitat for wading birds such as snipe and lapwing, and supports numerous wintering wildfowl. Reedbeds are home to marsh harriers and bitterns, making it a key site for birdwatching.

Name: RSPB Ouse Washes
Description: RSPB Ouse Washes is a significant floodplain wetland in Cambridgeshire, providing crucial habitat for wintering wildfowl and breeding waders. The reserve features wet grassland, ditches, and reedbeds, playing a vital role in flood storage for the region.

Name: RSPB Point of Ayr
Description: Point of Ayr is a vital high-tide roost for waders and wildfowl at the Dee Estuary mouth. Coastal marsh, saltmarsh, and sand dunes provide habitats. It attracts gulls, terns, and wintering hen harriers. Located on Wales' northernmost tip.

Name: RSPB Pulborough Brooks
Description: RSPB Pulborough Brooks is a wetland nature reserve in the Arun Valley, West Sussex. It comprises wet grasslands, woodlands, and heathland, providing habitat for diverse birdlife including ducks, geese, and waders. Visitors can explore nature trails and hides.

Name: RSPB Rainham Marshes
Description: RSPB Rainham Marshes is a significant nature reserve located in Purfleet, Essex, protecting diverse habitats including extensive marshland, reedbeds, and grasslands. It supports numerous bird species, insects, and water voles. The reserve features well-maintained walking trails, multiple bird hides, and a modern visitor centre offering educational programmes and wildlife observation opportunities. It focuses on vital conservation efforts and public access to nature.

Name: RSPB Ribble Discovery Centre
Description: The Ribble Discovery Centre, on Lytham seafront, offers information about the Ribble Estuary's wildlife and conservation. Visitors explore interactive displays and events, learning about this vital National Nature Reserve. It serves as a gateway to understanding the estuary's ecology.

Name: RSPB Rye Meads
Description: Rye Meads is a wetland reserve on the River Lea, offering diverse habitats like reedbeds and wet grassland. It provides excellent birdwatching opportunities with several hides, making it a key site for waterfowl and migrating birds in Hertfordshire.

Name: RSPB Saltholme
Description: RSPB Saltholme is a nature reserve on Teesside, between Stockton-on-Tees and Hartlepool. The site features wetlands and grasslands, providing crucial habitats for diverse bird species and wildlife. Visitors explore trails, hides, and a visitor centre.

Name: RSPB Snettisham
Description: RSPB Snettisham is a coastal reserve on The Wash in Norfolk, known for its large numbers of wading birds. Thousands of knots, oystercatchers, and godwits feed on the mudflats. High tides push vast flocks closer to the shoreline and hides, creating a spectacular natural event.

Name: RSPB South Stack Cliffs
Description: South Stack Cliffs, near Holyhead, is an RSPB reserve on Anglesey, North Wales. It features dramatic cliffs and heathland, home to guillemots, razorbills, and puffins during breeding season. Visitors observe seabirds and choughs from viewing points.

Name: RSPB St Aidan's
Description: RSPB St Aidan's is a 400-hectare wetland reserve near Leeds, built on a former open-cast coal mine. It features reedbeds, lakes, and grasslands, providing habitat for various bird species and offering visitor walking routes.

Name: RSPB St Bees Head
Description: St Bees Head is England's only cliff-nesting colony of seabirds, located on the Cumbrian coast. It offers stunning views, significant geological features, and a thriving wildlife habitat for species like guillemots and razorbills.

Name: RSPB Strumpshaw Fen
Description: RSPB Strumpshaw Fen is a significant wetland reserve in the Broads, Norfolk. It features extensive reedbeds, grazing marsh, and wet woodland, supporting rare wildlife. Visitors can explore trails, hides, and an accessible boardwalk, observing marsh harriers, bitterns, and swallowtail butterflies. The site focuses on conservation and habitat management.

Name: RSPB Tetney Marshes
Description: Tetney Marshes is a coastal reserve on the Humber Estuary. It consists of saltmarsh, mudflats, and sand dunes, providing habitats for various wading birds and wildfowl, especially during migration periods. The site is a Ramsar wetland of international importance.

Name: RSPB Titchwell Marsh
HostOrg: Royal Society for the Protection of Birds
Description: RSPB Titchwell Marsh is a coastal wetland reserve in Norfolk, offering diverse habitats from reedbeds and saltmarsh to a sandy beach. It provides a vital stop-over for migratory birds and supports various resident species throughout the year.

Name: RSPB Valley Wetlands
Description: RSPB Valley Wetlands, Anglesey, Wales, is a significant wetland habitat. It features shallow lakes, reedbeds, and wet grasslands, supporting diverse birdlife. It provides breeding grounds and overwintering areas for wildfowl and waders.

Name: RSPB Wolves Wood
Description: Wolves Wood is an ancient woodland reserve in Suffolk, managed by the RSPB. It features a diverse mix of tree species, including oak, ash, and hazel, supporting varied wildlife. Accessible trails allow visitors to explore the peaceful habitats.

Name: Rufford Country Park
Description: Rufford Country Park features the historic Rufford Abbey ruins, gardens, and woodland walks. Visitors can explore a lake, craft centre, and various outdoor activities. The park provides family-friendly events and educational opportunities.

Name: Rufford Old Hall
Description: Explore the charming Victorian gardens, featuring unique topiary squirrels amidst lush planting.

Name: Ruislip Woods National Nature Reserve
Description: Ruislip Woods National Nature Reserve is a significant ancient woodland in the London Borough of Hillingdon. It encompasses Mad Bess Wood, Copse Wood, Manor Farm, and Park Wood. The site features diverse habitats, supporting varied flora and fauna.

Name: Runfold Wood
Description: Runfold Wood is a 12-hectare nature reserve east of Farnham in Surrey.  It is managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Runnymede
Description: Runnymede offers expansive water-meadows along the River Thames and adjoining hillsides, providing diverse habitats.

Name: Rushbeds Wood
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Rushbeds Wood is a 56-hectare nature reserve near Wotton Underwood in Buckinghamshire, managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust.  It is a surviving fragment of the ancient Bernwood Forest.

Name: Rushy Mead
Description: Rushy Mead is a 4.6-hectare nature reserve on the bank of the River Stort in Essex, between Sawbridgeworth and Bishop's Stortford.

Name: Russia Dock Woodland
Description: Russia Dock Woodland in Rotherhithe, London, is a diverse urban woodland and ecological park managed by The Conservation Volunteers. Weekly volunteer sessions maintain its wildlife habitats. It offers green space for local communities and supports urban biodiversity.

Name: Rutland Water
Description: Rutland Water is a reservoir, an artificial lake, in Rutland, England, east of Rutland's county town, Oakham.  It is filled by pumping from the River Nene and River Welland, and provides water to the East Midlands.

Name: Ruxley Gravel Pits
Description: Ruxley Gravel Pits is an 18.7-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Ruxley, Orpington, in the London Borough of Bromley, and originally dug between 1929 and 1951.

Name: Rye Harbour
Description: Rye Harbour LNR is a 325.4-hectare local nature reserve in Rye in East Sussex.

Name: Rye Meads
Description: Rye Meads is a 58.5-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Rye House, Hoddesdon, Hertfordshire.

Name: Salcey Forest
Description: Ancient woodland stretches across this Forestry England site, offering a haven for diverse wildlife within its dappled light. Visitors can wander through mature trees, cycle along winding paths, and immerse themselves in the sights and sounds of nature. It's a place to breathe deep and discover the beauty of a thriving woodland ecosystem.

Name: Sale Water Park
Description: Sale Water Park is a large country park in Sale, Greater Manchester, covering 152 acres around a lake. It offers water sports, walking trails, and diverse wildlife habitats for visitors to explore and enjoy.

Name: Salmonsbury Meadows SSSI
Description: Salmonsbury Meadows is an 18-hectare biological and geological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Gloucestershire, notified in 1985.  The site is listed in the 'Cotswold District' Local Plan 2001-2011 as a Key Wildlife Site.

Name: Saltbox Hill
Description: Saltbox Hill is a 22.2 biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in three separate areas in Biggin Hill in the London Borough of Bromley.

Name: Saltfleetby – Threddlethorpe Dunes
Description: Saltfleetby-Theddlethorpe Dunes is a national nature reserve on the coast of Lincolnshire, England, in the parishes of Saltfleetby and Theddlethorpe.  It is managed in part by Natural England; in part by the Lincolnshire Wildlife Trust, and consists of 1,377 acres of sand dunes, salt marsh, sand and mudflats.

Name: Salthill Quarry
Description: Salthill Quarry is a nature reserve of the Wildlife Trust for Lancashire, Manchester and North Merseyside, near Clitheroe in Lancashire.  It is a local nature reserve and a Site of Special Scientific Interest, notable as a site of fossilised remains of crinoids.

Name: Salthouse Marshes
Description: Salthouse Marshes is a 66-hectare nature reserve west of Sheringham in Norfolk.  It is managed by the Norfolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Saltwells Nature Reserve
Description: Saltwells National Nature Reserve is 100 hectares of ancient woodland, grassland, and wetlands in Dudley, West Midlands. It features diverse habitats, including multiple geological Sites of Special Scientific Interest (SSSIs), and is home to a variety of wildlife. A sculpture trail is present, but there is no dedicated visitor centre.

Name: Samphire Hoe
Description: Samphire Hoe is 30 hectares of restored coastal land between Dover and Folkestone, created from Channel Tunnel excavations. It opened in 1997 and is now an internationally recognised nature reserve, a haven for diverse wildlife, and offers recreational and educational opportunities.

Name: Sand Point, Somerset
Description: Sand Point offers dramatic coastal views across the Bristol Channel, featuring a biologically and geologically significant SSSI with scarce plants like the Cheddar pink.

Name: Sanday, Inner Hebrides
Description: Sanday, an Inner Hebridean tidal island, showcases some of Scotland's youngest volcanic rocks and is linked to Canna by sandbanks.

Name: Sandham Memorial Chapel
Description: Surrounded by peaceful lawns and traditional orchards, the property offers expansive views across the iconic Watership Down landscape.

Name: Sandilands, Lincolnshire
Description: Sandilands features dynamic coastal habitats with expansive sandy beaches and valuable dune systems, supporting diverse wildlife and unique plant communities.

Name: Sandown Meadows
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 17 hectares.

Name: Sandscale Haws
Description: Sandscale Haws National Nature Reserve protects coastal habitats on the Duddon Estuary, providing a vital home for rare natterjack toads.

Name: Sandwell Valley
Description: RSPB Sandwell Valley is a nature reserve located within the broader Sandwell Valley Country Park in the West Midlands. It focuses on wildlife conservation, particularly around Forge Mill Lake, and offers bird hides and nature trails. The wider country park, a Green Flag award-winner, also features two lakes, a golf course, and provides access to Forge Mill Farm and Sandwell Park Farm.

Name: Sandwich and Pegwell Bay
Description: Sandwich and Pegwell Bay is a 615-hectare nature reserve in Kent, managed by the Kent Wildlife Trust.  It is a National Nature Reserve, and it includes a Geological Conservation Review site, Prince's Beachlands Local Nature Reserve and two Special Areas of Conservation, Sandwich Bay and Thanet Coast.

Name: Sandylay and Moat Woods
Description: Sandylay and Moat Woods is a 7.5-hectare nature reserve east of Great Leighs in Essex.

Name: Santon Downham
Description: This vast expanse of ancient woodland offers a haven of natural beauty, where towering trees create a dappled canopy over winding paths. Explore a rich tapestry of wildlife, from elusive deer to vibrant birdlife, as you wander through this serene landscape. It's a perfect destination for walkers and cyclists seeking immersion in nature's tranquility and opportunities for quiet contemplation.

Name: Santon Historical Site
Description: This ancient woodland in South East England offers a haven for wildlife, with dappled sunlight filtering through mature trees onto carpets of bluebells in spring. Explore winding paths perfect for walking and cycling, immersing yourself in the sights and sounds of nature, from chattering birds to the rustle of unseen creatures. It's a place to connect with the wild, breathe fresh air, and discover the enduring beauty of a thriving forest ecosystem.

Name: Sapperton Valley
Description: Sapperton Valley is a 3.7-hectare nature reserve near Chalford in the Stroud district of Gloucestershire, England.

Name: Savernake Forest
Description: This ancient woodland, managed by Forestry England, offers a haven of natural beauty where towering trees create a dappled canopy. Explore its winding paths and discover a rich tapestry of wildlife, from elusive deer to vibrant birdlife, all while enjoying opportunities for invigorating walks and peaceful cycles amidst the serene surroundings. It's a place to reconnect with nature and experience the wild heart of South East England.

Name: Sawbridgeworth Marsh
Description: Sawbridgeworth Marsh is a 6.3-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest near Sawbridgeworth in Hertfordshire, apart from a small area in the north which is in Essex.

Name: Sayes Court
Description: Sayes Court is a historic garden site in Deptford, South East London, once home to John Evelyn. It features community gardens, orchards, and open green space, developed and maintained by local volunteers.

Name: Scalby Beck Nature Reserve
Description: Scalby Beck Nature Reserve is a 24-hectare site near Scarborough, North Yorkshire, launching in 2026. This project aims to enhance biodiversity, improve water quality, and provide flood protection along Scalby Beck. It offers public access.

Name: Scarning Fen
Description: Scarning Fen is a 4-hectare nature reserve west in Dereham in Norfolk.  It is managed by the Norfolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Scoska Wood
Description: Scoska Wood is a limestone ash wood and pasture located in Littondale, North Yorkshire, between the villages of Litton and Arncliffe. It is a National Nature Reserve and Site of Special Scientific Interest, known for its ancient woodland, ash trees, and diverse flora and fauna, including rare moths and limestone grassland species.

Name: Scotney Castle
Description: Scotney Castle's picturesque SSSI gardens surround a moated lake with an island, set amidst sloping woodlands rich in seasonal flora.

Name: Sculthorpe Moor
Description: Sculthorpe Moor is a Norfolk nature reserve managed by the Hawk and Owl Trust. It features wetlands, woodlands, and reedbeds, supporting diverse bird species and wildlife. Accessible boardwalks and hides provide visitor exploration opportunities year-round.

Name: Seaford Head
Description: Seaford Head is a 150.2-hectare Local Nature Reserve east of Seaford in East Sussex.

Name: Seale Chalk Pit and Meadow
Description: Seale Chalk Pit is a 1.2-hectare geological Site of Special Scientific Interest west of Guildford in Surrey.

Name: Seale Wood
Description: This ancient woodland offers a haven for diverse wildlife, with winding trails inviting exploration through a tapestry of trees. Discover a rich natural environment where you can immerse yourself in walking, cycling, and simply enjoying the beauty of nature. It's a place to connect with the wild and experience the tranquility of the Midlands countryside.

Name: Seasalter Levels
Description: Seasalter Levels is a significant wetland site near Whitstable, Kent, managed primarily by the RSPB in partnership with organizations including Kent Wildlife Trust and Canterbury City Council. It comprises freshwater grazing marsh and has undergone extensive restoration to create mosaic habitats. The reserve is crucial for breeding and wintering waterbirds, enhancing local biodiversity, and contributes to flood resilience and water quality in the area. Its size has expanded through restoration efforts, now encompassing a substantial area of wetland habitat.

Name: Seaton Delaval Hall
Description: Seaton Delaval Hall features expansive gardens, adding ecological value to the Northumberland coastal landscape.

Name: Sefton Meadows
Description: This expansive woodland in Northern England invites exploration with its ancient trees and vibrant undergrowth, offering a haven for diverse wildlife. Wander or cycle through its dappled light, discovering hidden glades and listening to the symphony of birdsong. It's a place to immerse yourself in nature's embrace and experience the simple joy of the outdoors.

Name: Selborne Common

Name: Selsdon Wood

Name: Selwyns Wood

Wander winding paths through towering trees, listen to the birdsong, and keep an eye out for deer grazing in the dappled sunlight. This expansive woodland offers a refreshing escape for walkers and cyclists to immerse themselves in the beauty of the natural world.

Name: Setmurthy

Visitors can immerse themselves in the natural beauty, exploring winding trails perfect for walking and cycling amidst ancient trees and vibrant flora. It's a place to connect with nature, breathing in the fresh air and discovering the hidden wonders of this captivating landscape.

Name: Seven Barrows

Description: Seven Barrows is a Bronze Age bowl barrow cemetery, 4-hectare of which are designated a biological Site of Special Scientific Interest, at Upper Lambourn in the civil parish of Lambourn in the English county of Berkshire.  It is managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust and it is a Scheduled Monument.

Name: Seven Sisters Country Park
Description: Seven Sisters Country Park is a 280-hectare nature reserve in East Sussex, featuring iconic chalk cliffs, river valley, and grassland. It offers walking, birdwatching, cycling, and canoeing. A visitor centre provides information about the park.

Name: Sevenoaks Wildlife Reserve
Description: Sevenoaks Gravel Pits is a 73.7-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest on the northern outskirts of Sevenoaks in Kent.

Name: Sewardstone Marsh
Description: Sewardstone Marsh is a large marshland area in the Lee Valley Regional Park, known for its diverse birdlife and wetland habitats. It features walking trails and provides important breeding grounds for various waterfowl and migratory species within a protected nature reserve.

Name: Shabden Park
Description: Shabden Park is a 103-hectare nature reserve in Chipstead in Surrey.  It is owned by Surrey County Council who manage the woodland areas, while the Surrey Wildlife Trust manage the grassland.

Name: Shadwell Wood
Description: Hales and Shadwell Woods is a 15.4-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north-east of Saffron Walden in Essex.

Name: Shaptor Woods
Description: Shaptor Woods near Bovey Tracey has a mix of ancient semi-natural woodland, conifer plantation and regenerating broadleaf. The site is notable for its birdlife and is home to dormice. It features walking routes and is part of the East Dartmoor Woods and Heaths SSSI.

Name: Shapwick Heath NNR
Description: Shapwick Heath NNR, part of the Somerset Levels and Moors, is a diverse wetland mosaic. Habitats include reedbeds, fens, open water, grassland, and woodland. It supports otters, bitterns, and marsh harriers. The site holds Ramsar and SAC status.

Name: Shapwick Moor
Description: Shapwick Moor Nature Reserve, owned by the Hawk and Owl Trust, provides habitats for wintering and breeding wading birds, otters, owls, and raptors. It forms part of the Avalon Marshes landscape in Somerset.

Name: Sharpham Moor Plot
Description: Sharpham Moor Plot is a 0.5-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest at Sharpham in Somerset, UK, notified in 1967.

Name: Sheepleas

Name: Sheringham Park
Description: Sheringham Park features diverse mature woodlands, an extensive collection of rhododendrons, azaleas, and magnolias, offering expansive coastal views.

Name: Sherwood Forest National Nature Reserve

It protects England's largest collection of ancient oak trees, including the Major Oak, and supports diverse wildlife. The site is a significant cultural landscape linked to Robin Hood legends.

Name: Sherwood Heath
Description: Sherwood Heath is a Nottinghamshire nature reserve. It features ancient oak woodland, plantation woodland, and lowland heath. The site supports specialist heathland invertebrates, woodcock, and tree pipit, with areas of managed open heathland.

Name: Sherwood Pines

Name: Silk Stream

Name: Simonside

This wild and beautiful setting offers endless opportunities for invigorating walks and cycling adventures amidst breathtaking natural scenery.

Name: Sissinghurst Castle Garden
Description: This garden boasts an internationally respected plant collection, particularly its old garden roses, considered one of the finest in the world.

Name: Sizergh Castle & Garden
Description: Sizergh Castle & Garden's estate and beautiful gardens are nestled within the scenic landscapes of the Lake District National Park.

Name: Sizewell Belts
Description: Sizewell Marshes form a 260-acre biological Site of Special Scientific Interest adjacent to Sizewell in Suffolk.  It is in the Suffolk Coast and Heaths Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, and is part of a 356-acre nature reserve managed by the Suffolk Wildlife Trust as Sizewell Belts.

Name: Skinflats Marsh
Description: Skinflats Marsh is a coastal wetland, part of the Inner Forth SSSI, providing vital habitats for wintering and breeding wildfowl and wading birds. Features saltmarsh and reedbed areas, supporting otters and the rare sea aster mining bee.

Name: Skip Garden King's Cross
Description: The Skip Garden in King's Cross is a community food growing garden, kitchen, and educational space. It uses repurposed skips as raised beds to cultivate vegetables, herbs, and fruits. The garden hosts workshops on food growing, composting, and ecology, powered by renewable energy.

Name: Skippers Island
Description: Skipper's Island is a 94.3-hectare nature reserve north of Kirby-le-Soken in Essex, England.

Name: Skipwith Common NNR
Description: Skipwith Common NNR is a significant lowland heathland in North Yorkshire, encompassing approximately 274 hectares. It hosts rare flora and fauna, including notable insect and bird species. This National Nature Reserve is a prime example of the Vale of York's diminishing heathland and is actively managed for conservation.

Name: Skokholm
HostOrg: Wildlife Trust of South and West Wales
Description: Skokholm or Skokholm Island is an island 2.5 miles off the coast of Pembrokeshire, Wales, south of the neighbouring island of Skomer.

Name: Skomer
HostOrg: Wildlife Trust of South and West Wales
Description: Skomer or Skomer Island is an island off the coast of Pembrokeshire, in the community of Marloes and St Brides in west Wales.  It is well known for its wildlife: around half the world's population of Manx shearwaters nest on the island, the Atlantic puffin colony is the largest in southern Britain, and the Skomer vole is unique to the island.

Name: Sladden Wood
Description: Sladden Wood is a 7-hectare nature reserve north of Alkham in Kent.  It is managed by the Kent Wildlife Trust.

Name: Slaley Forest

Discover a rich tapestry of flora and fauna, offering a peaceful escape and opportunities for mindful exploration.

Name: Sliabh Beagh
HostOrg: Department of Agriculture, Environment and Rural Affairs (DAERA)
Description: Sliabh Beagh is a trans-border blanket bog in Counties Tyrone and Fermanagh, Northern Ireland. A Special Area of Conservation, it supports diverse bog plant communities, including Hen Harrier. Restoration focuses on hydrological improvements and promoting peat formation.

Name: Slievenacloy Nature Reserve
Description: Slievenacloy Nature Reserve in the Belfast Hills features wet heath, grassland, and blanket bog habitats. It supports diverse wildlife, including breeding waders like snipe and curlew, and various insects. Restoration efforts enhance biodiversity.

HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust

It features wet woodland, a stream, and a small pool, supporting diverse flora and fauna including bluebells in spring, water horsetail, and marsh thistle. The reserve is managed by Sandwell Metropolitan Borough Council and links to Sandwell Valley Country Park.

Name: South Swale

Name: South Walney

Name: Southerham Farm

It is designated as a Local Nature Reserve and a Priority Habitat by Natural England, representing one of the last examples of traditionally managed neutral grassland in the county, featuring a diverse range of plant species and significant ecological value.

It was a spit with a semi-permanent connection to the mainland, but a storm in 2013 made the road down to the end of Spurn impassable to vehicles at high tide.

Name: Stanmore Marsh Wetlands

Name: Staple Hill
Description: This ancient woodland in South East England offers a haven for diverse wildlife, with opportunities to spot deer and a rich array of birds amongst the mature trees. Visitors can explore winding paths perfect for walking and cycling, immersing themselves in the tranquil beauty of the natural landscape. It's a place to reconnect with nature, breathe in the fresh woodland air, and discover the hidden wonders of the forest.

Name: Stapleford Woods
Description: Explore a vibrant expanse of ancient woodland and maturing trees, alive with the sounds of birdsong and the rustle of unseen creatures. Wander winding trails through dappled sunlight, discover hidden streams, and breathe in the fresh, earthy air. This tranquil haven offers opportunities for peaceful walks and invigorating cycles amidst a flourishing natural landscape.

Name: Staunton Harold
Description: Staunton Harold boasts iconic English views across its serene small lakes, formed by a flowing brook in the Leicestershire countryside.

Name: Stave Hill Ecological Park
Description: Stave Hill Ecological Park is a 5.2-acre nature reserve in Rotherhithe, South East London. It features diverse habitats including woodlands, grasslands, and ponds. The park includes a re-created volcanic landscape and is managed by TCV.

Name: Steep Holm Island
Description: Steep Holm Island is a rugged limestone island in the Bristol Channel, west of Weston-super-Mare. A designated SSSI and nature reserve, it hosts seabird colonies, rare plants, and historical remains. The Kenneth Allsop Memorial Trust manages the island to protect its unique wildlife and heritage.

Name: Stenders Quarry SSSI
Description: Stenders Quarry is a 2.8-hectare biological and geological Site of Special Scientific Interest in the Forest of Dean, Gloucestershire, England, notified in 1966 and renotified in 1990.

Name: Stiperstones
Description: The Stiperstones is a distinctive hill in Shropshire, England.  The quartzite rock of the ridge formed some 480 million years ago.

Name: Stiperstones Landscape National Nature Reserve
Description: The Stiperstones Landscape National Nature Reserve is a spectacular landscape of heather-clad moorland and jagged quartzite ridges in south Shropshire. It is home to rare plants like cloudberry and sundew, and birds such as red grouse, skylark, and stonechat. It is a Site of Special Scientific Interest and a National Nature Reserve, known for its unique geology and diverse upland habitats.

Name: Stockbridge Common Marsh
Description: This SSSI along the River Test floodplain boasts diverse wetland habitats including marsh, fen, and meadows, supporting a rich flora of 180 flowering plant species.

Name: Stockbridge Down
Description: This biological SSSI boasts diverse chalk grassland and scrub habitats, supporting a rich array of butterflies and moths.

Name: Stockbury Hill Wood
Description: Stockbury Hill Wood is a 5-hectare nature reserve near Stockbury, north-east of Maidstone in Kent.  It is managed by the Kent Wildlife Trust.

Name: Stocker's Lake
Description: Stocker's Lake is an old flooded gravel pit of approx 90 acres at Rickmansworth, Hertfordshire, England, within the Colne Valley Regional Park which is designated as a Local Nature Reserve.  The lake is owned by Affinity Water and managed by the Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust assisted by the Friends of Stocker's Lake.

Name: Stockhill Wood
Description: This sprawling woodland in South East England offers a haven for diverse wildlife, from elusive deer to a symphony of birdsong amongst ancient trees. Explore winding trails perfect for walking and cycling, immersing yourself in the sights and sounds of a flourishing natural landscape. It's a place to connect with nature and discover the quiet beauty of the forest.

Name: Stocking Springs Wood
Description: Stocking Springs Wood is a 1.1-hectare nature reserve between Ayot St Lawrence and Ayot St Peter in Welwyn Hatfield district in Hertfordshire.

Name: Stodmarsh National Nature Reserve
Description: Stodmarsh National Nature Reserve, located in the Stour Valley near Canterbury, Kent, is a unique wetland environment covering approximately 241-250 hectares. It is internationally recognized as a Ramsar site, Special Protection Area (SPA), and Special Area of Conservation (SAC) due to its extensive reedbeds (the largest in the South East of England), open water, wet grassland, alder woodland, and carr. The reserve supports diverse birdlife, including breeding marsh harriers, bearded tits, and wintering bitterns, as well as a variety of invertebrates, rare plants, and a strong population of water voles.

Name: Stoke Common
Description: Stoke Common is a 100-hectare Site of Special Scientific Interest and Special Area of Conservation in Buckinghamshire. It protects rare lowland heathland, part of the Chiltern commons, with diverse habitats. The City of London Corporation manages this biodiversity site.

Name: Stoke Common Meadows
Description: Stoke Common Meadows is a biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in north Wiltshire, England.  The 10.

Name: Stoke Park Wood
Description: This ancient woodland, managed by Forestry England, offers a haven for diverse wildlife amidst a tapestry of mature trees. Explore winding paths perfect for walking and cycling, immersing yourself in the tranquil beauty and spotting the creatures that call this vibrant ecosystem home. It's a place to connect with nature and discover the quiet wonders of the South East.

Name: Stoke Wood
Description: Stoke Wood is an ancient woodland in Oxfordshire, near the village of Stoke Lyne. It offers gentle walking trails and is home to diverse wildlife including muntjac deer and birds. Historically part of Bernwood Forest, it features mature oak and beech trees.

Name: Stoke Woods
Description: This expansive woodland in the South West of England offers a haven for diverse wildlife, from ancient trees teeming with birdsong to the rustle of smaller creatures in the undergrowth. Visitors can explore miles of trails, perfect for invigorating walks or cycling adventures, immersing themselves in the tranquil beauty and rich natural tapestry. It's a place to connect with nature, breathe in the fresh air, and discover the wonders of a thriving woodland ecosystem.

Name: Stone Wood
Description: Stone Wood is a nature reserve south-west of Shadoxhurst in Kent.  It is managed by Kent Wildlife Trust.

Name: Stoneacre, Kent
Description: Stoneacre offers serene meadows, a traditional orchard, and a charming garden, showcasing Kent's natural rural beauty.

Name: Stonefolds
Description: Stonefolds is a nature recovery site near Hadrian's Wall in Northumberland National Park. It focuses on restoring peatlands, woodlands, and floodplains. The site contributes to broader nature recovery efforts within the park, aiming to meet national net zero targets.

Name: Stonehenge Landscape
Description: A vast landscape of chalk grassland around Stonehenge undergoing reversion projects to restore this precious habitat for wildlife.

Name: Stonesby Quarry
Description: Stonesby Quarry is a 3.2 hectares biological Site of Special Scientific Interest between Stonesby and Waltham on the Wolds in Leicestershire.

Name: Stoneywell
Description: Stoneywell offers charming gardens and tranquil woodlands, nestled within the scenic Charnwood Forest.

Name: Stort Navigation
Description: The Stort Navigation is the canalised section of the River Stort running 22 kilometres from the town of Bishop's Stortford, Hertfordshire, downstream to its confluence with the Lee Navigation at Feildes Weir near Rye House, Hoddesdon, Hertfordshire.

Name: Storton's Pits
Description: Storton’s Pits is a former gravel extraction site, now a nature reserve located in Northampton. It features lakes, reedbeds, and grassland, supporting diverse waterfowl, invertebrates, and rare plants. The site is managed for wildlife conservation.

Name: Stour Estuary
Description: Stour Estuary is a 2,523 hectare biological and geological Site of Special Scientific Interest which stretches from Manningtree to Harwich in Essex and Suffolk.  It is also an internationally important wetland Ramsar site, a Special Protection Area and a Nature Conservation Review site.

Name: Stourhead
Description: Stourhead's expansive estate, at the River Stour's source, features celebrated landscape gardens, farmland, and extensive woodlands.

Name: Stover Canal
Description: Stover Canal is a historic transport waterway bordered by wet woodland, fen, and unimproved grassland. The reserve supports diverse wetland plants, invertebrates, and breeding birds, offering a tranquil environment for wildlife. It is part of a wider nature reserve managed for biodiversity and conservation.

Name: Stow Maries Halt
Description: Stow Maries Halt is a 2.2-hectare nature reserve south of Stow Maries in Essex.

Name: Stowe Gardens
Description: Stowe Gardens features extensive parkland and lakes, an iconic and influential example of the natural English landscape style.

Name: Stratford-upon-Avon Local Nature Reserve
HostOrg: Stratford Town Trust and Stratford-on-Avon District Council
Description: Stratford-upon-Avon Local Nature Reserve is a 71-acre site in Stratford-upon-Avon, designated in 2023. It is part of The Stratford Riverside Project, creating a green corridor between Fisherman's Car Park and Lucy's Mill Bridge. The reserve features diverse habitats including riverbanks, meadow grassland, reedbeds, and wetlands, offering opportunities to view wildlife such as deer, kingfishers, and otters. It is managed in partnership by Stratford-on-Avon District Council and Stratford Town Trust.

Name: Strawberry Banks
Description: Strawberry Banks is a 5. 06-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Gloucestershire, notified in 1993.

Name: Street Heath
Description: Street Heath is a 12.5 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest 4 km west of Glastonbury in Somerset, notified in 1966.

Name: Stringer's Common
Description: Stringer's Common is a 30-hectare nature reserve east of Worplesdon in Surrey.  It is owned by Surrey County Council and managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Strome Castle
Description: Perched on a dramatic headland between two sea lochs, this Highland ruin offers breathtaking coastal views and a wild Scottish landscape.

Name: Studland Beach
Description: Studland features famous sandy beaches and a vital nature reserve, supporting diverse coastal wildlife along the edge of Poole Harbour.

Name: Studley Royal Park
Description: Its 800 acres feature magnificent designed parkland and stunning landscaped gardens.

Name: Sudbury Hall
Description: Sudbury Hall boasts Grade II listed gardens, offering a significant and beautiful landscape for exploration.

Name: Sumburgh Head
HostOrg: The Royal Society for the Protection of Birds
Description: Sumburgh Head is a nature reserve and lighthouse at the southern tip of mainland Shetland. It is a key breeding site for seabirds including puffins, guillemots, razorbills, and kittiwakes. The site offers panoramic views and an accessible visitor centre.

Name: Sunnycroft
Description: Sunnycroft's suburban garden provides a valuable wildlife haven with mature trees and a small orchard, offering essential green space.

Name: Sutcliffe Park
Description: Sutcliffe Park, located in Greenwich, is a significant greenspace incorporating a re-naturalised section of the River Quaggy. It forms a key part of flood alleviation and biodiversity enhancement projects, encouraging natural habitats and was designated a Local Nature Reserve in 2006.

Name: Sutton and Hollesley Commons
Description: Sutton and Hollesley Heaths is a 483.3-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south-east of Woodbridge in Suffolk.

Name: Sutton Fen
Description: Sutton Fen, an RSPB reserve in the Norfolk Broads, is a secluded and largely inaccessible wilderness protecting diverse fenland habitats. It is nationally recognised for its special wildlife, supporting rare plants like the Fen Orchid, insects such as the Swallowtail butterfly, and birds like Bitterns, Marsh Harriers, and Cranes. It is one of the most important UK sites for water beetles and wetland plants, and visitors can observe its unique biodiversity and ongoing conservation efforts, often through guided events due to its restricted access.

Name: Sutton Manor
Description: Discover a haven of ancient woodland and diverse wildlife, perfect for exploring on foot or by bike. Wander through towering trees, listening to birdsong and searching for fleeting glimpses of woodland creatures. This tranquil natural setting offers a refreshing escape and a chance to reconnect with the beauty of the British countryside.

Name: Sutton's Fen
Description: Sutton's Fen is a relic of ancient fenland and marsh pasture. Fed by spring water, it supports diverse sedges, rushes, and grasses, attracting dragonflies, damselflies, and butterflies. Over 100 plant species thrive, including greater tussock-sedge and southern marsh-orchid. Roe deer and water voles inhabit the reserve.

Name: Swanwick Lakes
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Swanwick Lakes is a 35-hectare nature reserve in Swanwick in Hampshire.  It is managed by the Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust.

Name: Swarland Wood
Description: This extensive woodland in Northumberland offers a haven for diverse wildlife, from woodland birds flitting through ancient trees to deer grazing in peaceful glades. Visitors can explore winding trails, perfect for invigorating walks or bike rides, immersing themselves in the sights and sounds of a thriving natural landscape. It's a place to reconnect with nature, breathe in fresh air, and discover the beauty of the Northumbrian countryside.

Name: Swell Wood
Description: Swell Wood is an ancient woodland and Coronation Meadow in Somerset. It hosts a significant heronry, numerous bat species, and many ancient trees. The reserve is managed for biodiversity and accessible via public footpaths.

Name: Swettenham Meadows Nature Reserve
Description: Swettenham Meadows is a nature reserve in Cheshire, England, on the north bank of Swettenham Brook, a short distance north east of Swettenham village and 2.5 miles east of Holmes Chapel village.

Name: Swift's Hill SSSI
Description: Swift's Hill is a 9.15-hectare biological and geological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Gloucestershire, notified in 1966 and renotified in 1984.

Name: Swineshead & Spanoak Woods
Description: Ancient woodland and former parkland trees on clay soil near Swineshead. This site features a rich mix of ash, oak, and field maple, supporting diverse flora and fauna. Maintained by the Woodland Trust for public access and wildlife.

Name: Swithland Wood
Description: Swithland Wood is a designated Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and a recently designated National Nature Reserve (NNR) in Leicestershire, East Midlands. This ancient woodland features historic slate quarries and diverse ecosystems. Owned and managed by Bradgate Park Trust, it offers significant habitats for wildlife and is popular for walks.

Name: Sydenham Hill Wood and Cox's Walk
Description: Sydenham Hill Wood is a ten-hectare wood on the northern slopes of the Norwood Ridge in the London Borough of Southwark.  It is designated as a Local Nature Reserve and Site of Metropolitan Importance for Nature Conservation.

Name: Syderstone Common
Description: Syderstone Common is a 43.7-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest west of Fakenham in Norfolk, England.

Name: Sydlings Copse
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 22 hectares.

Name: Sylvia's Meadow
Description: Sylvia's Meadow is a nature reserve and a Site of Special Scientific Interest owned and managed by Cornwall Wildlife Trust.  It is a herb rich, 5-hectare site situated near Gunnislake, in East Cornwall, England.

Name: Symonds Yat Rock
Description: This stunning natural viewpoint in the Wye Valley offers breathtaking panoramic views across ancient woodlands and the winding River Wye. Explore miles of trails winding through the trees, perfect for invigorating walks and cycling adventures, where you might spot soaring birds of prey or discover hidden woodland creatures. It's a place to immerse yourself in the raw beauty of the landscape and connect with nature.

Name: Sywell Country Park
Description: Sywell Country Park is a Green Flag Award winning site in Northamptonshire. Built around a former Victorian reservoir, it provides habitat for diverse wildlife, including overwintering wildfowl. The park offers walking trails, bird hides, a play area, and a cafe for visitors.

Name: Talybont Reservoir
Description: Talybont Reservoir, located in the Brecon Beacons National Park, is a significant water body within the Usk catchment. Designated as a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and a local nature reserve, it is central to conservation efforts and supports various wildlife habitats, particularly important for wintering wildfowl and passage migrants. Welsh Wildlife Trust collaborates with Dŵr Cymru Welsh Water on catchment partnership initiatives here, focusing on nature-based solutions and biodiversity enhancement.

Name: Tame Valley Canal
Description: The Tame Valley Canal is an 8.5-mile green corridor in Birmingham, connecting to the national canal network. It traverses industrial landscapes, offering walking and cycling routes, and is a significant wildlife haven within an urban setting.

Name: Tandle Hill Country Park
Description: Tandle Hill Country Park in Oldham covers 110 acres of woodland and grassland, offering panoramic views across the Manchester Plain and Pennine Hills. The park features a children's play area, cafe, and picnic spots.

Name: Tardebigge Reservoir
Description: Tardebigge Reservoir is a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) in Worcestershire, England. It serves as a feeder reservoir for the Worcester and Birmingham Canal, supporting diverse wetland habitats and birdlife. The area offers opportunities for walking and wildlife observation.

Name: Tarn Hows
Description: This picturesque tarn, fed by valley and basin mires, drains via Tom Gill which cascades over several small waterfalls.

Name: Tarr Steps
Description: Tarr Steps features an ancient clapper bridge crossing the River Barle, set within Exmoor's Tarr Steps Woodland National Nature Reserve. The reserve is owned and managed by the Exmoor National Park Authority, offering diverse wildlife habitats and scenic riverside walks.

Name: Tattershall Castle (Lincolnshire)
Description: Tattershall Castle's moated grounds provide wetland habitats for diverse wildlife and wildfowl.

Name: Tatton Park
Description: Tatton Park features a vast 2,000-acre deer park, home to red and fallow deer, alongside extensive gardens and diverse landscapes.

Name: Teal Lough NNR
Description: Teal Lough NNR is a lowland raised bog in County Londonderry/Tyrone, Northern Ireland, within the Teal Lough Special Area of Conservation (SAC) and Teal Lough and Slaghtfreeden Bogs Area of Special Scientific Interest (ASSI). It is valued for its unique biodiversity and significant peatland features, representing a crucial conservation area for this rare habitat, and is part of the wider Sperrins Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty (AONB).

Name: Tees-Swale: Naturally Connected
Description: Tees-Swale: Naturally Connected is a landscape initiative in the North Pennines AONB. It focuses on restoring and connecting habitats, including peatlands and river systems across the Tees and Swale catchments, enhancing biodiversity and water quality.

Name: Telegraph Hill, Hertfordshire
Description: Telegraph Hill is a nature reserve near Lilley in north Hertfordshire.  It is in the Chilterns Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty.

Name: Tentsmuir Point NNR
Description: Tentsmuir Point NNR, on the North East Fife coast, features sand dunes, woodlands, and intertidal habitats. This dynamic landscape is home to seals, migratory birds, and diverse plant life. Visitors can enjoy walks and observe wildlife.

Name: Terrace Meadows SNCI
Description: Terrace Meadows SNCI, a traditional hay meadow in Sherborne, is managed to protect and enhance its rich biodiversity. This Site of Nature Conservation Interest provides important habitat for wildflowers, grasses, and invertebrates. It offers public open space for local residents.

Name: Testwood Lakes
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Testwood Lakes is a 55-hectare nature reserve in Totton to the northwest of Southampton in Hampshire, England.  It is managed by the Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust.

Name: Tewin Orchard and Hopkyns Wood
Description: Tewin Orchard and Hopkyns Wood is a 4.3-hectare nature reserve in Tewin in Hertfordshire.

Name: Tewinbury
Description: Tewinbury is a 7.5-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest near Tewin in Hertfordshire.

Name: Thames Barrier Park
Description: Thames Barrier Park in East London offers landscaped gardens, a rose garden, and wildflower areas providing important urban habitats. It features fountains, a children's play area, and views of the iconic Thames Barrier.

Name: Thames Chase Community Forest
Description: Thames Chase Community Forest spans east London and south Essex. This community forest features woodlands, parks, and open spaces, offering a range of recreational activities. The forest centre provides information, a shop, and a café.

Name: Thames Chase Forest Centre
Description: This expansive woodland in South East England offers a haven for diverse wildlife, where ancient trees stand sentinel over winding paths. Visitors can explore a rich tapestry of nature through walking and cycling trails, immersing themselves in the sights and sounds of a thriving natural environment. It's a place to connect with the outdoors and discover the beauty of a flourishing forest ecosystem.

Name: Thames Road Wetland
Description: Thames Road Wetland is a constructed wetland in Crayford, Bexley, filtering surface water before it enters the River Cray. Managed by Thames21, it improves water quality and provides vital habitat for local wildlife. The site helps mitigate pollution impacts on the river system.

Name: Thatcham Reed Beds
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Thatcham Reed Beds is a 67.4-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest east of Newbury in Berkshire.

Name: The Carbon Landscape
Description: Risley Moss Nature Reserve is a significant lowland raised bog and wetland site in Warrington, managed by Warrington Borough Council. It is a Local Nature Reserve, Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI), and Special Area of Conservation (SAC), forming a key part of The Carbon Landscape partnership programme. The reserve is vital for biodiversity, carbon capture, and connecting communities with nature in a historically industrial landscape.

Name: The Carrifran Wildwood
Description: The Carrifran Wildwood is a rewilding project in the Southern Uplands of Scotland, managed by Borders Forest Trust. Since 2000, over 600,000 native trees have been planted, restoring woodland and associated habitats. The site focuses on ecological restoration and biodiversity.

Name: The Coombes, Hinton Parva
Description: The Coombes protects a steep-sided dry valley with rich chalk grassland, supporting a variety of grasses and important butterfly populations.

Name: The Courts Garden
Description: A tranquil English country garden, showcasing diverse plant collections, mature trees, and peaceful water features.

Name: The Crumbles
Description: The Crumbles, near Eastbourne, is a unique shingle beach and vegetated ridge formed by coastal processes. Located in East Sussex, it supports a distinctive range of coastal plants and invertebrates, part of the Eastbourne Coastal Local Nature Reserve.

Name: The Cyril Hart Arboretum
Description: Discover a vibrant tapestry of ancient trees and diverse habitats within this beautiful Forestry England woodland. Wander winding paths through a haven for wildlife, keeping an eye out for woodland birds and shy mammals. It's an ideal spot for invigorating walks, peaceful cycling, and immersing yourself in the sights and sounds of the natural world.

Name: The Ercall
Description: The Ercall is a small hill in Shropshire, England, between The Wrekin and Wellington.  It is an internationally important geological site, part of The Wrekin and The Ercall Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: The Flit
Description: The Flits is a National Nature Reserve in Herefordshire, an area of low-lying grassland, fen, scrub, and woodland on peaty soils within the floodplain of the River Wye. It is notable for its diverse invertebrate community, including many rare flies, spiders, and beetles, as well as numerous butterfly and moth species. While public access is permitted for quiet enjoyment, there are no waymarked trails.

Name: The Forest and the Highlands
Description: The Forest and the Highlands is a 29.74-hectare nature reserve north of East Horsley in Surrey.

Name: The Forest of Dean
Description: This ancient woodland offers a haven for diverse wildlife, with ancient oaks and beeches creating a majestic canopy. Explore winding trails perfect for walking and cycling, immersing yourself in the sights and sounds of a thriving natural environment. Discover hidden streams and glades, a true escape into the heart of nature.

Name: The Gill
Description: The Gill is a 12-hectare nature reserve north of Goudhurst in Kent, England.  It is managed by the Kent Wildlife Trust.

Name: The Great Canal Orchard
Description: The Great Canal Orchard in Wolverhampton is a community green space managed by the Canal & River Trust. It features various fruit trees, providing fresh produce for local communities and hosting events. The site is situated along the canal network.

Name: The Great North Bog
Description: The Great North Bog protects 92% of England's upland peat, spanning 7000 sq km across Northern England. This initiative restores degraded peatlands, vital for carbon storage, biodiversity, and water quality.

Name: The Green Park
Description: The Green Park covers 40 acres of mature grassland and trees in central London. Located between Buckingham Palace and Piccadilly, it provides a tranquil, open space popular for relaxation. Part of the Royal Parks, it is a significant green lung for the city.

Name: The Growing Space
Description: The Growing Space is a community garden in Wincanton, Somerset, offering a welcoming environment for local people. It provides opportunities to learn gardening skills, connect with nature, and improve wellbeing. Produce is utilised by the Balsam Centre cafe and distributed within the local community.

Name: The Hermitage (Scotland)
Description: Ancient woodlands along the River Braan feature towering Douglas-fir trees, creating a majestic forest landscape.

Name: The Hudnalls
Description: The Hudnalls is an ancient woodland reserve within the Wye Valley Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, Gloucestershire, representing a vital fragment of the Atlantic rainforest. It is globally significant for its rich lichen, moss, and fern communities, supporting diverse woodland birds and wildlife. The site's varied terrain slopes towards the River Wye.

Name: The Larches
Description: The Larches is a 25-hectare nature reserve north of Detling, which is north of Maidstone in Kent.  It is managed by Kent Wildlife Trust.

Name: The Loons and Loch of Banks
Description: The Loons and Loch of Banks is a significant wetland on the Orkney mainland. It features wet grassland, reedbeds, and open water, providing habitat for breeding waders and wintering ducks and geese. It is the largest remaining wetland of its type in Orkney.

Name: The Mens
Description: The Mens is a 205.2-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest west of Billingshurst in West Sussex.

Name: The Mere, Ellesmere
HostOrg: Shropshire Council / The Mere Charitable Trust
Description: The Mere at Ellesmere is a glacial lake in Shropshire, forming part of the Shropshire Meres and Mosses Ramsar site. It comprises open water, reedbeds, and woodland habitats, supporting diverse wildlife. The site is popular for walks and wildlife observation.

Name: The Naze
Description: The Naze Nature Reserve is a 45 hectare nature reserve on The Naze peninsula north of Walton-on-the-Naze in Essex.  It is managed by the Essex Wildlife Trust,.

Name: The Needles
Description: Dramatic chalk stacks rise from the sea, part of a Marine Conservation Zone and Site of Special Scientific Interest protecting its unique coastal landscape, shore, and heath.

Name: The Needles Batteries
Description: Dramatic clifftop landscapes overlooking the iconic Needles chalk stacks provide vital nesting sites for seabirds and unique coastal flora.

Name: The Park, University of Gloucestershire
Description: The Park, University of Gloucestershire is a 9.5-hectare community green space in Cheltenham, Gloucestershire.

Name: The Pennings
Description: The Pennings is a wet grassland site bordering the River Dove in Suffolk. Historically managed as hay meadow, it features reedbed, fen, and wet woodland. The site supports rich plant and invertebrate life.

Name: The Regent's Park Wildlife Garden & West Pond
